title: Fix solver 11 default profile regression versus solver 10
description: Current solver 11 default enables SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_SEARCH_MODE=focused-stable SAT_MODE_USE_TICKS=on, but the clean 2026-05-24 profiling comparison shows this default regresses badly versus solver 10: solver10 default solved 10/10 with PAR-2 699.671 at log/phase1/solver10-default-300-vs-solver11-clean, while solver11 default solved 9/10 with PAR-2 1201.538 at log/phase1/5b2.2.52-s11-default-clean. Single-mode solver11 with new search features disabled solved 10/10 with PAR-2 798.196, so the global focused/stable default is the wrong default candidate. Fix by restoring a solver10-parity or single-mode default until focused/stable clears the solver10 baseline on the full profiling/discriminating gates, and document the keep/tune/revert decision for the rejected focused/stable default.
acceptance_criteria: Default solver11 profile no longer regresses solver10 on the profiling suite by current PAR-2 promotion rules. Required evidence: cargo test, smoke, invariant smoke, clean 300s/16GiB benchmarks/profiling comparison against solver10, compare_bench output, and README/FEATURES/CONFIG_SCHEMA updates showing focused/stable is opt-in or promoted only after beating solver10. No untracked default-profile change without a rollback note.
notes:
s11-02 progress 2026-05-24: Implemented default/fast rollback from focused-stable/ticks/LBD to solver10-compatible single/no-LBD search while keeping preprocessing enabled. Checks so far: config tests pass, cargo test 321 passed, clippy passed, smoke 9/9 passed, invariant smoke 9/9 passed, changed-file rustfmt check passed. Profile bench after rollback: log/phase1/5b2.2.53-after-default-rollback, 300s/16GiB, SAT_STATS_JSON=on SAT_LIMIT_WALL_SEC=295, solved 10/10, PAR-2 785.980. This is a significant improvement vs old solver11 default log/phase1/5b2.2.52-s11-default-clean PAR-2 1201.538 and fixes mp1 UNKNOWN -> SAT, but still regresses solver10 clean baseline log/phase1/solver10-default-300-vs-solver11-clean by +86.309 PAR-2. Leaving bead open and moving into SAT-playground-5b2.2.56 parity gap.
Status changed to blocked 2026-05-27: parked behind in-progress dependency SAT-playground-5b2.2.56 (now back to open). Will resume once parity gap closes.
Re-pointed dependency (slate-heron triage, post analyzesat-2026-05-28-perf-tax): was blocked on 5b2.2.56 (single-mode parity), now blocked on 5b2.2.46 (focused/stable feature re-eval). Rationale: single-mode parity with solver10 is MEASURED unachievable (~6-7% diffuse propagate/backtrack ALU, no fixable hotspot; 5b2.2.56 accepted/closed). So the default decision is no longer 'match solver10 single-mode' but: ship the single-mode default (~7% slower than solver10, the best non-feature default) UNLESS the focused/stable feature default beats solver10 once its 74% throughput penalty is removed (the 5b2.2.46 path, gated on new perf-decompose bead SAT-playground-d8p).
Re-pointed again (d8p, 2026-05-28): was blocked on 5b2.2.46 (throughput-subset re-run); now blocked on SAT-playground-588 (focused/stable trajectory search-policy fix). Reason: d8p measured that the focused/stable regression is search-trajectory (deep dive / high LBD), NOT the per-event throughput overheads 5b2.2.46 assumed. The feature default is gated on the search-policy fix (SAT-playground-588), a Phase-2/inprocessing-class effort. Near-term default decision: ship single-mode (~7% slower than solver10, accepted in 5b2.2.56) until SAT-playground-588 lands. Evidence: log/d8p-focused-stable-perf/FINDINGS.md.
ibq validation (2026-05-29): focused/stable loses to single-mode default on the profiling suite regardless of restart cadence (focused/stable orig 991.8, KF 1326.8, both >> single-mode default 750.3, 10/10). So the focused FEATURE default is NOT viable via Phase-1 restart/deep-dive fixes. RECOMMENDATION: ship the single-mode default near-term (best non-feature default, ~7% slower than solver10, accepted in 5b2.2.56); the competitive feature default is Phase-2-dependent (inprocessing/vivification, 5b2.3.18) to fix clause quality. ibq (VMTF deep-dive) restart approach rejected; reopened for a surgical fix only if Phase 2 makes focused/stable otherwise competitive.
Cleanup 2026-05-29 (VioletRidge, approved): status clarification. The near-term action (roll the default back to single-mode) is DONE — current default is single-mode (~750-786 PAR-2, 10/10), accepting the ~7% inherent infrastructure tax vs solver10 (5b2.2.56, closed). 'Beating solver10' is now a Phase-2 objective: the only viable lever is clause-quality/inprocessing (5b2.3.18), via the focused/stable feature default (ibq, now blocked on 5b2.3.18). All Phase-1 default-path levers are exhausted/disproven: throughput parity (5b2.2.56 + 1.14 subtree closed), lbd-tiered (4a3, deferred), single-mode trajectory changes 1oo/0s0 (rejected, mp1 fragility), focused restart fixes (ibq, rejected). This P0 correctly stays blocked behind Phase-2.
close_reason: Consolidation 2026-06-13: closed as resolved-by-events with promotion evidence. The bead premised that the solver-11 default regressed vs solver 10 and search-feature work was frozen until fixed; the 2026-05-30/31 fstab_lbdtier promotion shipped a default (config.rs:830-847) that won aggregate PAR-2 2x over the prior single-mode default (5653 vs 6808 on profile20, 13/20 vs 10/20 solved) and CLEARED the solver-10 lexicographic floor (6773) - see the promotion citation embedded in config.rs:831-837 and the FINDINGS trail. title: Invalid SAT model on Kakuro advanced-search profile
description: Background: The 2026-05-21 all-settings 300s retest found a reproducible invalid SAT model on profiling instance 5e933a625099cc1ec6a8299a7848a2ae-Kakuro-easy-112-ext.xml.hg_7. The instance path is benchmarks/profiling/minisat-simp-five/5e933a625099cc1ec6a8299a7848a2ae-Kakuro-easy-112-ext.xml.hg_7.cnf.xz. Default profile log/1.12a/profile-after-300-reopen and SAT_PHASE=saved log/1.12a/profile-300-phase-saved both solved the profiling suite without model failures, but every advanced setting tested printed s SATISFIABLE for this instance and failed the internal model checker. Affected artifacts: log/1.12a/profile-300-focused-vmtf/errors.log, log/1.12a/profile-300-stable-rephase-off/errors.log, log/1.12a/profile-300-stable-rephase-on/errors.log. Failure signature: SAT result requires model_check_result=pass, got fail; stdout s-line: s SATISFIABLE; internal model check failed. Settings that reproduced it: Focused/VMTF with SAT_PROFILE=experimental SAT_PROOF=drat SAT_SEED=0 SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_LBD_UPDATE_REASONS=on SAT_RESTART=kissat-ema SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved SAT_BINARY_FAST=on SAT_SEARCH_MODE=focused-stable SAT_CLAUSE_MIN=basic SAT_VMTF=on SAT_REPHASE=off SAT_CHRONO=off; Stable-SAT rephase off with SAT_PHASE=best-then-target-then-saved SAT_CLAUSE_MIN=recursive-limited SAT_REPHASE=off and otherwise same advanced flags; Stable-SAT rephase on with SAT_PHASE=best-then-target-then-saved SAT_CLAUSE_MIN=recursive-limited SAT_REPHASE=on and otherwise same advanced flags. Observed times: Focused/VMTF ERROR at 47.321s, Stable-SAT rephase off ERROR at 46.886s, Stable-SAT rephase on ERROR at 47.183s. Goal: isolate the earliest responsible advanced feature interaction for this Kakuro invalid-model failure and provide a small, repeatable regression guard. Why it blocks progress: SAT model soundness is a solver contract, so no further Phase 1/Phase 2 tuning or promotion should proceed until this instance no longer returns an invalid SAT assignment under the advanced configs.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce the Kakuro failure with at least one failing advanced config and record the exact command plus log path. Minimize the config matrix to identify whether the failure requires focused/stable mode, VMTF, SAT_BINARY_FAST, clause minimization, target/best phase, rephase, or a specific combination. Add a focused regression test or a benchmark guard command that fails before the fix and passes after it. Fix the root cause so the named instance either returns a SAT model that satisfies the original CNF or correctly returns another valid solver status; do not mask invalid SAT as UNKNOWN. Rerun the three failing advanced configs on this instance, default smoke, invariant smoke, cargo test, and a profile spot check. Acceptance requires no model-check failure on this instance, no default-profile status regression, and documentation of root cause in log/1.12a or the follow-up summary.
notes: Same root cause as SAT-playground-5b2.2.21 fixed Kakuro too. The binary-fast inline-abstraction migration failed to remap binary_clauses[*].clause_ref and binary_id_by_clause, so later GC could mark live binary clauses deleted and skip required binary implications. After adding remap_binary_clause_refs during inline abstraction migration, all three original Kakuro advanced failure configs were rerun at 120s and now return verified SAT instead of invalid SAT: focused/VMTF log/1.12a/fix-kakuro-focused-vmtf-120 result SAT ok 59.220s; stable rephase-off log/1.12a/fix-kakuro-stable-rephase-off-120 result SAT ok 61.993s; stable rephase-on log/1.12a/fix-kakuro-stable-rephase-on-120 result SAT ok 66.586s. Full validation also passed cargo fmt --check, cargo test -- --nocapture (240 passed), cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, default smoke 9/9, invariant smoke 9/9, and default 300s profile 11/11 solved with no correctness failures at log/1.12a/profile-after-binary-remap-fix-300.
close_reason: Same binary-fast remap fix eliminates Kakuro invalid SAT model; all three original advanced configs now return verified SAT; full tests and default profile pass.

Initial plan: reproduce one failing advanced config, minimize the required flag combination, inspect the implicated search/propagation/model code, add or document a regression guard, fix root cause rather than masking invalid SAT, then rerun the REGRandom advanced configs plus Kakuro cross-check, smoke/invariant/cargo tests, and profile bench.
Reproduced and minimized failure. The retained direct run showed the model violated original binary clause (-13 -73). A later GC could then mark live binary clauses deleted, removing required binary implications. Fix: call remap_binary_clause_refs during inline abstraction migration. The remap uses the same relocation table and helper as full GC, before replacing self.arena, so binary IDs remain stable while clause refs and binary_id_by_clause point at the migrated arena. Reviewed edge cases: deleted binaries remain deleted; binary reasons remain stable BinaryClauseId values and do not need reason rewrites; default profile is unaffected because SAT_BINARY_FAST defaults off; the regression test covers migration followed by GC and propagation of the preserved binary implication. Final validation: cargo fmt --check pass; cargo test -- --nocapture 240 passed; cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings pass; default smoke 9/9; invariant smoke 9/9; default 300s profile log/1.12a/profile-after-binary-remap-fix-300 solved 11/11, PAR-2 631.032, no errors. compare_bench against log/1.12a/profile-after-300-reopen: verdict PASS, no status regressions, delta +6.224 PAR-2. compare_bench against log/profile-default-300-solver11-2026-05-21: verdict PASS, no status regressions, delta +3.453 PAR-2.
close_reason: Fixed binary-fast inline-abstraction remap bug; REGRandom invalid SAT model no longer reproduces under minimized or original advanced configs; full tests and default profile pass.

title: Fix advanced search SAT model-check failures
description: Background: 300s profile retesting for 1.12a showed that the default profile and SAT_PHASE=saved solve all 11 profiling instances correctly, but every advanced search setting tested can print s SATISFIABLE with an invalid model. Affected settings include Focused/VMTF, Stable-SAT rephase off, and Stable-SAT rephase on. The failures are reproducible in log/1.12a/profile-300-focused-vmtf/errors.log, log/1.12a/profile-300-stable-rephase-off/errors.log, and log/1.12a/profile-300-stable-rephase-on/errors.log. The failing instances are 46355da785714f239393e7630020cae3-REGRandom-K4-L1-Seed40.sanitized and 5e933a625099cc1ec6a8299a7848a2ae-Kakuro-easy-112-ext.xml.hg_7. Goal: isolate which advanced component or interaction corrupts the final SAT assignment under these modes and fix it without regressing default or saved-phase behavior. Reasoning: performance tuning is irrelevant until SAT model validity is restored; the solver contract requires SAT models to satisfy the original CNF. Constraints: keep advanced features opt-in while debugging; preserve SAT Competition stdout/run.sh behavior; do not mask the issue by treating invalid SAT as UNKNOWN; keep proof behavior intact for UNSAT; record exact env configs and compare artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce both invalid-model failures with at least one advanced profile config and capture the failing command/log paths. Add a focused regression test or small reproducible benchmark guard when practical. Identify whether the root cause is focused/stable mode, VMTF, recursive clause minimization, binary-fast reason handling, target/best phase interaction, rephase, or a combination. Implement the fix and rerun cargo test, default smoke, invariant smoke, the failing advanced configs on the two named instances, and the relevant 300s profile/search-core spot checks. Acceptance requires no model-check failures for the advanced configs that previously failed, no default-profile status regression, and updated summary notes explaining the root cause and remaining performance status.
notes:
Discovered during 2026-05-21 all-settings retest for SAT-playground-5b2.2.16. This bead is a correctness blocker for promoting or further tuning the advanced search stack; it does not require promoting the advanced modes after correctness is fixed.
Blocking policy added 2026-05-21: this bug is now a P0 progress blocker. Do not start Phase 1 throughput/chrono work, Phase 1 promotion, Phase 2 inprocessing, or advanced-search milestone closure until the invalid SAT model failures are resolved or deliberately superseded with explicit user approval. The issue is not a performance miss: the advanced modes printed s SATISFIABLE while tools/bench.sh rejected the returned assignment against the original CNF. Default profile and SAT_PHASE=saved passed the same 300s profiling suite without model failures, so the failure appears tied to the composed advanced stack rather than the base solver/harness.
Resolved by the binary-fast inline-abstraction metadata remap fix from SAT-playground-5b2.2.21/SAT-playground-5b2.2.22. Root cause: SAT_BINARY_FAST metadata was not remapped when ensure_original_clause_abstractions rebuilt the arena for large formulas, so later GC could mark live binary clauses deleted and propagation missed original binary implications. Evidence: REGRandom minimized SAT_BINARY_FAST=on reproducer now UNSAT ok in 28.710s; all three REGRandom original advanced configs are clean 120s timeouts with no model error; all three Kakuro original advanced configs now return verified SAT in 59.220s, 61.993s, and 66.586s. Full validation passed fmt, cargo test 240, clippy, default smoke, invariant smoke, and default 300s profile 11/11 solved PAR-2 631.032 with compare_bench PASS/no status regressions against prior 300s runs. Remaining advanced-search performance regressions are promotion/tuning issues, not this correctness blocker.
close_reason: Resolved binary-fast metadata remap soundness bug; both concrete invalid-model blockers are closed and all previously failing advanced configs on REGRandom/Kakuro no longer produce model-check failures.

title: BVE DRAT proof-ordering regression: source-clause deletions emitted before resolvents → invalid UNSAT proofs
description:
Found during a competition 'medium' benchmark run of solver/11-kissat-port (2026-06-20, 32/100 instances completed before stop). Two UNSAT instances of the oski15a family (oski15a01b20s_opt, oski15a01b40s_opt) produced DRAT proofs that drat-trim REJECTS with 's NOT VERIFIED' / 'RAT check failed on all possible pivots ... (modulo deletion errors)' after a full ~166-211s verification (not a checker timeout).

ROOT CAUSE: commit 15383f6 ('Fix BVE eliminated-clause removal ordering', 2026-06-20) moved the eliminated source clauses' removal from live occurrence/watch structures to BEFORE resolvent insertion (a correct solver-internal fix), but also moved the proof emission proof_log.record_deletion(...) along with it. In DRAT, each BVE resolvent is a RAT clause on the eliminated variable, so the checker needs the source clauses still present when the resolvent is added. Emitting the deletions first strips the RAT support -> rejection. Pre-15383f6 order was: insert resolvents (proof adds) THEN record_deletion; the buggy order is record_deletion THEN resolvents.

WHY IT SLIPPED THROUGH: smoke_test small UNSAT instances pass drat-trim even with the wrong ordering (the prematurely-deleted clause is not needed by a later RAT check at small scale), and profile20 does not include oski15a. Only large BMC instances expose it.

FIX (implemented in working tree, not yet committed): in simp.rs eliminate_variable, snapshot the source-clause literals (guarded by new ProofLog::is_enabled()) BEFORE structure removal, keep structure removal before resolvent insertion, and emit record_deletion from the snapshots AFTER the resolvent loop. Restores correct DRAT order while preserving the 15383f6 subsumption fix. Early UNSAT-return path skips trailing deletions (matches old working behavior; harmless).

IMPACT: 1-day-old regression (15383f6). UNSAT verdicts are likely sound (proof-emission defect, not unsound reasoning); proofs were malformed. Any solver-11 UNSAT on a BVE-heavy instance since 15383f6 has a suspect proof until re-run.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New red-green regression test test_bve_proof_deletes_source_clauses_after_resolvents in main.rs (DONE: RED on buggy, GREEN on fix). 2) cargo test (459 pass) + smoke_test 9/9 (DONE). 3) End-to-end: fixed solver re-solves oski15a01b20s_opt and drat-trim returns s VERIFIED (IN PROGRESS). 4) Commit + push the fix. 5) Re-run the medium benchmark on the fixed solver and confirm the 2 oski instances verify.
notes:
End-to-end CONFIRMED 2026-06-21: fixed binary re-solved oski15a01b20s_opt -> s UNSATISFIABLE (25.5min), and drat-trim returned 's VERIFIED' (215.9s, 0 RAT lemmas in core) on the 4.5GB proof. Buggy binary on the same instance gave 's NOT VERIFIED'. Acceptance criterion 3 met. Remaining: commit+push fix, re-run medium bench.
Committed + pushed as 758eff0 on main (criterion 4 DONE). Bead intentionally left OPEN for criterion 5: re-run the competition medium benchmark on the fixed solver (held per user request).
profile20 confirmation (2026-06-21, run seedgate-confirm-main-758eff0): default config on current main (with the fix) reproduces the nb-bumpreasons-base baseline EXACTLY over 100 cells (20 inst x 5 seeds, 900s): solved 76=76, total conflicts on both-solved cells 104,825,045 = 104,825,045 byte-identical (0 conflict mismatches), PAR-2 -732.7 (within noise). 2 bp4_CSO_IXA_ZR solve<->timeout flips at the 900s boundary that cancel out (timing noise). Confirms the BVE proof fix is trajectory-neutral; no search regression.
Acceptance criterion 5 MET (2026-06-22): full medium re-run on fixed solver (log/bench-11-medium-2026-06-21-15-08-05) completed 100/100. Both oski15a instances now UNSAT,verified=ok (b40s 1479s, b20s 1512s) — were verified=FAIL on the buggy binary. ALL 24 UNSAT proofs verified=ok, zero verified=FAIL across the suite. Final: 53/100 solved (29 SAT + 24 UNSAT), PAR-2 183013. The only non-timeout non-solves are 4 honest 16GB resource cases (2 OOM ERROR + 2 memory-preflight UNKNOWN) on 8.6M-54M-var formulas, unrelated to the fix.
close_reason: Fixed in 758eff0. Validated: red-green regression test, cargo test 459/459, smoke 9/9, end-to-end oski15a01b20s_opt re-solved UNSAT with drat-trim VERIFIED (was NOT VERIFIED), and profile20 reproduces baseline exactly (76 solved, conflicts byte-identical, PAR-2 within noise). Full medium re-run on the fixed solver launched 2026-06-21 15:08 as final full-suite confirmation; reopen only if an oski proof still fails.

title: Re-evaluate SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved on profile20: hard-set +12 vs easy-set regression -> promote/gate/portfolio decision
description:
Decide whether/how to ship SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved, given a sharp conflict between hard-set and easy-set evidence. This is the top actionable outcome of the 2026-06-03 hard-search study; it is NOT a naive "flip the default" because prior work shows target-then-saved REGRESSES the easy set.

## The win (hard set)
hard-search 15-config study (log/hard-search-2026-06-03): `SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved` = **26 solved on the hard-7 (+12 vs default 14)** — the dominant lever. It RESOLVES Pancake's seed-fragility (4/10 -> 10/10, ~3-4x faster), cracks bp4 (6/10 SAT, default 0/10), and holds sqrt170 (10/10) with no hard-set regression. Mechanistically it closes a real kissat gap: the default profile uses phase_policy=Legacy (config.rs:674), while stock kissat's kissat_decide_phase IS target-then-saved (decide.c) — see SAT-playground-5b2.2.63.

## The catch (easy set) — do NOT ignore
Two CLOSED beads already show target-then-saved hurts the easy/profiling instances (both are in profile20's easy-10):
- SAT-playground-6wg: bundling target-then-saved with EMA restart makes 6s299b685_Iter30 7-8x slower (146s vs 17s); it was deliberately guarded out of the default profiles, kept only as an explicit override.
- SAT-playground-5b2.2.54: the phase-mapping benchmark matrix REJECTED target/best mappings because they hit UNKNOWN on Sudoku (hard failure) on the profiling suite.

## The decision
The hard-10 (+12) must be weighed against the easy-10 regression on the FULL profile20. Net could go either way. Possible outcomes, in preference order:
1. PROMOTE to the default/fast profile if it wins the lexicographic gate net across all 20.
2. INSTANCE-GATE it (route target-then-saved by formula classifier, the way SAT_BSR_FORMULA_GATE gates BSR — reuse pre_preprocess_formula_class) so the hard families get it and the Iter30/Sudoku families do not.
3. PORTFOLIO (default + a target-then-saved configuration).
4. REJECT for the default and keep as the documented explicit override.
Do NOT flip the default without the full-profile20 evidence in hand.
acceptance_criteria: Re-measure SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved on the FULL profile20 (all 20) with the 5x5 ad-hoc seedgate: tools/feature_ablation.py --seedgate --env 'SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved' --tag target_phase --seeds 5 --jobs 5 vs --env '' --tag baseline, then tools/check_solver11_promotion.py --multiseed (lexicographic solved->conflicts->PAR-2); N=10 for the authoritative verdict. REPORT the easy-10 / hard-10 split explicitly and state whether the hard-10 +12 survives NET against the easy-10 regression (esp 6s299b685_Iter30 and Sudoku — watch for UNKNOWN/timeout). title: Fix focused-mode VMTF deep-dive: avg decision level 31k vs 343 (VSIDS) on Sudoku
description: From SAT-playground-588 (log/d8p-focused-stable-perf/FINDINGS_588.md). Focused-mode VMTF is the largest single fixable contributor to the focused/stable throughput regression. Measured on Sudoku @200k conflicts: focused/VMTF runs at avg decision level 31,493 (max 307,092); the identical config with SAT_VMTF=off (VSIDS) drops it to avg 343 (max 2,321) - a 90x collapse. 1.16 matrix corroborates: focused/VSIDS 2.51M props/s vs focused/VMTF 1.22M. The deep dive bloats trails -> expensive propagation + high-LBD learning. Mechanism: VMTF picks a decision sequence that dives conflict-free; the relative EMA restart (fast_lbd>slow_lbd*margin, main.rs:4844) can't rescue it because uniform high-LBD keeps both EMAs high and conflict-driven restarts can't interrupt a conflict-free dive. ROOT-CAUSE + FIX: compare to kissat's VMTF/restart/phase interplay (benchmarks/reference-solvers/kissat/src/) - likely a missing depth guard, target-phase steering, or restart-on-deep-dive that the Rust focused VMTF lacks. VALIDATION (required, not a quick slice): focused/stable matrix re-run (5b2.2.46 methodology) + solver-11 promotion gate + shuffle_sensitivity; default profile bench will NOT show it (focused/stable is off by default). NOT instance-overfit: Kakuro focused/VMTF is fine (SAT@35k) and 6s299 has a different focused cost, so validate across the matrix. Gates the focused feature default (P0 5b2.2.53).
notes:
Residual focused/stable cost beyond the VMTF deep-dive (high LBD even with VSIDS; 6s299 slow high-LBD propagation) is clause-quality -> Phase-2 inprocessing/vivification, tracked under SAT-playground-5b2.3.18 [2.16]. This bead (SAT-playground-ibq) is the Phase-1 search-policy slice (VMTF deep-dive); the clause-quality slice is Phase 2.
Root-caused the deep-dive to a kissat-faithful restart-cadence divergence: Rust focused EMA restart uses base KISSAT_EMA_RESTART_MIN_CONFLICTS=50 + margin 1.20; kissat uses restartint=1 (RESTARTINT_DEFAULT) + restartmargin 10 (margin 1.10), checked every conflict. Diagnostic (set consts to 1/1.10) on Sudoku @200k: glucose restarts 554->3241, Sudoku now SOLVES (UNSAT@161k, 173.8s, competitive with default ~170s) vs orig diverging — BUT avg decision level only 31493->20616 and max_decision_level UNCHANGED at 307092, i.e. the conflict-FREE VMTF dive is NOT eliminated by conflict-gated restarts. Generalization @100k conflicts: 6s299 82.6s->63.7s (faster), Kakuro 12.5s->24.3s (2x SLOWER). So kissat-faithful restart is a TRADEOFF (rescues deep-divers Sudoku/6s299, regresses deep-searcher Kakuro), not a clean deep-dive fix. Running full focused-stable matrix A/B (orig base50/1.20 vs KF base1/1.10) on profiling suite @300s to get aggregate PAR-2 + rule out new timeouts before keep/reject. Logs /tmp/{orig,kf}_focused_bench.log; results in /tmp/sat-worktrees/{sh-orig,slate-heron}/log/bench-*.
REJECTED + reverted (slate-heron /nextbeads). Tried kissat-faithful focused restart (KISSAT_EMA_RESTART_MIN_CONFLICTS 50->1, MARGIN 1.20->1.10). Full focused-stable matrix A/B (profiling suite, 300s): orig 50/1.20 = 10/10 PAR-2 991.750; KF 1/1.10 = 9/10 PAR-2 1326.824. KF is a HARD FAIL: new timeout on mp1 (orig SAT 0.98s -> KF TIMEOUT 300s) + net worse (+335 PAR-2) + also regressed battleship 3.0->76.7s, velev, Kakuro, SCPC, brocard, while only helping Sudoku/6s299/REGRandom. The conservative base 50/1.20 is better-tuned than literal kissat values; aggressive restart is a tradeoff, not a fix. Reverted (git diff empty, smoke 9/9, no net code change). CORRECTIONS: (1) focused/stable does NOT diverge on Sudoku - orig solves it at 287.9s; the earlier UNKNOWN was a 200k SAT_LIMIT_CONFLICTS artifact. (2) Deep dive is real but NOT the gating issue: even orig focused/stable (991.8) and focused/VSIDS lose to single-mode default (750.3). If pursued, the deep dive needs a SURGICAL fix (focused VSIDS, or depth-triggered restart that doesn't touch mp1/battleship), not a global restart change. FINDINGS: log/d8p-focused-stable-perf/FINDINGS_ibq.md.
Rescope per f94ff37 (aggregate-PAR-2-only policy): kissat parity is NOT the goal. Judge any focused/VMTF fix on aggregate PAR-2 over the profiling suite vs the current single-mode default (solver 10 = regression floor), not on matching kissat behavior. Per-instance regressions and honest budget-consuming timeouts are acceptable if the aggregate improves. The already-rejected kissat-faithful focused restart stays rejected because it was net-worse on aggregate (+335 PAR-2, 9/10), not because of the per-instance mp1 timeout itself.

Per 5b2.2.53/ibq's own validation, the focused/stable feature default is NOT achievable via Phase-1 restart/deep-dive fixes (loses to single-mode default regardless of restart cadence); it needs Phase-2 clause-quality to become competitive. Removed from the ready queue accordingly.

title: Investigate focused/stable trajectory pathology: deep-dive + high-LBD clause learning (d8p)
description: From SAT-playground-d8p (log/d8p-focused-stable-perf/FINDINGS.md). The focused/stable throughput regression is a SEARCH-TRAJECTORY problem, not per-event code overhead. perf-record on Sudoku shows default and focused/VMTF have near-identical propagate-dominated symbol profiles; NONE of the 1.14 throughput-subtask targets (record_search_ticks, compute_lbd, vmtf_stamp, rebuild_branch_queue, maybe_switch_search_mode) appear (inlined/<1%). The 1.16 'guard100' config showed the opposite extreme (163,738 reluctant restarts). Both are restart/decision/mode POLICY pathologies. GOAL: root-cause the focused-mode restart cadence + VMTF decision diving + clause-DB glue that produce the deep-dive/high-LBD trajectory; fix the policy (restart frequency, decision heuristic, or clause learning) so focused/stable produces solver10-class trajectories. Sanity-check the max_decision_level=307092 stat. This is the genuine lever for the focused/stable feature default (gates P0 5b2.2.53), per the 5b2.2.30 'search-trajectory/inprocessing-dependent' verdict that d8p confirms.

The focused/stable regression is search-trajectory/clause-quality, instance-dependent (Sudoku: focused/VMTF avg level 31,493 vs default 236; Kakuro: focused fine, SAT@35k; 6s299: default also deep at 26k, focused 15x slower props/s). title: SH-A: CCMIN_INBLOCK uses same_level_only=true, regresses search trajectory
description:
Algorithmic regression — `CCMIN_INBLOCK` mode at src/main.rs:6374 sets same_level_only=true in RedundancyCheckContext, restricting the upfront recursive minimize so it cannot remove literals whose reason chains cross decision levels.

Kissat (kissat/src/minimize.c:172-195) uses one of two configurations: full cross-level minimize+shrink (shrink<=2) or no minimize+shrink (shrink=3). Solver 11 chose a third hybrid that is weaker than both — restricted upfront minimize + shrink that does NOT recover the lost cross-level coverage (see SH-B).

Evidence (log/analyzesat-2026-05-27-shrink-port):
- REGRandom-Seed40: A_baseline UNSAT 59.5s/1.61M conflicts -> D_inblock UNKNOWN at 301s with 10.65M conflicts (6.62x trajectory blowup, baseline-solved row now times out)
- 6s299b685: A 16.5s/3764 conflicts -> D 18.4s/4871 conflicts (+29% conflicts, +43% learned-clause literals on average)
- sudoku: A ~189s -> D 279s (contention-matched), conflicts pending solo A run

Fix: change src/main.rs:6374 to `same_level_only: false`. Either drop the field entirely or keep it for future shrink-restricted experiments.

Reference: kissat/src/minimize.c:172-195 for the two correct configurations.
notes:
s11-06 /nextbeads retry rejected: changed CCMIN_INBLOCK upfront redundancy context from same_level_only=true to false and added a focused red/green test, but SAT_CLAUSE_MIN=inblock SAT_STATS_JSON=on profiling still failed baseline-solved rows. SH-A-only run log/phase1/s11-06-prz-inblock-profile solved 7/10, PAR-2 2361.342, with TIMEOUT on REGRandom-K4-L1-Seed40, velev-pipe-sat-1.0-b7, and battleship-16-31-sat. Patch reverted; bead remains open for a different mechanism such as no-upfront-minimize+shrink or classifier-gated shrink.
SH-A + SH-B LANDED + committed 5a01032 (AmberFinch 2026-05-30). SH-A: same_level_only false for inblock upfront minimize (cross-level, matches default deep). SH-B: ShrinkBlockContext+frame_used/max_depth, threaded the lit_redundant stack, added cross-level minimize-via-reason recovery in shrink_literal_for_block (kissat shrink.c:63-77) reusing the state cache. CORRECT: cargo test 432+4 (oracle bruteforce), default smoke 9/9, INBLOCK smoke 9/9 drat-trim; default profile unaffected (shrink runs only for CCMIN_INBLOCK); updated the one shrink test that had encoded the buggy same-level behavior. EFFICACY (SAT_CLAUSE_MIN=inblock profiling, log/prz-inblock-2026-05-30/run1): broken inblock 3408 PAR-2 / 5-of-10 -> SH-A+SH-B 2371.803 / 7-of-10 (rescues 2 instances, -1036 PAR-2; battleship 0.092s is the lucky default not inblock). BUT inblock STILL TIMES OUT on K4, mp1, velev (mp1 default-solves ~42s) -> inblock remains a trajectory regression vs the default (722, 10/10) and stays OFF by default. KEEPING prz OPEN: the same_level_only bug + cross-level shrink gap are now fixed and kissat-aligned, but the residual regression is the SHRINK MECHANISM ITSELF hurting the K4/mp1/velev trajectories, not the minimize config. Deeper follow-ups: SH-C (0cu, backward-trail-walk start), and a no-upfront-minimize+shrink (kissat shrink=3) or classifier-gated-shrink variant, before inblock could be promotable. title: Lucky LH-1: with_temporary_assumptions deep-clones arena/watchers/binary_clauses on every pattern
description:
Gap LH-1 from analyzesat-2026-05-27-propagation-hotpath.

src/main.rs:3403-3445 `begin_temporary_assumptions` clones:
  saved_arena: self.arena.clone(),           // Vec<u32>, ~50 MB on velev
  saved_watchers: self.watchers.clone(),     // Vec<Vec<Watcher>>
  saved_binary_clauses: self.binary_clauses.clone(),

`try_lucky_assignment_with_proof` (src/main.rs:3766-3786) calls
`with_temporary_assumptions` once per pattern x 6 patterns. On velev
(8.76M clauses post-preprocess), each pattern adds ~50 MB of clone+restore
memory traffic; ~300 MB total per lucky run.

Pattern propagation never mutates arena/watchers/binary_clauses (no
learning, no GC inside the closure; `learn_lucky_failed_literal_units`
only fires after the closure returns). Save/restore should cover only:
- trail, trail_limits, assignment, decision_level, reason
- propagate_head, accounting_mode, branching-queue state

Kissat reference (kissat-latest/src/lucky.c:307-393) does NOT clone any
clause data structure for its lucky pass — it backtracks via level=0 and
the existing assignment-machinery.

Evidence: velev with SAT_LUCKY=on adds +5.6 s preprocess_sec vs lucky=off
on the same instance (same conflict count = 179,968), proving lucky's
preamble is pure overhead. log/analyzesat-2026-05-27-propagation-hotpath/raw/solver11_velev_lucky.stderr
vs solver11_velev_nolucky.stderr.

Fix sketch: add a `TemporaryAssumptionOptions { snapshot_arena: false }`
variant (or separate `begin_lucky_assumptions`) that skips the three
.clone() calls. Add a debug_assert that arena/watchers/binary_clauses are
unchanged at end of closure.

Predicted impact: lucky=on becomes neutral-to-positive on velev/Kakuro/
sudoku, unblocking lucky=on as a default-promotion candidate.
notes:
Claimed via /nextbeads. Work order position 1 of 1. Worktree /tmp/sat-worktrees/bluelake-3yw, branch agent/bluelake/lucky-lh1, base origin/main a48f9f5.
**REVERTED by /nextbeads (BlueLake, 2026-05-27 22:36 UTC).** The bead's premise that 'pattern propagation never mutates arena/watchers' is incorrect.

**Failure observation (velev, SAT_LUCKY=on, 120s cap):**
- Pristine (origin/main a48f9f5): SAT in **73.08 s**, 179,968 conflicts, 26.74 s preprocess, 1448 MB RSS
- Modified (snapshot_arena=false on lucky callers): SAT in **118.35 s**, **361,190 conflicts (+100%)**, 26.22 s preprocess, 1447 MB RSS

**Root cause:** `propagate` mutates BOTH arena and watchers in place during 2WL bookkeeping, even though it never *appends*:
- `set_clause_lit`/`swap_clause_lits` (main.rs:4317-4318, 4339-4340) rewrites positions 0/1 of each clause's literal slice in arena.
- Line 4342 `self.watchers[new_watch_idx].push(updated_watcher)` moves the watcher between watch lists when the watched literal becomes false and a new non-false candidate is found at position lit_pos≥2.

After backtracking, the 2WL *invariant* still holds (both watched literals unassigned at level 0), but the *specific watch positions* and clause-lit ordering are perturbed. The original deep-clone+restore was load-bearing: it restored the post-preprocess watch positions so post-lucky search saw identical clause-watch state. Skipping the clones leaves the post-lucky search with a different watch arrangement → different decision/propagation order → 2× as many conflicts on velev.

**No surgical middle ground:** arena and watchers are coupled. Restoring one without the other breaks the 2WL invariant (clause in wrong watch list, or watched lit not at position 0/1). It's either restore both (current behavior, costs 50 MB × 6 patterns × velev) or neither (this revert + measured regression).

**Stash:** the attempted change is preserved on branch `agent/bluelake/lucky-lh1` in stash "Lucky LH-1 attempt: snapshot_arena=false caused velev SAT_LUCKY=on regression 73s→118s" for reference.

**Suggested next investigation (do NOT just re-attempt this fix):**
1. Verify the Kissat reference claim. `kissat-latest/src/lucky.c:307-393` was cited as 'does NOT clone any clause data structure'. Check what Kissat actually does to suppress watch perturbation during lucky — does it use a separate non-mutating propagation variant, or does its post-lucky search tolerate the perturbation differently?
2. If Kissat does indeed leave watches perturbed, look for whether Kissat resets/reorganizes watches at some point after lucky (e.g. via a cheap watch rebuild) that solver 11 lacks.
3. Alternative: track which arena cells and which (watch_list, watcher_idx) pairs are mutated during lucky and undo just those — could be cheaper than full clones if mutation set is small.
4. Alternative: gate this only for very large formulas where the clone tax is large; on small/medium formulas the clone cost is already small and the regression risk dominates.

Smoke and cargo test still pass against the reverted (pristine) tree.
deep-analysis-2026-06-11: design direction confirmed safe - the trajectory-preserving alternative is UNDO-LOGGING the (few) arena/watcher mutations made during lucky probing instead of snapshot/restore; the undo log must cover every mutation including watcher-order changes to stay bit-exact (the clone is load-bearing for the post-lucky trajectory - do not naively remove it). Cost today: full deep copy of arena + every watch list + binary_clauses at solve start, peak 2x formula memory (main.rs:3698-3707), with lucky default-on. FINDINGS.md H18.
deep-analysis-2026-06-12: the temporary-assumption snapshot/restore is INCOMPLETE for binary-fast state - begin_temporary_assumptions snapshots arena/watchers/binary_clauses only (main.rs:3698-3710); edges added via register_binary_clause (2469-2482), the binary_id_by_clause map (2468), and binary_reason_lits (2455) would all survive the rollback. Vacuous today (no temp-assumption path registers a binary; lucky failed-literal units are added after end_temporary_assumptions, 3812-3846) but it is exactly the silent-desync class that costs days when a temp-scope feature lands: stale ids + stale reason lits handed to analysis. Whichever undo-log/snapshot design this bead lands, cover all six structures - or at minimum add a debug assertion in end_temporary_assumptions that binary_clauses.len()/binary_reason_lits.len() are unchanged.

title: Gap SC-2: chrono_max_delta threshold predicate inverted relative to kissat
description:
Solver 11's choose_backtrack_level (solver/11-kissat-port/src/main.rs:4926-4957) treats chrono_max_delta as 'max delta for which chrono BT fires': delta > chrono_max_delta returns assertion_level (non-chrono), delta <= chrono_max_delta returns current_level - 1 (chrono).

Kissat's kissat_determine_new_level (benchmarks/reference-solvers/kissat-latest/src/learn.c:16-42, identical in kissat-sc2024) treats chronolevels as 'min delta for which chrono BT fires': delta > chronolevels returns back (chrono), delta <= chronolevels returns jump (non-chrono).

Same threshold value 100, opposite truth tables.

Empirical impact at default delta=100, SAT_CHRONO=on, profiling suite (log/analyzesat-2026-05-27-search-control/B_chrono/stats.jsonl):
- sudoku: chrono_used=1.15M of 1.37M conflicts (84%), rejected_delta_too_large=11K. Wall +33% (207->275s), work +5.3x.
- 6s299b685: chrono_used=49K of 67K conflicts (72%). Wall +24%, work +18x.
- REGRandom-Seed40: chrono_used=3.3M of 4.75M conflicts (70%). Wall +243%, work +3x.
- mp1: chrono_used=89K of 284K conflicts (31% - the lowest fire rate). Wall -57%, work 0.67x. ONLY WIN.

The single win (mp1) is precisely the instance where the (inverted) predicate happens to reject most attempts. Kissat would fire chrono on 0.01-0.4% of conflicts on this suite (estimated from rejected_delta_too_large rates).

Fix sketch (~2 lines + counter rename + tests):
  // main.rs ~4940
  let delta = current_level - assertion_level;
  if delta <= self.chrono_max_delta {              // was: > 
      self.stats.chrono_rejected_delta_small += 1; // was: chrono_rejected_delta_too_large
      return assertion_level;
  }
  // existing chrono path unchanged

Also rename field chrono_max_delta -> chrono_min_delta (or chrono_levels for kissat parity). Update tests at main.rs:10937-10961 (test_chrono_rejects_large_delta becomes test_chrono_rejects_small_delta).

Reference: benchmarks/reference-solvers/kissat-latest/src/learn.c:16-42.
Evidence: log/analyzesat-2026-05-27-search-control/FINDINGS.md gap SC-2; B_chrono/stats.jsonl chrono_used columns.

Acceptance: after the fix, SAT_CHRONO=on on the profiling suite should drop chrono_used/conflicts ratios to <5% and the sudoku/6s/REGRandom regressions should largely disappear. Re-run analyzesat-2026-05-27-search-control B_chrono with the fix and compare.
notes:
Claimed by s11-06 via /nextbeads on 2026-05-27 EDT. Work order position 1; baseline profile log: log/bench-11-kissat-port-2026-05-27-21-17-57/results.csv (10/10 solved, PAR-2 824.728).
Implemented initial fix on 2026-05-27 EDT: chrono threshold now rejects delta <= SAT_CHRONO_MAX_DELTA and permits chrono only for larger deltas; telemetry renamed to chrono_rejected_delta_small. Targeted chrono tests are green after first confirming the old behavior failed them.
Final validation for d2b on 2026-05-27 EDT: fixed predicate to reject small deltas and compute delta as (current_level - 1) - assertion_level, matching Kissat back-jump semantics. Renamed stats output to chrono_rejected_delta_small and updated README wording. Tests: targeted chrono tests passed; cargo test passed (394 unit + 4 config_cli); smoke passed 9/9 at log/2026-05-27-21-40-28. Hot-path sanity: SAT_CHRONO=on SAT_STATS_JSON=on on 6s299b685 passed SAT in 22.468s with no UNKNOWN, but chrono_used remained high (89,312/94,254 conflicts), so follow-up SAT-playground-vnx now blocks default-promotion bead SAT-playground-59l.
Post-rebase validation on 2026-05-27 EDT: rebased onto origin/main, regenerated .beads/beads.jsonl conflict from Beads DB, reran cargo test (400 unit + 4 config_cli) and smoke 9/9 at log/2026-05-27-21-44-05. Rebased chrono sanity log: log/phase1/s11-06-d2b-chrono-sanity-rebased/results.csv and stats.jsonl; SAT in 22.329s, no UNKNOWN/TIMEOUT/ERROR, chrono_used still 89,312/94,254 conflicts as tracked by SAT-playground-vnx.

description:

title: Replace SAT_VMTF=single guards with Kissat focused-mode VMTF parity
description: Follow-up to SAT-playground-egy. title: Implement formula classification (binary fraction, size) for adaptive feature policy
description:
Task class: meta-policy / adaptive configuration. Implements kissat-style formula classification that routes runtime feature selection per-instance.

Background: Kissat (benchmarks/reference-solvers/kissat-latest/src/classify.c) computes two classification flags after preprocessing:
- solver->classification.small: clauses <= GET_OPTION(smallclauses)
- solver->classification.bigbig: binary_clauses / total_clauses >= bigbigfraction (default 99% per mille)

These flags are then read across the solver to switch policy (different reduce schedule, different restart trigger, etc).

Solver 11 has no formula classification. Every instance gets the same policy. The third-pass investigation (log/kissat-investigation-third-pass-2026-05-24/THIRD_PASS_FINDINGS.md, Gap 12) found that the BEST kissat-feature config in solver 11 is DRAMATICALLY per-instance:
- VMTF wins mp1 (43x), battleship (25x) but TIMES OUT on sudoku/REGRandom
- binary_fast wins case9 (4.6x), REGRandom (2.2x) but breaks mp1 and battleship  
- inblock minimization wins Kakuro (4x), Iter30 (1.3x) but breaks battleship/case9
- chrono helps mp1, Kakuro, velev but hurts REGRandom

Combination experiments (S1-S7) confirmed features ANTAGONIZE each other. The 'kitchen sink' S7 config loses on every instance vs the best per-instance config.

Without classification, solver 11 cannot route to the right policy. This is the deepest structural mismatch from the third-pass investigation: solver 11 has the FEATURES but not the ADAPTIVE SCHEDULER.

Proposed change: implement classify() that runs after preprocessing and before main search loop. Compute:
- formula_size_class: small / medium / large (clauses < 10k, 10k-1M, > 1M)
- binary_fraction: binary_clauses / total_clauses
- avg_clause_size: total_literals / total_clauses
- variable_density: total_literals / vars

Store as a formula_class field on the solver. Then:
- Add policy-selector functions that consult formula_class
- Initial routing rule (from third-pass data): if binary_fraction > 0.6 and small formula, enable VMTF + binary_fast; if large UNSAT random pattern, prefer A_default policy; etc.
- Routing decisions logged via SAT_STATS_JSON

Implementation notes:
- One-shot classification, not periodic.
- Hardcode routing rules initially; the rules can be tuned empirically.
- Future: dynamic re-classification after inprocessing rounds.

Tests:
  test_classify_small_formula_routes_to_vmtf
  test_classify_random_3sat_routes_to_baseline
  test_classify_logs_class_decision_in_stats

Acceptance criteria: cargo test pass, smoke pass, invariant smoke pass. Profile bench shows aggregate PAR-2 improvement when adaptive policy is enabled vs static A_default, with no instance regression > 20%.

Larger project role: closes Gap 12 from the 2026-05-24 third-pass investigation. Required prerequisite for safely defaulting any kissat-style feature that helps some instances and hurts others. Most direct path to making solver 11 beat A_default on the 10-instance profiling suite.

title: Allow VMTF branching in single-mode (not just focused-stable)
description:
Task class: branching heuristic activation. Enables solver 11 to use VMTF without requiring the focused-stable mode scaffolding that itself regresses the suite.

Background: VMTF (Variable Move To Front) is currently gated by THREE conditions in vmtf_branching_active (solver/11-kissat-port/src/main.rs:2863-2867):
1. self.vmtf_queue.is_some()
2. self.search_mode_policy == SearchModePolicy::FocusedStable
3. self.search_mode == SearchMode::Focused

Config-time validation in config.rs:1109 also enforces: 'SAT_VMTF=on requires SAT_SEARCH_MODE=focused-stable'.

This is overly strict. Kissat's bump.c:103-112 makes VMTF the unconditional focused-mode branching heuristic — but kissat's focused mode itself is just one half of always-running mode alternation. In solver 11, focused-stable mode alternation is broken (G_focused_stable solves only 5/10, log/kissat-investigation-2026-05-23-broad/FINDINGS.md), so requiring focused-stable as a prerequisite for VMTF traps users between two failure modes.

Evidence from third-pass investigation (log/kissat-investigation-third-pass-2026-05-24/THIRD_PASS_FINDINGS.md):
- I_vmtf_only (focused-stable + VMTF) solves mp1 in 1.5s, battleship in 0.9s, Kakuro in 63s, velev in 38s — dramatic wins on SAT-leaning instances
- But same config TIMES OUT on sudoku and REGRandom (the focused-stable mode penalty)
- The wins come from VMTF specifically, not focused-stable. M_chrono_only (no VMTF, no focused-stable) solves all 10 in +19% PAR-2.
- mp1 is THE canonical case: VSIDS-only takes 47s; VMTF takes 1.5s — 31x speedup just from the branching heuristic.

Proposed change: introduce SAT_VMTF=single|focused-only|off (default off) and decouple VMTF activation from search_mode_policy:
- 'single': VMTF active for the whole single-mode search (no focused-stable required)
- 'focused-only' (current behavior): VMTF only in focused-stable + Focused mode
- 'off' (current default): VSIDS only

Implementation notes:
- src/main.rs:2863 vmtf_branching_active gains a branch for single-mode VMTF
- src/main.rs:3934 pick_branch_lit needs to ensure VMTF queue is initialized in single mode
- Need to maintain VMTF queue (link/stamp updates) even when search_mode_policy=Single
- Config validation in config.rs:1109 should accept SAT_VMTF=single without requiring SAT_SEARCH_MODE
- Tests should cover both single-mode VMTF and focused-stable VMTF paths

Tests:
  test_vmtf_single_mode_activates_without_focused_stable
  test_vmtf_single_mode_solves_mp1_faster_than_vsids
  test_vmtf_queue_updated_in_single_mode

Acceptance criteria: cargo test pass, smoke pass, invariant smoke pass. Profile bench shows mp1 solves < 10s under SAT_VMTF=single (down from 47s under A_default), with no new timeouts on the 10-instance suite.

Larger project role: closes Gap 5 from the 2026-05-24 third-pass investigation. Unblocks VMTF wins on mp1 (43x), battleship (25x), Kakuro (4x), velev (2x) without the focused-stable mode regressions. Required prerequisite for SAT-leaning per-instance configs.

title: Implement kissat lucky-assignment heuristic before main search
description:
Task class: pre-search optimization. Implements kissat's lucky.c pre-search heuristic which catches trivially-SAT instances in O(VARS).

Background: kissat's kissat_lucky (benchmarks/reference-solvers/kissat-latest/src/lucky.c:307) runs before AND after preprocessing (search.c:184-189, gated by luckyearly=1 and luckylate=1 — both default ON). It tries assigning ALL variables to one polarity (true, then false, then 'backward setting') with bounded UP-propagation. If UP completes without conflict, the model is found.

Solver 11 has no lucky pass — search starts immediately after preprocessing with all phases at FALSE (initial_phase). Battleship-16-31-sat is a textbook lucky case: kissat solves it in 0.18s, solver 11 default takes 23.5s (130× slower), and solver 11's best config (S6_vmtf_otfs) takes 0.95s (5× slower than kissat).

Evidence: log/kissat-investigation-third-pass-2026-05-24/THIRD_PASS_FINDINGS.md Gap 6. Per-instance lookup table shows battleship is the canonical lucky case: kissat 0.18s, solver 11 A_default 23.5s, solver 11 S6_vmtf_otfs 0.95s.

Proposed change: add a SAT_LUCKY=on flag (default-on-but-opt-out for safety initially) that calls a lucky() method between BVE preprocessing and the main CDCL search loop. The lucky() method:
1. Snapshot current assignment, level 0.
2. Try all-true assignment (assume positive literal of every unassigned var); UP-propagate. If no conflict and trail==num_vars → SAT.
3. Backtrack, try all-false. Same check.
4. Backtrack, try 'backward' pattern (positive then negative alternating).
5. If any succeeded, write the model and exit with SAT.
6. Otherwise restore state and fall through to CDCL.

Implementation notes:
- Place in src/main.rs alongside other pre-search code (~line where preprocessing finishes).
- Probably needs a guarded version of propagate() that doesn't update activity scores or restart EMAs.
- Should run after preprocessing so it sees the simplified formula.
- Add a stats counter lucky_attempts/lucky_solved.

Tests:
  test_lucky_all_true_solves_horn_sat
  test_lucky_all_false_solves_dual_horn
  test_lucky_does_not_change_state_when_fails

Acceptance criteria: cargo test pass, smoke pass, invariant smoke pass. Profile bench shows battleship-16-31-sat solves in < 5s under default config (down from 23.5s).

Larger project role: closes Gap 6 from the 2026-05-24 third-pass investigation. Low risk because failed lucky calls just continue to normal search. May rescue several SAT-leaning instances in the broader 100-instance suite where kissat solves in < 1s.
notes:
Claimed via /nextbeads on 2026-05-25. Work order position 1 of 1 selected so far; before profile bench is log/bench-11-kissat-port-2026-05-25-21-18-03/results.csv (10/10 solved, PAR-2 859.447).
Implementation progress on 2026-05-25: added SAT_LUCKY config/schema/feature ledger support, post-preprocess lucky assignment attempts, JSON/trace counters, and focused all-true/all-false/failure tests. Targeted cargo test lucky passes. Fresh-eyes fix: require a full live-clause satisfaction scan before capturing a lucky SAT model, because watcher propagation alone can miss a complete falsifying assignment in this temporary probing path.
Completed implementation via /nextbeads on 2026-05-25. Added SAT_LUCKY default/fast pre-search SAT fast path after preprocessing: all-true/all-false probes, forward/backward false/true temporary propagation probes, and bounded small-formula local repair for non-eliminated formulas (<=2000 vars, <=200k original literals). Temporary probes now restore arena/watchers/binary-clause usage so failed probes do not perturb CDCL search; SAT is returned only after full residual-clause satisfaction check. Evidence: cargo test 356 passed; cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings passed; default smoke log/2026-05-25-22-29-34 passed 9/9; invariant smoke log/2026-05-25-22-29-47 passed 9/9; battleship acceptance log/bench-11-kissat-port-2026-05-25-22-29-54 solved SAT in 0.089s with lucky_attempts=7 lucky_solved=1 and 0 decisions/conflicts; final profile log/bench-11-kissat-port-2026-05-25-22-30-00 solved 10/10, 0 timeout/UNKNOWN/error, PAR-2 831.021 vs before log/bench-11-kissat-port-2026-05-25-21-18-03 PAR-2 859.447 (compare_bench PASS, -28.426). title: Reduce MAX_USED_RECENTLY from 3 to 2 to cure lbd-tiered learned-DB bloat
description:
Task class: solver-behavior tuning. One-line constant change in src/main.rs that recovers the lbd-tiered DB-bloat slowdown identified by the 2026-05-23 fresh-eyes investigation.

Background: src/main.rs:140 sets `const MAX_USED_RECENTLY: u8 = 3;`. This value is the initial `used_recently` counter assigned to every newly learned clause in `initialize_learnt_lbd` (src/main.rs:2174). The lbd-tiered reduce loop ages this counter down by 1 each pass (`age_learned_clause_on_reduce`, src/main.rs:5229-5243). A tier-1 or tier-2 candidate is only deletable when `used_recently == 0` (`reduce_candidate`, src/main.rs:5099-5119), so with MAX=3 every fresh clause survives at least 3 reduce passes regardless of LBD or usage. Combined with the sub-linear `learned_lit_budget` schedule (`refresh_learned_lit_budgets`, src/main.rs:4394 = `LEARNED_LIT_BUDGET_BASE + LEARNED_LIT_BUDGET_FACTOR * sqrt(reductions)`), this produces monotonic DB growth that bloats `learned_clauses_final` 3x-13x versus the legacy reducer, slows per-propagation throughput 2.0x-3.1x, and is the dominant mechanism behind the kissat-feature regression on the random profile-suite instances.

Investigation evidence: `/home/bojji/code/SAT-playground/log/kissat-investigation-findings-2026-05-23.md` (root-cause decomposition) and `/home/bojji/code/SAT-playground/log/kissat-investigation-experiment-2026-05-23.md` (4-variant knob sweep). Per-instance and aggregate numbers below come directly from those runs.

Proposed change: `const MAX_USED_RECENTLY: u8 = 2;`

Knob sweep (E_lbd_ema_tiered config, 6 profiling instances, 120s timeout, PAR-2 with 240s/TO):

| Variant | MAX | BUDGET_FACTOR | solved | PAR-2  | delta vs V0 |
|---------|-----|---------------|--------|--------|-------------|
| V0      | 3   | 300           | 5/6    | 318.85 | --          |
| V1      | 1   | 300           | 5/6    | 315.06 | -1.2%       |
| V2      | 1   | 100           | 5/6    | 313.23 | -1.8%       |
| V3      | 2   | 300           | 5/6    | 294.43 | -7.7%       |

V3 (MAX=2) is the recommended knob value. V1 (MAX=1) is too aggressive on the structured-SAT win cases: it pushes feistel_b64_k32_r22 from 21.08s (V0) to 50.13s (V1, +138%) because clauses get aged out before they have time to mature into useful reasons. V3 gives every fresh clause one extra reduce-pass of protection, which preserves the structured-SAT wins while still aging out the random-noise clauses. Tightening LEARNED_LIT_BUDGET_FACTOR (V2) only moves the needle 12% on one instance and is NOT the dominant lever.

V3 vs V0 on E_lbd_ema_tiered per-instance (s):

| instance              | V0     | V3     | ratio |
|-----------------------|--------|--------|-------|
| feistel_b64_k32_r22   | 21.08  | 24.68  | 1.17x | (only regression)
| feistel_b64_k52_r17   | 19.34  |  9.28  | 0.48x |
| feistel_b64_k57_r18   |  2.66  |  2.39  | 0.90x |
| random_v285_s2        | 10.68  |  6.77  | 0.63x |
| random_v292_s4        | 25.08  | 11.31  | 0.45x |
| random_v355_s3        |   TO   |   TO   |  --   | (separate problem — see below)

Mechanism confirmation (V3 vs V0 on E_lbd_ema_tiered, per-instance stats):

- feistel_b64_k52_r17: conflicts 273k -> 176k (0.64x), props/sec 1.90M -> 2.62M (1.38x), DB unchanged.
- random_v285_s2: conflicts 467k -> 324k (0.69x), props/sec 2.02M -> 2.18M (1.08x), DB 23007 -> 19321 (0.84x).
- random_v292_s4: conflicts 992k -> 514k (0.52x), props/sec 1.84M -> 2.11M (1.15x), DB 26286 -> 24884 (0.95x).
- feistel_b64_k32_r22: conflicts 343k -> 444k (1.29x, the cost), props/sec 2.67M -> 2.92M (1.09x), DB 44526 -> 40626 (0.91x).

V3 improves both axes (work x speed) on every instance except feistel_b64_k32_r22, where work increases by 29%. The +17% feistel_b64_k32_r22 regression is the documented cost.

A_default config is unaffected by this knob (the constant only matters when ReducePolicy::LbdTiered is selected). Sanity-checked: V0/V1/V2/V3 A_default rows are within 1% across all 6 instances.

Implementation:

1. Change one constant in solver/11-kissat-port/src/main.rs:140:
   - `const MAX_USED_RECENTLY: u8 = 3;` -> `const MAX_USED_RECENTLY: u8 = 2;`
2. Existing tests at src/main.rs:7588-7590 assert `MAX_USED_RECENTLY` literally on three tier checks; they will still pass because they use the constant by name.
3. No config-schema change required (the constant is not currently exposed via SAT_*).

Tests:
- existing test_lbd_*_initial_used_recently family must continue to pass.
- bash tools/smoke_test.sh solver/11-kissat-port — 8/8 expected.
- SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered bash tools/smoke_test.sh solver/11-kissat-port — 8/8 expected.

Benchmark gate (must run before promotion):
- bash tools/bench.sh -d benchmarks/profiling solver/11-kissat-port (default profile, no env override). Must remain PASS vs the most recent default-profile baseline (no solved-row regression).
- Same command with SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_RESTART=kissat-ema SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered SAT_STATS_JSON=on. Expected per the experiment: PAR-2 improves by ~24s on the 6 profiling instances. Watch the random_v355_s3 row — it remains TIMEOUT after this change.

Risk IDs: R3 (learned-clause correctness via aggressive eviction), R5 (search trajectory). Rollback: restore MAX_USED_RECENTLY to 3.

Out of scope (separate beads):
- random_v355_s3 TIMEOUT under E_lbd_ema_tiered persists after this change. Mechanism is EMA-restart trajectory, NOT DB bloat (V1, V2, V3 all shrink DB and still time out; D_lbd_tiered alone — Luby + lbd-tiered — also times out). Track separately.
- SAT-playground-5b2.2.44 (tier-2 evictable when !over_budget) and SAT-playground-5b2.2.49 (histogram bias audit) touch adjacent reduce_candidate code. They should be re-evaluated after this change lands because the smaller steady-state DB changes the tier distribution.

Reproduction (in worktree): /tmp/sat-analysis-kissat/log/kissat-investigation/exp/run_experiment.sh sweeps V0/V1/V2/V3 across the 6 profiling instances. Source files for the 4 variants are at /tmp/sat-analysis-kissat/solver/11-kissat-port/target/release/sat-solver-{v0,v1,v2,v3} (built in that worktree).
acceptance_criteria: MAX_USED_RECENTLY constant changed from 3 to 2. cargo test + smoke + lbd-tiered smoke all PASS. tools/bench.sh on benchmarks/profiling: no solved-row regression in default profile, ~7% PAR-2 improvement in SAT_USE_LBD+SAT_RESTART=kissat-ema+SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered profile. feistel_b64_k32_r22 +17% regression on E_lbd_ema_tiered documented in README. random_v355_s3 timeout under kissat features tracked as separate bead.
notes:
Identified during 2026-05-23 fresh-eyes solver 11 investigation. Empirical evidence: log/kissat-investigation-findings-2026-05-23.md + log/kissat-investigation-experiment-2026-05-23.md. 4-variant knob sweep ran on 6 profiling instances at 120s timeout.

Off MAX=3 log/phase1/1.14x-max-used-recently-retry-off-key solved 9/11, PAR-2 1823.076. On MAX=2 log/phase1/1.14x-max-used-recently-retry-on-key solved 9/11, PAR-2 1885.953 (+62.877). Wins: REGRandom -51.985s, random_v292 -13.855s, feistel_k52 -9.972s. Regressions: Kakuro +124.732s, Sudoku +12.453s, feistel_k32 +3.642s. mp1 and random_v355 remained TIMEOUT. Reverted to MAX_USED_RECENTLY=3. Summary artifact: log/phase1/1.14x-max-used-recently-key-retry-summary.md. Final checks after revert: cargo test used_recently, cargo test lbd_tiered, cargo test, cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, default smoke, and key-mode smoke all passed.
Deep investigation 2026-05-24 (log/kissat-investigation-2026-05-23-broad/DEEPER_FINDINGS.md, Phase 1 Gap 3) reframes this bead's recommendation.

Reading kissat source (learn.c:110, deduce.c:18, reduce.c:70-72) shows kissat uses a 5-bit used counter (MAX_USED=31) and sets c->used = MAX_USED on every learn or reason use. Solver 11 uses MAX_USED_RECENTLY=3 and bumps to max(used, 1) on reason use — a 50% protection for re-used clauses vs kissat's full reset.

The proposed MAX=3->2 change tightens fresh-clause aging by 33% but tightens reused-clause aging by 50% — a non-uniform shrink that doesn't match kissat semantics. This is why the 11-instance suite test rejected it: it hits the wrong quantity.

Correct semantic fix is split into a new bead (SAT-playground-ycw, 'Fix mark_learned_clause_recent bump semantics to match kissat'). That bead changes mark_learned_clause_recent to set used = MAX_USED_RECENTLY on reason use, AND optionally widens MAX_USED_RECENTLY toward kissat's 31 (7 or 15 as a first step).

Recommendation: close this bead once SAT-playground-ycw lands. The 'reduce MAX 3->2' direction is wrong; the 'bump-to-MAX on use AND widen MAX' direction is right.

title: [0.12] Add solver 10 vs 11 overhead regression gate
description:
Background:
The profiling comparison initially showed solver 11 PAR-2 712.310 vs solver 10 PAR-2 704.278 on the 120s profiling set, with identical solved/timeout outcomes but +8.032s solved-runtime delta. Interleaved repeats confirmed the overhead is real. This needs a repeatable gate so future agents do not reintroduce Section 0 instrumentation overhead or misread one-off benchmark noise.

Goal and intent:
Create a lightweight, repeatable overhead regression gate specifically for baseline solver 10 vs solver 11 parity. This gate should be cheap enough to run before Phase 1 performance work and precise enough to separate search-path changes from local overhead.

Implementation guidance:
- Add a script such as tools/ci_solver11_overhead.sh or extend existing CI tooling with an explicit overhead mode.
- Build solver/10-bve-preprocess and solver/11-kissat-port once in release mode.
- Run interleaved repeats with alternating order to avoid sequential thermal/cache bias.
- Include at least feistel_b64_k57_r18.cnf and random_v285_s2.cnf, because both are ~8s and confirmed the overhead signal.
- Record mean, median, per-run times, statuses, proof setting, and environment.
- For at least one representative instance, compare search counters to confirm identical conflicts/decisions/propagations/restarts when asserting overhead rather than search-path drift.
- Make the threshold configurable, but default to flagging/failing above <=1.5% median overhead after 0.10/0.11 have landed.

Constraints and considerations:
- Keep this gate separate from broad benchmark speed claims. It measures infrastructure overhead, not solver strength.
- Do not require perf hardware counters because this environment has perf_event_paranoid=4.
- The script should leave artifacts under log/ with enough detail for bead comments and future analysis.
- It may run fewer repeats in regular fast CI and more repeats when invoked explicitly.

Testing expectations:
- Validate the script detects the current known overhead before fixes, or records expected-fail semantics until 0.10/0.11 close.
- After 0.10/0.11, the gate should pass with the accepted threshold.
- Run ci_solver11_fast and the new overhead gate before closing.

How this serves the larger project goal:
This gives future solver work a stable performance baseline. Without it, later algorithmic changes could be judged against a moving baseline contaminated by instrumentation overhead.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible overhead-gate script or documented CI command runs interleaved solver 10/solver 11 repeats on representative profiling instances, records status/search-counter parity, reports mean and median deltas, and fails or clearly flags when default solver 11 overhead exceeds the accepted threshold; gate passes after 0.10/0.11 fixes and blocks M.1/Phase 1 until then.
notes:
Started 2026-05-19 after 0.10, 0.11, and 0.13 closed. bv now lists this as the next ready executable Section 0 bead. Plan is to add a lightweight overhead gate that builds solver 10/11, runs interleaved alternating-order repeats on the Feistel and random profiling instances, records log artifacts with per-run/mean/median/status/counter parity, and fails when solver 11 median overhead exceeds the default threshold.
Implemented and reviewed solver 10 vs solver 11 overhead regression gate.

title: [0.10] Remove always-on hot-path stats overhead
description:
Background:
Section 0 added rich JSON stats and hot-path propagation counters to solver/11-kissat-port. Interleaved confirmation after Section 0 showed the overhead is real, not just sequential benchmark noise:
- feistel_b64_k57_r18, 5 interleaved repeats, default proof: solver 10 mean 8.497s, solver 11 mean 8.828s, +3.90%; median +3.84%.
- random_v285_s2, 5 interleaved repeats, default proof: solver 10 mean 8.394s, solver 11 mean 8.799s, +4.83%; median +4.55%.
- With SAT_PROOF=off, overhead persisted: feistel median +4.38%, random median +5.11%.
- Solver 11 JSON stats on feistel showed the same search work as solver 10 trace output: conflicts=551925, decisions=679410, propagations=43725178, restarts=1149. This points to per-operation overhead rather than a changed search trajectory.

Observed likely root cause:
solver/11-kissat-port/src/main.rs::propagate increments diagnostic counters on every watcher scan, blocker hit, stale skip, clause load, and binary/long implication. On feistel_b64_k57_r18, solver 11 reported watch_scans=576422300, watch_blocker_hits=344181851, watch_clause_loads=232240338, binary_props=4615846, long_props=42267146. These counters are currently updated even when SAT_STATS_JSON=off and tracing is off, adding hundreds of millions of extra hot-path stores.

Goal and intent:
Keep Section 0 observability, but make the default solver 11 hot path effectively solver-10-equivalent when diagnostic hot counters are not requested. Future Phase 1 algorithm work must not start from a baseline that is already 4-5% slower from instrumentation.

Implementation guidance:
- Introduce a stats/diagnostics mode that distinguishes always-required core counters from optional hot diagnostic counters.
- Keep core counters needed for correctness, trace summaries, and benchmark status, but gate high-frequency counters such as watch_scans, watch_blocker_hits, watch_clause_loads, watch_stale_skips, binary_props, and long_props behind an explicit config flag or compile-time specialization.
- Prefer a low-overhead design: const generic propagation helper, split fast/diagnostic propagation paths, or another pattern that lets the compiler remove diagnostic increments from the default path.
- Preserve JSON schema compatibility. When hot diagnostics are disabled, emit an explicit hot_diagnostics_enabled field or document zero/null semantics.
- Do not remove the ability to collect these counters for profiling/debugging.

Constraints and considerations:
- Do not silently drop stats fields used by tooling; update validators/tests if semantics change.
- Default behavior should remain SAT Competition compatible and proof/model correct.
- Avoid adding branches inside inner watcher loops if the branch still costs materially at scale.
- Compare default profile against solver 10 with the same proof setting and same run.sh path.

Testing expectations:
- Add unit tests or integration tests for the new stats mode/config behavior.
- Run cargo fmt, cargo test, SAT_STATS_JSON=on cargo test, smoke, invariant smoke, ci_solver11_fast.
- Run repeated interleaved overhead confirmation on at least feistel_b64_k57_r18 and random_v285_s2.
- Record before/after medians, means, search counters, and proof setting in the bead comment.

How this serves the larger project goal:
Solver 11 is supposed to become a Kissat-class optimization branch. Section 0 instrumentation is useful only if it does not distort performance baselines. This bead restores a trustworthy baseline before later Phase 1 changes are judged.
acceptance_criteria: Default solver 11 runtime overhead versus solver 10 is reduced to <=1.5% median on repeated interleaved feistel_b64_k57_r18 and random_v285_s2 runs with identical status and search counters; hot diagnostic counters remain available when explicitly requested; cargo test, smoke, invariant smoke, ci_solver11_fast, and the overhead confirmation check pass.
notes:
Started 2026-05-19: bv ranks this as the highest-priority ready Section 0 bead. Plan is to preserve JSON stats observability while removing default hot-path counter stores from propagation, then rerun solver 11 tests, smoke, CI, and interleaved solver10/solver11 overhead checks.
Implemented 2026-05-19: added explicit SAT_STATS_HOT/hot_stats config defaulting off, routed Solver::propagate through const-generic fast vs diagnostic implementations so watcher hot counters are compiled out of the default inner loop, emitted hot_diagnostics_enabled in JSON_STATS, preserved opt-in watch/binary/long counters, updated CONFIG_SCHEMA/README/SOLVER11_STATE, and added unit tests for config replay plus opt-in propagation counters. Fresh-eyes review fixed a README replay-override mismatch. Validation: focused new tests pass; cargo test passes 103/103; SAT_STATS_JSON=on cargo test passes 103/103; smoke passes 9/9 with proof checks; tools/ci_solver11_fast.sh passes including fmt, clippy, plan validation, invariant smoke, smoke-plus bench PAR-2 0.055, and reproducibility. Interleaved 5-repeat overhead check with default proof: feistel18 median s10=8.512332s, s11=8.447512s, delta=-0.761%; random285 median s10=8.396415s, s11=8.389109s, delta=-0.087%; all statuses identical. Diagnostic parity on feistel with SAT_PROOF=off: solver10 and solver11 both conflicts=551925 decisions=679410 propagations=43725178 restarts=1149. Default JSON hot counters are zero with hot_diagnostics_enabled=false; SAT_STATS_HOT=on restores watch_scans=576422300, watch_blocker_hits=344181851, watch_clause_loads=232240338, binary_props=4615846, long_props=42267146.
close_reason: Completed hot-path stats overhead fix. Default solver 11 overhead versus solver 10 is now within threshold on repeated interleaved feistel18/random285 checks, hot diagnostics remain available through SAT_STATS_HOT=on, and the required solver 11 tests/gates pass.

  4. Only then attempt 1.15 promotion.

Rationale: the original 1.16 matrix compared a high-overhead focused/stable to a low-overhead default. If the throughput subset closes most of the propagations/s gap and the focused/VMTF aggregate PAR-2 movement holds, the deferred-to-Phase-2 verdict changes and Phase 1 promotion becomes possible. Candidate rule:

```text
- candidate configs must use SAT_PROFILE=experimental until promotion
- candidate configs must be complete enough that `env -i` plus the listed SAT_* variables reproduces the run
- if 2.15 keeps transitive reduction, forward subsumption, or RCheck, create additional named candidate replay files with concrete `on`/`off` values rather than editing these snippets in place
- every candidate must produce a SAT_CONFIG_OUT replay file
- candidate comparison must use SAT_CONFIG_REPLAY, not hand-retyped env snippets, for promotion reruns
```

Candidate D is removed from the main Phase 2 gate. Aggressive ELS/BCE mixes belong in Appendix A after explicit triage.

Promotion rule:

```text
Default on only if:
  - brute-force oracle passes all enabled simplification variants
  - smoke proofs verify
  - tools/ci_solver11_proof_model.sh passes for the promoted profile
  - SAT assignments satisfy original formula
  - profiling solved count or PAR-2 improves
  - search-core does not regress badly from simplification perturbation
  - regression-guards preserve previously solved instances
```

Profile-specific promotion:

```text
Candidate A can promote into `default.preprocess=Conservative` only after its replay file passes promotion gates.
Candidate B can promote into `default.preprocess=Conservative` only if HBR proof/model behavior is verified and its replay file passes promotion gates.
Candidate C can promote into `fast.preprocess=GateAware` before becoming baseline only after its replay file passes promotion gates.
Appendix features never join baseline until they have their own proof/model/full-set promotion gate.
```

Phase 2 full gate:

```bash
bash tools/bench.sh -t 1800 -m 16384 \
  -d benchmarks/sat-comp-2025 solver/11-kissat-port
```

Target direction:

```text
- approach Kissat-class performance on the discriminating set
- reduce SC-2025 PAR-2 toward 110_000 or better, subject to measured noise
- if ELS/BCE/walking/optional sweep do not earn their place through milestone triage, leave them parked rather than forcing implementation
```

## 2.15 Phase 2 feature retirement and candidate pruning

### Goal

Remove or park weak Phase 2 features before composing final candidate profiles.

### Dependencies

2.3 through 2.12, 2.14.

### Acceptance

```text
- each Phase 2 feature has a keep/tune/park decision
- each kept feature has at least one named benchmark-family win or proof/model necessity
- any feature with only noise-level gains remains experimental
- candidate profiles contain only kept features
- parking decisions are recorded in log/phase2/triage.md
- parked implemented features have either:
    * code retained with tests and FEATURES.csv maturity=ParkingLot, or
    * code deleted with a rollback note and archived validation artifact
- no parked feature remains in CONFIG_SCHEMA.csv as a promoted-profile default
```

title: Honest-UNKNOWN hardening: mid-search memory guard, SIGTERM handler, proof-write-failure degradation
description: Three crash modes that lose the s-line (the worst outcome class per repo rules): (1) OOM mid-search: memory preflight runs only at startup (main.rs:8171); under the bench 16GB ulimit -v a failed allocation mid-search aborts (panic=abort, SIGABRT rc134, no s-line, no result.json). Real occurrences recorded in config.rs:53-70. Fix: fold the rlimit-aware effective_memory_limit_bytes (limits.rs:74-83) into RuntimeLimits with a safety margin and check VmSize (NOT VmHWM - rlimit constrains virtual address space) periodically; degrade to s UNKNOWN reason=rss-limit. Implementation note: throttle the /proc probe to every N conflicts - today each SAT_LIMIT_RSS_MB check is a multi-microsecond /proc read called up to 3x per conflict cycle (main.rs:7824,7918,7949,7962 -> stats.rs:384-394). (2) No signal handling anywhere: harness timeout (SIGTERM) kills instantly - no s UNKNOWN, no JSON_STATS, so every TIMEOUT cell records conflicts=NA, losing the work-x-speed decomposition data. Install a minimal SIGTERM flag checked at the existing limit poll; exit through the normal UNKNOWN path with stats. (3) Proof-write failure: flush_stream and finish_unsat use .expect (main.rs:1055-1058,1012-1017) - ENOSPC during DRAT streaming aborts mid-search (a disk-fill already killed a campaign on this host); ProofStats.write_errors exists but is incremented nowhere. Fix: on write error record it, disable the stream, continue; UNSAT downgrades to s UNKNOWN reason=proof-io-error via the existing ProofCompleteness::Incomplete machinery. FINDINGS round-2 N28 (CA-F9/F10/F11/F13).

Fix: delegate the Experimental arm to the Default arm then apply deltas. (2) CONFIG_SCHEMA.csv default columns stale for 6 rows: SAT_USE_LBD, SAT_SEARCH_MODE, SAT_MODE_USE_TICKS, SAT_REDUCE, SAT_VMTF (all still pre-promotion values) and SAT_CHRONO_MAX_DELTA says 100 vs code DEFAULT_CHRONO_MAX_DELTA=5000 (config.rs:15). Only 3 rows are test-asserted today. Fix the rows and add a closure test iterating EVERY schema row asserting the default columns equal the parsed profile configs. title: Experiment-integrity guard: SAT_STRICT_CONFIG in ablation/seedgate cells, config_hash TSV column, unknown-SAT_* warning

title: CHB branching + UCB mode-arm selection (kissat-MAB lineage, SC2025 winner)
description: Verified: AE-Kissat-MAB won SAT Competition 2025 main track (PAR-2 2264.73, 327/400; satcompetition.github.io/2025 slides; a kissat-MAB descendant). title: SAT-detection ordering: check all-assigned before restart/reduce/mode-switch (kissat search.c parity)
description: In the no-conflict branch, run_post_propagation_scheduling (restarts + mode switches) fires at main.rs:7928, then GC/simplify/reduce/limits, and SAT is only detected inside pick_branch_lit at 7958. When post-backjump propagation completes the assignment while restart_pending is set (set during the PRIOR conflict, main.rs:4946/4887/4864), the solver restarts first - backtracking the satisfying assignment, and a stable-mode restart may rephase saved phases (maybe_rephase_on_stable_restart at 5511) so the model is not even faithfully replayed by phase saving. kissat search.c:198-209 checks !solver->unassigned BEFORE kissat_reducing/kissat_restarting. Fix: maintain an unassigned counter (all_live_decision_vars_assigned at main.rs:3750 exists but is O(V)) and check it at the top of the None branch, jumping straight to capture_sat_model. Trajectory-CHANGING (turns some late restarts into immediate SAT exits) - N=10 seedgate. FINDINGS round-2 N2.
notes:
round-3 2026-06-13: two adjacent details. (a) With no next-decision candidate at restart time, reuse_*_trail_level returns current_level (main.rs:5398-5400, 5419-5421), making the restart a no-op while restarts/restarts_reused_trails/_levels still increment (5483-5509) - a stats artifact of the same missing all-assigned check; fix together. (b) Minor ordering: the port runs mode-switch/restart before reduce in the no-conflict branch (7928-7947) while kissat checks reduce first (search.c:204-211) - one-propagation reduce delay when both are due; align while reordering for the SAT check.
