title: DRAT stream hygiene: stop copying the input formula into the proof; emit deletion lines from simplify/trim
description: record_live_original_clauses_for_proof (main.rs:7543-7549, called at 7666 before eliminate, origin commit 1457d57) writes EVERY live original clause as a DRAT addition at solve start under the default ProofPolicy::Drat. Costs: O(formula) write I/O on every run including SAT/UNKNOWN (tmp written then discarded); proof ~doubles on preprocess-light UNSAT; and the duplicate copies make every original-clause d line ineffective in drat-trim (it deletes one copy, the CNF copy stays active) - defeating eliminate/BSR deletion lines and slowing verification. kissat never logs original clauses as additions. Fix: emit additions only for clauses whose normalized form differs as a multiset from the input (typically zero), or drop the pass and accept benign checker warnings for dedup cases. ALSO: delete_clause_for_simplify (main.rs:3254-3270) and trim_root_false_literals_with_proof (3203-3252) emit no DRAT deletions - root-satisfied clauses and fat pre-trim originals stay in the checker active set forever (kissat collect.c:321 logs them); add record_deletion at both sites. Trajectory-neutral. Validate via smoke test drat-trim gate. FINDINGS round-2 N1/N3.
notes: Consolidation 2026-06-13: absorbed 5b2.2.18.10 (closed as duplicate) - merged scope adds: gate the per-clause canonical literal sort in write_clause_line (main.rs:963-982, O(k log k) per learned clause AND per deletion) behind a canonical-output flag, default OFF (checkers do not need sorted clauses); consider opt-in binary DRAT for local benching. One trajectory-neutral PR: formula-prefix removal + simplify/trim d-lines + sort gating, validated by the drat-trim smoke gate.

title: BSR subsumption-queue mark hygiene: marks leak on budget exhaustion; queue fills undrained when BSR gated off
description: Two leak paths: (a) budget-exhausted return from backward_subsumption_check leaves the queue populated with header mark=2 set and nothing ever resets them (simp.rs:996-998; enqueue at 221-227; outer loop drops the queue at 1382-1384); (b) with run_full_backward_subsumption=false the eliminate loop STILL enqueues via gather_touched_clauses and try_eliminate_var resolvents into a queue nobody drains - O(touched+resolvents) wasted memory on exactly the large formulas the gate targets, plus mark=2 leaking into search headers, surviving GC (main.rs:6070-6076) and the abstraction rebuild (main.rs:3091). Latent today (search only tests mark==1), but any eliminate() re-entry skips mark!=0 clauses permanently (simp.rs:217) - silently shrinking BSR reach. HARD BLOCKER for inprocessing reuse (5b2.3.1). Fix: drain-and-unmark on every early exit + skip enqueueing when BSR is off; kissat resets subsume flags at candidate collection (forward.c:139). FINDINGS.md S8 + BVE-agent F15.

round-3 2026-06-13: the mark==2 leak also survives the inline-abstraction MIGRATION path, not just GC - ensure_original_clause_abstractions copies clause_header_mark verbatim during the arena rebuild (main.rs:3091) exactly like GC does (6074). Both copy sites need the scrub or the drain-on-exit fix covers them.

title: Congruence closure over extracted gates (AND/equiv first, XOR increment)
description: Absent, previously unplanned - and the only XOR-aware reasoning kissat has (congruence.c 4636L: extract AND/XOR/ITE gates syntactically, hash by normalized inputs, merge same-input gate outputs as equivalences, propagate merges to fixpoint, forward-subsume rewritten-gate clauses; first pass of every kissat probe, delay backoff at yield <0.1%). Targets tseitin_grid_n12_m12 (XOR grid), VexRiscv BMC (structural sharing), and finishes what bounded-window sweeping misses. Subset first: AND + equivalence with a union-find repr shared with ELS; XOR extraction (arity<=4 by clause counting) is the highest-value increment. Merges are cashed in by ELS (prerequisite, 5b2.3.34). Note 5b2.3.12 covers only gate pattern hints for BVE - not closure, no XOR. Effort M-L; time-box XOR/ITE increments separately. FINDINGS.md inventory 2.3.
notes: deep-analysis-2026-06-12: PRIORITY RAISED P3->P2. Two new arguments: (1) the DRAT-safe XOR question is settled - CryptoMiniSat-style Gauss-Jordan was evaluated and rejected (XOR-derived propagations have no compact DRAT justification; CMS disables Gauss under DRAT), making congruence-with-XOR-extraction (congruencexors/congruencexorarity in kissat options.h) the ONLY proof-compatible XOR reasoning available for the miter/XOR/crypto-flavored hard-10. (2) Port from kissat-LATEST, not sc2024: the 4.0.0->4.0.4 diff fixes an ITE-gate witness polarity bug in congruence.c (PUSH_STACK cond -> not_cond on the extension stack) - the sc2024 version can produce INVALID SAT MODELS, a correctness-rule violation; also a match-test fix and an iterator aliasing fix in the cond-equivalence merge.

title: BSR marks-based O(c) subsumption/strengthen check; decouple or retire sorted-walk gating
description: subsumption_relation is an O(driver_len x candidate_len) nested scan per pair (simp.rs:366-386) - worst case 10^6 literal compares for 1 budget tick. kissat forward.c:330-385 marks the driver lits once per driver (per-literal byte scratch), then each candidate check is one O(len) scan with O(1) membership + single-flip tracking for strengthening. The marks scheme is order-insensitive, which also retires two adjacent defects: (a) the sorted merge-walk is gated on inline_original_abstractions (>=750k clauses, main.rs:145) - an unrelated condition - so all mid/small formulas always pay the quadratic path (simp.rs:353-360); (b) clauses_sorted_by_var is set once (main.rs:2059) and never invalidated though root propagation physically permutes clause literals via swap_clause_lits (main.rs:4421-4445), so the sorted walk soundly-but-silently MISSES subsumptions on propagation-touched clauses exactly where it is active. Also kills the per-candidate driver-lit enum dispatch (simp.rs:370,412,884-890). This is the concrete hot-path mechanism for 5b2.3.11. FINDINGS.md S1/S2.
notes:
2026-06-17 (IndigoGlacier): measured-footprint REJECT of the marks-over-sorted slice. Implemented default-OFF SAT_BSR_MARKS_OVER_SORTED routing the would-have-sorted (driver,candidate) pairs to marked_subsumption_relation; cargo test 459 green incl. new regression test marks_path_recovers_subsumption_the_sorted_walk_misses, smoke 9/9. Before seedgate, measured real inprocessing effect (SAT_STATS_JSON + SAT_LIMIT_CONFLICTS=3000) on all 8 large profile20 instances the bead claimed were affected: pre_bsr_subsumed/strengthened are BYTE-IDENTICAL off vs on for bp4(identical ticks 36968521), sudoku-N30, REGRandom, VexRiscv, velev, 6s299, Kakuro. ONLY brocard differs: subsumed 368842->368840, strengthened 1094854->1095475 (+621, ~0.06%). => the 'live on 8 of 20' severity claim is WRONG (it was inferred from clause-count headers, not measured misses); sorted-walk silent-miss is effectively absent on profile20 (only brocard, negligible). Identical preprocessing output => identical deterministic search => any seedgate is a foregone TIE except brocard, whose only 'win' would be a forbidden lucky-order flip. Slice stashed (solver/11-kissat-port stash@{0}), not committed. Bead left OPEN; the full marks rewrite + sorted-walk retirement is even lower-value than thought for profile20 PAR-2.
fresh-review 2026-06-17: ground-up source review confirms this bead should not stop at the current default-off SAT_BSR_MARKS_OVER_SORTED slice. The larger target is a true Kissat/CaDiCaL-style amortized marks relation: mark the reusable side once per driver/candidate sweep and make each checked clause pay one linear scan, rather than calling marked_subsumption_relation with a fresh candidate mark per (driver,candidate) pair. Current source still marks the candidate in simp.rs:512-533 and routes each pair through subsumption_relation at simp.rs:414-471. Keep the flag slice as a correctness/effectiveness repair for sorted-walk misses, but treat the full per-driver marks rewrite as the real hot-path item. Do not create a separate marks bead; fold any 64-bit abstraction/sorted-path cleanup here.

Implemented a true per-driver BSR marks relation, first broadly for BSR candidate checks and then narrowed only to the branch where the old selector would have used candidate-marked relation. cargo test and smoke passed for the broad patch, but 5x5 seedgate tag bsr-driver-marks was aborted after clear solved-count regressions: oddball seed0/3 moved to TIMEOUT and mp1 seed1 hit a 60s targeted timeout despite baseline solving in ~2s. The narrowed variant still timed out mp1 seed1 at 60s. Root cause appears trajectory sensitivity from changed strengthening/subsumption behavior/order, not a pure relation-check speedup. All Rust changes reverted; do not reattempt this as a default-path rewrite without a mechanism that proves identical edits/order or a much narrower gate.

title: BVE resolvent-engine refactor: single-pass flat-buffer generation, value-aware merges, unit/empty harvest, sorted two-pointer merge, direct proof deletions
description: One coherent rewrite of try_eliminate_var to the kissat resolve.c shape: (1) single pass generating resolvents into a flat scratch buffer with separators while counting against the bound (resolve.c:88-262) - implements 5b2.3.25 (every resolvent currently computed twice: merge_size_only simp.rs:1227-1246 then merge_into_vec 1275-1296) and 5b2.3.26 (materialize before removing originals; currently Phase 2 reads tombstoned clauses, simp.rs:1266-1296 - unlocks in-pass GC 5b2.3.23); (2) value-aware merging - skip satisfied antecedents, drop falsified literals; today bounds are computed against garbage once mid-pass units land (simp.rs:1090-1157 never consult lit_value; kissat resolve.c:116-187 + flush_units eliminate.c:160-205); (3) harvest unit/empty resolvents even when the elimination aborts on the growth bound (kissat learns them unconditionally and excludes units from the resolved count, resolve.c:216-237); (4) two-pointer merge over the already-var-sorted antecedents (CanonicalSorted default): O(c+d) vs current O(c*d) nested scans, early complementary-pair exit, early size-limit exit, sorted output bypassing the normalize re-sort (simp.rs:1102-1154,568-572); (5) log DRAT deletions directly from live clauses after materialization, dropping the proof_deletions Vec<Vec> buffering currently paid even with proofs disabled (simp.rs:1265-1269). title: BVE/BSR: garbage-collect arena during eliminate pass (tombstones never reclaimed -> OOM)
description: remove_original_clause_preprocess (simp.rs:282) tombstones clauses (clause_set_deleted, deleted_clause_words++) without reclaiming arena memory, and this path is shared by both BVE and BSR. BVE can append resolvents through add_original_clause_from_slice, while BSR's backward_subsumption_check (simp.rs:886) can delete subsumed clauses through remove_original_clause_preprocess and shrink clauses through strengthen_original_clause_preprocess (simp.rs:441). The eliminate() driver (simp.rs:1283, while-loop 1329-1335) never calls maybe_garbage_collect (that runs only in the search loop, main.rs:5551). A long default pass grows the arena monotonically: originals + BVE resolvents + BSR-deleted tombstones + stale occurrence entries -> OOM. Add periodic in-pass GC when the garbage ratio is high (reuse maybe_garbage_collect / GC_GARBAGE_RATIO_*). This is the shared memory mechanism behind the VexRiscv OOM and can be triggered by either BVE-heavy or BSR-heavy formula mutation, not just BVE.
acceptance_criteria: In-pass GC added for the eliminate pass and exercised for both BVE deletion/resolvent growth and BSR subsumption/strengthening; arena/peak memory bounded across a long eliminate pass; VexRiscv no longer OOMs. The implementation must explicitly account for dense arena-word-indexed relocation/metadata allocations on this path, especially ensure_original_clause_abstractions and GC relocation: it must not add new arena.len()-sized scratch beyond existing GC requirements, and if current GC relocation remains dense, document why the in-pass GC trigger keeps old arena + relocation map + rebuilt arena below the 14-16 GB cap on VexRiscv, or replace that relocation with sparse live-clause remapping/side tables. Validate on the FULL profile20 with a multi-seed sweep of at least 5 seeds per instance: run tools/feature_ablation.py --seedgate with at least 5 seeds for the candidate and the current default, decide with tools/check_solver11_promotion.py --multiseed using the lexicographic solved-to-conflicts-to-PAR-2 gate, and record the per-instance and aggregate delta. Include at least one BSR-on stress case that performs subsumption/strengthening enough to exercise the GC trigger. cargo test + bash tools/smoke_test.sh green; no SAT/UNSAT correctness contradiction, invalid model, or missing/invalid proof.
notes:
2026-06-07 amendment from VexRiscv OOM log/code review: this bead should not be satisfied by merely scheduling GC earlier if the run can still hit the same arena.len()-sized relocation/metadata memory cliff. title: Make target+rephase combination exactly match kissat (reset_phases/decide_phase fidelity)
description:
Make the **target-phase ↔ rephase ↔ best-phase interaction** in solver/11-kissat-port match mainline kissat's `reset_phases()` + `kissat_decide_phase()` semantics exactly when both `SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved` and `SAT_REPHASE=on` are enabled (the combination this fix targets).

Context: the profile20 hard-search study (log/hard-search-2026-06-03) found phase policy is the dominant lever (target_phase +12 solved on the hard-7, rephase_500 +7). The repo's rephase/target/best wiring diverges from kissat in several concrete ways; the combination was never tested and won't reproduce kissat's dynamic. Reference: kissat-latest/src/rephase.c (`reset_phases`, `rephase_*`), decide.c (`kissat_decide_phase`), backtrack.c (target/best save). Repo: solver/11-kissat-port/src/main.rs `apply_rephase` (5242), `reset_target_phase` (5120), `pick_branch_phase`/`effective_phase_policy` (5005/4688), `maybe_capture_phase_prefix` (5158).

## Divergences to fix (repo → kissat)

1. **target after rephase — SEED, don't empty.** kissat does `memcpy(target, saved, VARS)` (rephase.c reset_phases) so target = the freshly-rephased saved, then `target_assigned=0` so it re-accumulates from that baseline. Repo `reset_target_phase()` fills target with UNASSIGNED (emptied). Fix: copy saved→target after the schedule fn, then zero target_assigned.

2. **best_assigned reset only on 'best' rephase.** kissat zeroes best_assigned only when the scheme is `best` (best is re-earned). Repo never resets best_assigned. Fix: reset best_assigned on the best-scheme rephase so best re-captures.

3. **inverted scheme.** kissat sets saved = uniform `-INITIAL_PHASE` (rephase_inverted). Repo flips the *current* saved per-var. Fix: invert relative to the initial phase uniformly.

4. **rephase interval growth.** kissat grows the limit ~ n·log³n (`UPDATE_CONFLICT_LIMIT(rephase, rephased, NLOG3N)`). Repo adds a fixed interval each time. Fix: match the NLOG3N growth schedule.

5. **best at decision time (biggest divergence — gate carefully).** kissat's `kissat_decide_phase` consults only `target → saved → INITIAL` (in stable; focused has the occasional INITIAL flip); **best is NEVER read at decision — it only feeds rephase**. Repo's stable sub-mode `effective_phase_policy` = `BestThenTargetThenSaved` (best read first). To match kissat exactly the stable decision order must be `target → saved → initial`. ⚠ This changes the **default** config (focused-stable uses BestThenTargetThenSaved in stable even with rephase OFF), so it is NOT purely a "combination" change — gate it to the phase combination or validate the default impact separately on profile20 before shipping.

6. **trigger parity.** Verify repo's "rephase on stable restart" (rephase_due_on_stable_restart, 5184) lines up with kissat's `kissat_rephasing` (stable && CONFLICTS > limit). Reconcile if they differ.

Out of scope here: the WalkSAT rephase slots — tracked by [A.1] Walking local-search rephaser (SAT-playground-5b2.6.1), which must make the full 6-slot schedule [best, walk, inverted, best, walk, original] match kissat when walk+rephase+target are all on.
acceptance_criteria: With SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved + SAT_REPHASE=on, the saved/target/best array updates and decision-phase selection match kissat's reset_phases()+kissat_decide_phase() exactly (walk slots excepted — see SAT-playground-5b2.6.1). Unit tests assert: (a) after a rephase target == saved (seeded, not emptied); (b) best_assigned reset only on the best-scheme rephase; (c) inverted yields uniform -INITIAL_PHASE; (d) rephase interval follows NLOG3N growth; (e) stable decision order target->saved->initial with best NOT consulted at decision (gated so the rephase-off default is preserved or separately re-validated on profile20). cargo test + smoke green; no SAT/UNSAT correctness or proof regressions; if default decision behavior changes, run the multi-seed profile20 lexicographic gate and record the delta.
notes:
deep-analysis-2026-06-11: additional fidelity gaps beyond reset_phases/decide_phase - (1) rephase interval is fixed at 1000 conflicts vs kissat NLOG3N growth (rephaseint * rephased * log10(rephased+9)^3) so late-search rephasing thrashes saved phases (main.rs:5248-5263 vs rephase.c:88-137); (2) cycle is [best,inverted,original] vs kissat [B,W,I,B,W,O] - substitute the W slots with B/O until walk (5b2.2.70) exists; (3) after rephase the port clears target to UNASSIGNED instead of kissat memcpy(target,saved); (4) best_assigned must reset on the B step (see 5b2.2.66 - it currently never resets at all); (5) kissat flushes the trail to level 0 before rephasing; the port fires inside perform_restart_if_pending with a possibly partially-reused trail (main.rs:5265-5269). FINDINGS.md R4.
Consolidation 2026-06-13: absorbed 5b2.2.66 (closed as duplicate) - merged scope now includes: best_assigned has NO reset path anywhere (frozen at historical high-water mark; kissat rephase.c:14-21 resets when best is consumed) and the stable decide default reads best FIRST (BestThenTargetThenSaved, main.rs:4706-4708,5031-5045) where kissat decide.c:159-215 never reads best in decide. IMPORTANT: these bite even with SAT_REPHASE=off, so validate the decide-order fix on the rephase-off default path separately. 5b2.2.64 (target-then-saved promote/gate decision) stays separate - measurement, not mechanism.
close_reason: Consolidated into 5b2.2.65 (kissat restart+phase parity) 2026-06-14 - reset_phases fires from the restart path; phase-reset fidelity + restart scheduling validated as one policy. Bug content preserved in 5b2.2.65.

Before any default promotion: (1) n>=3 confirmation of the -11.5 aggregate delta; (2) shuffle_sensitivity / suite-robustness check to gauge how fragile the battleship-driven win is; (3) full solver-10 + check_solver11_promotion.py gate. title: Phase-1 feature on/off combination + parameter-tuning sweep vs solver-10
description:
Systematic benchmarking to find a Phase-1 feature COMBINATION (and/or parameter tuning) that improves the default-profile aggregate PAR-2 — the gap the P0 SAT-playground-5b2.2.53 tracks (solver-11 single-mode default ~750-786 vs solver-10 ~700).

WHY THIS BEAD EXISTS: all Phase-1 features have been tested mostly ONE AT A TIME, and each regresses the single-mode default individually: focused/stable (5b2.2.53, ibq), lbd-tiered (4a3), restart trail-reuse (0s0), searched-cache (1oo), lucky (blocked at LH-1/3yw), throughput micro-opts (variance-neutral, [1.14] subtree closed). The common failure modes are mp1 trajectory fragility and a diffuse infra throughput tax (5b2.2.56). But feature INTERACTIONS can be non-linear and have NOT been systematically swept, and per-feature PARAMETERS have not been exhaustively tuned under the aggregate-PAR-2 objective. This bead captures that exploration.

SCOPE:
1. On/off combination sweep (use /analyzesat multi-config ablation) over: SAT_USE_LBD, SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered, SAT_SEARCH_MODE=focused-stable, SAT_VMTF, SAT_RESTART=kissat-ema, SAT_PHASE=target/best, SAT_CHRONO (now that SC-2/d2b is fixed), SAT_REORDER, SAT_RESTART_REUSE_TRAIL, SAT_LUCKY (once LH-1 unblocks). Prioritize combos with a mechanism rationale (e.g. LBD + tuned restart + clause-tiering together reducing conflicts enough to overcome overhead) over brute force.
2. Parameter tuning of promising features: restart cadence (KISSAT_EMA_RESTART_MIN_CONFLICTS base, margin), reduce schedule (SAT_REDUCE_DB_INIT/INTERVAL/MIN_INTERVAL), tier thresholds (TIER1/2 relative targets), EMA windows (SAT_EMA_SLOW_WINDOW), restart_block_margin.

DECISION METRIC: aggregate PAR-2 over benchmarks/profiling vs the single-mode default; a promotable winner must also clear the solver-10 regression floor and the 5b2.2.19 promotion gate (discriminating + SC-2025). Watch mp1/case9/battleship (trajectory-fragile) and REGRandom (UNSAT) — combos that regress those tend to lose aggregate.

HONEST PRIOR (moderate-low): individual features regress and the documented high-prior lever is Phase-2 clause-quality (5b2.3.18 inprocessing/vivification). This sweep is to rule feature synergies in or out before committing to Phase-2 as the sole path — a negative result is itself valuable (confirms Phase-1 features can't beat solver-10 even in combination). Record every kept/rejected combo + tuning with aggregate PAR-2 in the solver README, and use shuffle_sensitivity on any input-order-sensitive win.

Related: 5b2.2.53 (P0 goal), 5b2.2.19 (promotion gate), 5b2.5.6 (M.5 guarded-chrono+throughput milestone), 5b2.3.18 (Phase-2 lever). Supersedes the per-feature matrix approach of the closed 5b2.2.46.
close_reason: Consolidation 2026-06-13: closed as superseded-by-events. Premise (every Phase-1 feature individually regresses the single-mode default; sweep combinations to beat solver-10) predates the 2026-05-30/31 fstab_lbdtier promotion, which IS the winning combination (focused-stable + LBD + tick mode-switch + lbd-tiered + lucky; beat the solver-10 floor). title: Lucky LH-2: missing no_all_negative_clauses / no_all_positive_clauses precheck before AllTrue/AllFalse patterns

possibly satisfy a formula containing an all-positive (resp. all-negative)

title: Restart trail-reuse never fires in default profile (Gap CD-4)
description:
Kissat restart.c:69-110 runs reuse_focused_trail (focused) or reuse_stable_trail (stable) on every restart, using the next-decision variable's VMTF stamp / VSIDS score as the cutoff. Trail levels whose decision variable has higher rank than the next-pick are preserved.

Solver-11 restart_reuse_trail_level (main.rs:5046-5073) short-circuits to 0 unless search_mode_policy == FocusedStable. The default profile uses single mode, so trail reuse NEVER fires in the default profile — every restart is a full backtrack(0). Even within focused-stable, the focused-mode branch requires vmtf_branching_active() to be true (default SAT_VMTF=off), stacking another gate.

Cost: re-derives lower-level unit propagations after every restart on instances with many restarts (sudoku 617 restarts, REGRandom 3069, mp1 1020).

Fix: decouple restart_reuse_trail_level from search_mode_policy. Remove main.rs:5052-5054. Replace VMTF gate at main.rs:5061-5063 with a fallback to VSIDS scores when VMTF queue is absent. Make the default profile honour SAT_RESTART_REUSE_TRAIL=on even in single-mode.

See log/analyzesat-2026-05-26-clausedb-cycle/FINDINGS.md gap CD-4.
notes:
Claimed via /nextbeads (VioletRidge), work order 1 of 1. Default-path restart-subsystem mechanism (kissat VSIDS-cutoff trail reuse in single-mode; currently restart_reuse_trail_level short-circuits to 0 unless FocusedStable). Non-overlapping with in-flight 18.12 (conflict-analysis). Fresh eval under aggregate-PAR-2 policy: the README's single-mode trail-reuse rejection was the 'harmful SAT-prefix' hybrid under the OLD per-instance policy; this is the score-cutoff mechanism judged on aggregate PAR-2. NOTE the mp1 risk (trajectory-affecting; mp1 broke 1oo and a prior reuse hybrid) - decision is aggregate over the suite.
EVALUATED + reverting (VioletRidge /nextbeads, 2026-05-29, base origin/main 2f466ac). Implemented single-mode VSIDS-cutoff trail reuse: new Solver field restart_reuse_trail_single (from config.restart_reuse_trail), restart_reuse_trail_level single-mode branch now calls reuse_stable_trail_level when SAT_RESTART_REUSE_TRAIL=on (was unconditional return 0). Mechanism CONFIRMED working+correct: brocard reused_trails 0->3, reused_levels 0->9, both runs UNSAT-correct; cargo test 433 PASS (updated the single-mode no-reuse test into off-default + opt-in tests), smoke 9/9. EVALUATION (profiling suite, 300s, flag-off vs SAT_RESTART_REUSE_TRAIL=on, same binary): flag-off 786.5 PAR-2 (10/10). flag-on REGRESSES: mp1 SAT 45.2s -> TIMEOUT (+554.8; the trajectory-fragile instance, same one that broke 1oo). 4 rows measured before stop-losers-early (off 323.861 -> on 876.629, +552.8); mp1's +554.8 alone exceeds the 462.6 max recoverable from the unmeasured 6 rows, so net regression is guaranteed. title: Tier-1 clause protection is permanent in lbd-tiered reducer (Gap CD-3)
description:
Kissat reduce.c:65-87 decrements every reducible clause's c->used at every reduce. Tier-1 (glue <= tier1) clauses are protected only while c->used > 0. Once a tier-1 clause's used reaches 0 it can be reduced like any other clause, which keeps the tier-1 pool bounded.

Solver-11 reduce_db_lbd_tiered at main.rs:6014-6022 excludes tier-0 (== kissat tier-1) clauses from reduce_candidate unless emergency AND used_recently == 0 AND is_old_enough_for_emergency_demote. The emergency gate is learned_literals > hard_learned_lit_budget which is a tight budget; under normal operation tier-1 clauses NEVER age out.

Compounding: age_learned_clause_on_reduce at main.rs:6143-6157 only decrements meta.removable tier-2/3 clauses, so tier-0 used_recently never decreases either.

Fix: change tier-0 gate in reduce_candidate (main.rs:6014-6022) to mirror kissat: return None only when used_recently > 0; otherwise allow deletion. Then update age_learned_clause_on_reduce to decrement tier-0 used_recently too.

Existing bead SAT-playground-5b2.2.44 covers Tier 2 vs Tier 1 differentiation but does not address the permanent-protection semantics.

See log/analyzesat-2026-05-26-clausedb-cycle/FINDINGS.md gap CD-3.
notes:
VioletRidge 2026-05-29 (from 4a3 investigation): tier-0 permanent protection is REAL and confirmed (reduce_candidate main.rs:6382-6390: tier-0 only deletable on emergency AND used_recently==0 AND old-enough; age_learned_clause_on_reduce main.rs:6597 only ages removable used_recently>0). But 4iu's fix (let tier-0 age out -> delete MORE) is the direction case9 wants (default solves case9 by reducing aggressively, lbd-tiered keeps ~2x clauses and times out) yet the OPPOSITE of what mp1/REGRandom want (mp1 solved by hoarding; more deletion broke REGRandom in prior s11-06 attempts). So 4iu is a genuine knob but cannot resolve the opposite-preference tension on its own; validate strictly on aggregate PAR-2, never on mp1/case9 alone. lbd-tiered overall is not promotable (4a3 verdict: 1887 vs 842 PAR-2). Evidence: log/analyzesat-2026-05-29-lbd-tiered-trajectory/FINDINGS_4a3.md.
Deferred 2026-05-29 (VioletRidge, approved by Brian): lbd-tiered is not promotable per 4a3 (mp1/case9 want opposite clause-retention; SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered loses ~1887 vs baseline ~842 PAR-2). This improves a non-default, non-promotable feature with no current path to default. On ice; revisit only if Phase-2 (5b2.3.18) clause-quality work changes lbd-tiered viability.

title: Binary fast-path: per-edge bookkeeping eats predicted savings (Gap CD-1)
description: Source diff in analyzesat-2026-05-26-clausedb-cycle shows solver-11 SAT_BINARY_FAST=on still pays per-edge binary_clause_is_deleted check (main.rs:3919), per-edge mark_binary_clause_used write (main.rs:3928, 3932), and vec-of-vec fragmentation in BinaryImplications::Nested (main.rs:280-287). Kissat proplit.h:74-92 has zero arena dereference and zero per-binary bookkeeping; the implied lit is inline in head.blocking.lit. Initial evidence: B_binary_fast vs A_baseline on sudoku-N30-12 (50.8% binary fraction): props/s 5.25M vs 5.64M (binary_fast 7% SLOWER per prop), 6% wall improvement comes from 11% fewer conflicts (trajectory), not execution speedup. Fix: inline-tag watcher list (4-byte Watcher with binary bit; long-clause tail follows), eagerly remove deleted binaries from watcher list, drop per-binary used counter (kissat does not track it for binaries). See log/analyzesat-2026-05-26-clausedb-cycle/FINDINGS.md gap CD-1.
notes:
deep-analysis-2026-06-11: two concrete cost reductions for the fast path - (1) per-edge slice re-derivation: len_for(lit) + edge_for(lit,idx) redo lit_to_index + enum match + Vec::get + slice index per EDGE (main.rs:4280-4283,311-331); hoist the edge slice once per literal (kissat hoists begin/end pointers, proplit.h:54-58); the Flat variant exists but is never constructed outside tests (main.rs:8984,2097). (2) drop per-edge deleted-check + used_count/last_used_conflict RMW from the hot loop (main.rs:2499-2511) - handle deletion by edge removal, mark usage only on conflict/reason use. Kissat binary cost: one 4-byte tagged watch + 1-byte value, zero metadata (watch.h:18-44, proplit.h:76-93); the port pays ~3 random loads + 1 RMW per edge on top. FINDINGS.md H2/H19.
deep-analysis-2026-06-12: three lifecycle gaps to fold into the fast-path work - (1) strengthen 3->2 under binary_fast_path creates a PERMANENT dual representation: attach_clause registers the clause in the binary registry (main.rs:3627-3628) while its old long-clause watchers persist (lazy detach), so the clause is propagated forever by both the edge list AND the watcher path (the long path handles len-2, 4480-4483) - strict-detach on register_binary_clause from the strengthen path. (2) BinaryImplications::mark_deleted is a NO-OP for the Nested variant in production use (main.rs:360-364, constructed at 2097): deleted binaries leave 2 dead edges each, costing a per-edge binary_clause_is_deleted indirection into the 40-byte BinaryClause struct on every scan, with no compaction path (rebuild_flat_if_needed is a stub that clears dirty without rebuilding, 367-371). Add edge compaction under GC (BinaryClauseId is stable). (3) the Flat variant is dead code with a quadratic insert (Vec::insert + O(num-literals) offsets bump per edge, 341-357) and the lying stub - delete it or implement a real CSR rebuild; its enum match also sits in the hot accessor. Memory: arena copy + registry + 2 edges + binary_reason_lits + id-map is ~2.7x the default representation per binary.
Consolidation 2026-06-13: absorbed b16 (closed as duplicate) - merged scope: binary fast-path rework = inline-tagged edges / per-edge bookkeeping removal / strengthen-3->2 dual-representation fix / Nested-variant edge compaction / dead-Flat removal, PLUS jumpreasons reason-flattening as a gated sub-experiment inside the same enqueue path (kissat assign.c:32-45, default on for bigbig). Each behavioral piece gets its own N=10 gate; the rework itself is the enabler. 5b2.6.5 stays separate (long-clause watch-path experiments).

title: Frame-used singleton check in lit_redundant (Gap CV-2)
description: Solver 11's lit_redundant (main.rs:1619-1709) lacks kissat's O(1) singleton-frame fast-rejection from minimize.c:32-37. Kissat tracks frame->used (literal count at each level) during 1UIP deduce; when minimizing at depth 0 or along a binary chain, a literal at a level with frame->used <= 1 cannot be removed (removing it would leave the level empty). Without this check, solver 11 recurses through the full DFS only to discover unremovability. Action: add per-decision-level used counter on the analyzed-variable struct (kissat keeps it on frame), increment it during analyze_conflict_to_scratch_impl when a literal is at a non-current level, and short-circuit in lit_redundant when frame->used <= 1. Prerequisite for Gap CV-1 (port shrink). Reference: kissat/src/minimize.c:32-37, kissat/src/deduce.c:63. Evidence: log/analyzesat-2026-05-26-conflict-vmtf/FINDINGS.md.

title: Replace literal sorting proxy with Kissat-style initial watch selection
description:
Numeric literal sorting currently doubles as initial watch selection for canonical-sorted clauses. That couples subsumption-friendly representation to propagation/search trajectory and makes input-order preservation look better than it really is on a single Kakuro row. Implement a mechanism-level fix: normalize clauses, then select initial watches using a Kissat-style policy without relying on full physical literal sorting.

Implementation notes:
- Study kissat_sort_literals/new_original_clause and mirror the watch-choice intent, especially root-level behavior.
- Decouple stored clause order, watch choice, and any sorted data needed by subsumption.
- Avoid making DIMACS file order the default performance mechanism.
- Preserve explicit diagnostics for sorted/input-order modes until the new path is benchmarked.

Acceptance:
- Initial watch choice is an explicit function with focused unit tests for root-unassigned, assigned, falsified, duplicate, unit, binary, and long clauses.
- Sorted subsumption either uses a separate sorted view/metadata or is disabled only with measured justification.
- cargo test, default smoke, and invariant smoke pass.
- Profiling-suite benchmark compares canonical-sorted, canonical-input-order, and the new Kissat-style watch path with no new UNKNOWN/result errors.
notes:

Rationale: do the mechanism-level follow-up after reverting the overfit auto gate; inspect Kissat initial clause/watch behavior, then make watch selection explicit without making DIMACS input order a promoted default.
Implemented explicit SAT_INITIAL_CLAUSE_MODE=kissat-watch diagnostic path. It canonicalizes/deduplicates clauses, selects the first two watched literals with a Kissat-style order_kissat_initial_watches helper, keeps the remaining tail canonicalized, and disables sorted-subsumption for that mode because the physical clause order is no longer globally sorted. Added focused tests for root-unassigned/input-order watches, assigned/unassigned preference, falsified-level ordering, duplicate/unit/binary handling, tautology skip, satisfied skip, and falsified literal removal. Validation: cargo fmt --check; cargo test kissat_watch -- --nocapture; cargo test initial_clause -- --nocapture; cargo test (380 + 3); cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings; bash tools/smoke_test.sh solver/11-kissat-port (9/9, log/2026-05-26-18-08-57); SAT_CHECK_INVARIANTS=on bash tools/smoke_test.sh solver/11-kissat-port (9/9, log/2026-05-26-18-09-01); git diff --check. title: Auto-enable SAT_BINARY_FAST when SAT_FULL_BSR=on
description:
Task class: solver-behavior policy coupling.

Background: analyzesat-2026-05-26-preprocess discovered that SAT_FULL_BSR=on creates many short clauses (binaries) on certain formulas (Kakuro 24% literal reduction, velev 11% literal reduction). On formulas dominated by long clauses, these new binaries go through the long-watcher list in solver 11's default propagation path because SAT_BINARY_FAST=off by default.

The net effect on Kakuro: A_default (BVE+BSR) spends 34.6s on prep AND search takes 214.4s (256.5s total). D_no_bsr (BVE only) spends 4.8s prep AND search takes 42.3s (53.9s total) — search itself is 5.1x slower under BSR-preprocessed clauses.

On velev: A_default 27.9s prep + 51.4s search = 82.1s. D_no_bsr 5.3s prep + 8.9s search = 17.0s — search 5.8x slower under BSR.

Conflict trajectories are within noise (same conflicts, decisions, propagations counts before and after BSR). The slowdown is per-prop execution cost: BSR-produced binaries are propagated via the long-watcher path which inflates watcher list size without giving the implication lookup the binary fast path.

Kissat (benchmarks/reference-solvers/kissat-latest/src/forward.c:678-690 kissat_forward_subsume_during_elimination) integrates forward subsumption with the binary watch arrays and inline binary propagator.

Proposed change:
* When SAT_FULL_BSR=on at config-validation time, automatically set SAT_BINARY_FAST=on (unless explicitly disabled)
* Coordinate with the existing rule that SAT_BINARY_FAST=on disables SAT_CLAUSE_MIN (the binary-min-otfs investigation found this is unsafe — see log/analyzesat-2026-05-26-binary-min-otfs/FINDINGS.md); ensure SAT_CLAUSE_MIN remains at its current default (recursive-limited) when both are on

Tests:
* test_bsr_on_auto_enables_binary_fast
* test_bsr_on_preserves_clause_min_default
* test_explicit_binary_fast_off_still_honored

Acceptance: cargo test pass, smoke pass, SAT_LUCKY=on profiling suite shows Kakuro and velev recover at least 50% of D_no_bsr's wins (Kakuro <130s, velev <40s) while preserving REGRandom/brocard SAT-finding (still solving within 300s).

Evidence: log/analyzesat-2026-05-26-preprocess/FINDINGS.md (Gap PRE-2 section).

Companion to SAT-playground-f06 (formula classifier gating BSR per-instance) — this fix
helps the always-on path; f06 helps with selective skipping.

title: Make SAT_CHRONO=on default for kissat-feature configs
description:
Task class: default policy change. Promotes chronological backtracking to default based on third-pass evidence.

title: Align EMA slow window with kissat (4096 -> 100000)
description:
Task class: parameter alignment / restart calibration.

Background: Solver 11 (src/main.rs:148-149) sets EMA window constants:
  const RESTART_FAST_ALPHA: f64 = 1.0 / 32.0;     // window = 32
  const RESTART_SLOW_ALPHA: f64 = 1.0 / 4096.0;   // window = 4096

Kissat (benchmarks/reference-solvers/kissat-latest/src/options.h:49-50, averages.c:13-14):
  OPTION (emafast, 33, ...)
  OPTION (emaslow, 1e5, ...)     /* slow EMA window = 100,000 */

The fast windows are roughly aligned (32 vs 33). But solver 11's slow window is 4096, kissat's is 100,000 — a 24x difference. This means solver 11's slow EMA adapts FAR more quickly to recent glue changes, making the fast/slow ratio cross the restart trigger threshold more often than it would in kissat.

Combined with Gap 1 (no trail reuse on restart) and Gap 4 (margin 1.20 vs 1.10), this is part of why solver 11's EMA restart over-fires on UNSAT-random instances even though the per-fire conditions look conservative.

Evidence: log/kissat-investigation-third-pass-2026-05-24/THIRD_PASS_FINDINGS.md Gap 9. The interaction with kissat-ema restart trigger and lbd-tiered reducer is documented in the earlier DEEPER_FINDINGS.md, but this specific calibration mismatch was not bead-ified.

Proposed change: change RESTART_SLOW_ALPHA from 1/4096 to 1/100000, matching kissat. Make it configurable via SAT_EMA_SLOW_WINDOW so the trade-off can be tested with a parameter sweep.

Implementation notes:
- One-line constant change.
- May need to adjust restart_min_conflicts in tandem if EMA initialization takes longer (100k slow window = 100k conflicts before slow EMA stabilizes).
- Should be tested specifically with SAT_RESTART=kissat-ema enabled.

Tests:
  test_ema_slow_window_matches_kissat_after_change
  test_ema_restart_trigger_less_volatile_with_large_slow_window

Acceptance criteria: cargo test pass, smoke pass, invariant smoke pass. Parameter sweep on benchmarks/profiling under SAT_RESTART=kissat-ema shows restart count reduced 1.5-3x on REGRandom (currently 28k restarts on mp1 under C_lbd_ema) and trail rebuild waste decreased proportionally.

Larger project role: closes Gap 9 from the 2026-05-24 third-pass investigation. Companion to the trail-reuse work (existing bead 5b2.2.35); both together should make EMA restart no worse than Luby on UNSAT instances.
notes:

title: Fix mark_learned_clause_recent bump semantics to match kissat (Gap 3)
description:
Task class: solver-behavior algorithmic correctness. Refines the kissat lbd-tiered port semantics to match kissat's reference behavior.

Background: solver/11-kissat-port/src/main.rs:2255-2266 in mark_learned_clause_recent currently uses:

    let recent = self.learnt_used_recently(clause_idx).max(1);
    self.set_learnt_used_recently(clause_idx, recent);

This bumps the used_recently counter back to at least 1 when a learned clause is used as a propagation reason. By contrast, kissat (benchmarks/reference-solvers/kissat-latest/src/learn.c:110 and src/deduce.c:18) sets used to MAX_USED on every learn or reason use:

    c->used = MAX_USED;   /* MAX_USED = 31, a 5-bit field, see clause.h:14-17 */

kissat then ages used by 1 per reduce pass (reduce.c:70-72). So a kissat clause used recently is fully protected for ~MAX_USED reductions, regardless of when it was created. Solver 11's max(used, 1) semantics protect a fresh-then-reused clause for at most 1 additional reduce pass — far less than kissat.

Evidence: deeper investigation 2026-05-24 (log/kissat-investigation-2026-05-23-broad/DEEPER_FINDINGS.md, Gap 3) verified the divergence by reading kissat source line-by-line and tracing the keep rule in solver 11. Per-instance ablation showed this is one of two compounding mechanisms (with Gap 2 fixed-fraction deletion) that make D_lbd_tiered+E_lbd_ema_tiered keep the wrong subset of clauses.

Proposed change (2-part, atomic):
1. Set used = MAX_USED_RECENTLY in mark_learned_clause_recent instead of max(used, 1).
2. Consider widening MAX_USED_RECENTLY from 3 toward kissat's 31. A conservative first step is 7 or 15 (single u8 widening, no storage change). The current 3 was chosen pre-kissat-port and is too narrow.

Distinction from SAT-playground-5b2.2.51: that bead proposed reducing MAX_USED_RECENTLY 3→2 to age clauses faster, which was rejected on the 11-instance suite (log/phase1/1.14x-max-used-recently-rejected-summary.md). That fix changes the wrong dimension. The semantic fix proposed here (bump-to-MAX on use) is independent of MAX value: it preserves recently-used clauses better regardless of MAX. Closing 5b2.2.51 in favor of this bead is reasonable once this lands.

Implementation notes:
- One-line change in mark_learned_clause_recent (src/main.rs:2255-2266) plus optional MAX_USED_RECENTLY constant widening at src/main.rs:142.
- record_current_mode_glue_use should remain on every use (separate concern; current bead 5b2.2.49 audits that path for percentile bias).
- Update tests in src/main.rs:7710-7712 (used_recently after learn) and any test using mark_learned_clause_recent (~lines 7855, 7861).

Tests:
  test_mark_recent_resets_to_max_used
  test_aged_then_reused_clause_recovers_full_protection
  test_max_used_widening_does_not_break_tier_classification

Acceptance criteria: cargo test pass, smoke pass, invariant smoke pass, profile bench with SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered measurably reduces learned_clauses_final on per-instance basis OR retains them longer when reused. Per the +3% promotion rule, kept clauses should improve PAR-2 by >3% on the 10-instance profiling suite under D_lbd_tiered config.

Larger project role: closes one of four kissat-port implementation gaps identified in the 2026-05-24 deep investigation. The other three are: trail reuse on restart (existing bead 5b2.2.35), fraction-based reducer deletion (new bead to be created), and restart margin alignment (existing bead 5b2.2.41 needs new-evidence note).

title: Preserve target_phase across focused/stable restarts; reject all-mode persistence
description:
Task class: solver-behavior algorithmic bug. Root cause for the lack of differentiation between SAT_PHASE=saved and SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved / best-then-target-then-saved across recent matrices.

Background: src/main.rs:4086-4103 `perform_restart_if_pending`:

    fn perform_restart_if_pending(&mut self) -> bool {
        if !self.restart_pending { return false; }
        self.restart_pending = false;
        self.reset_target_phase();           // <-- wipes target_phase, target_assigned = 0
        if self.current_level() == 0 { return false; }
        ...
        self.maybe_rephase_on_stable_restart();
        self.backtrack(0);
        true
    }

`reset_target_phase` (src/main.rs:3848-3854) sets `target_phase.fill(UNASSIGNED)` and `target_assigned = 0`. This fires on EVERY restart (legacy-luby, kissat-ema, reluctant).

`maybe_capture_phase_prefix` (src/main.rs:3882-3903) writes into `target_phase` only when `assigned > self.target_assigned`. With Luby restarts firing every ~32-256 conflicts in the early-search regime, target_phase is reset before it accumulates a meaningful trail prefix. The next capture starts from `target_assigned = 0` and refills only the trail seen in the new (shorter) restart cycle.

Consequence: `target_phase[var]` is UNASSIGNED most of the time when `pick_branch_phase` consults it (src/main.rs:3801-3805 PhasePolicy::TargetThenSaved, src/main.rs:3815-3820 PhasePolicy::BestThenTargetThenSaved). The phase lookup falls through to `saved_or_initial_phase`, making `TargetThenSaved` behave indistinguishably from `Saved`. The `stats.phase_target_used` counter is small relative to `stats.phase_saved_used` in default-style configurations, confirming this in artifacts.

Kissat behavior for comparison:
- target_phase is reset on rephase / mode switch / specific milestones, NOT on every restart.
- target_phase accumulates the best trail prefix seen across many restart cycles within a phase block.
- best_phase is reset even less often (only on rephase).

Current SOLVER11_STATE.md text "Target phases are preserved across focused/stable mode switches and are reset only by restart handling" describes the current implementation, but the design choice that target should be wiped on every restart appears to be unintentional (no design note in the closed bead SAT-playground-5b2.2.8 [1.5] justifies it).

Goal: stop resetting target_phase on every restart. Keep the reset on:
- mode switch (focused <-> stable) - already handled separately in 5b2.2.23/24
- rephase events - already happens via `apply_rephase`
- explicit milestones if any are added later

Implementation notes:
- Remove `self.reset_target_phase();` from `perform_restart_if_pending`.
- Verify `maybe_capture_phase_prefix` already handles the "grow watermark" case correctly (it does: `if assigned > self.target_assigned`).
- Verify `reset_target_phase` is still called from the intended paths. Grep: `git grep -n reset_target_phase solver/11-kissat-port/src/`. Expected callers post-fix: mode switch handling and rephase. If nothing else calls it, the function may become dead.
- For `best_phase`, audit similarly. `capture_best_phase` only runs when `search_mode_policy == FocusedStable` OR `phase_policy == BestThenTargetThenSaved`. Confirm best_phase is not also wiped on restart.

Side question (file as follow-up if needed): `maybe_capture_phase_prefix` is called AFTER `run_post_propagation_scheduling` in the search loop (src/main.rs:5858-5863). Even after this fix, the first no-conflict iteration after a pending restart captures phase on the (now-truncated) trail. Hoisting the capture call above `run_post_propagation_scheduling` would let it record the long pre-restart trail. Consider as part of this fix OR a sibling bead.

Tests:
- test_target_phase_survives_restart (set target_phase via maybe_capture_phase_prefix, fire a restart, assert target_phase still populated)
- test_target_assigned_monotone_across_restarts
- test_target_phase_reset_on_rephase (regression: ensure rephase still clears as intended)
- test_pick_branch_phase_uses_target_after_restart
- existing phase / restart tests must continue to pass

Benchmark gate: search-core + discriminating with SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved and SAT_PHASE=best-then-target-then-saved, both in single mode and focused-stable mode. Counters: phase_target_used, phase_best_used, phase_saved_used, phase_initial_used (after SAT-playground-5b2.2.43 lands), restarts, luby_restarts. Expected: phase_target_used materially larger relative to phase_saved_used. PAR-2: improvement on SAT-heavy and mixed classes; neutral on UNSAT-heavy.

Risk IDs: R5 (search trajectory), R6 (phase-saving invariant from 5b2.2.8). Rollback: restore reset_target_phase call in perform_restart_if_pending.
acceptance_criteria: Focused/stable target_phase is no longer wiped by perform_restart_if_pending; single-mode target policies keep restart-time target reset because all-mode persistence caused profile regressions; rephase resets target_phase to start a new phase block; regression tests cover focused/stable survival, single-mode reset, monotone focused/stable target_assigned, target branch selection after focused/stable restart, and rephase reset; cargo test, smoke checks, and 11-instance 300s profile comparison pass without status regression.

title: Fix phase_initial_used stat mislabeling in Legacy phase policy
description:
Task class: solver-behavior bug fix in telemetry.

Background: src/main.rs:3766 in pick_branch_phase for PhasePolicy::Legacy increments self.stats.phase_initial_used += 1 and then returns self.saved_phase[var]. The phase actually returned is the saved phase (which enqueue updates on every assignment at src/main.rs:3114-3116), not the initial phase from self.initial_phase(var) / self.original_phase. The counter is therefore mislabeled.

Default profile evidence: log/bench-11-kissat-port-2026-05-22-19-41-52/stats.jsonl shows phase_initial_used=908189 and phase_saved_used=0 for a default-profile run. Read literally, this says 'no saved phases were used,' which is wrong — every decision in default went through saved_phase[var]. Anyone diagnosing whether phase saving is doing anything in default reads the wrong signal.

Goal: emit accurate counters in the Legacy arm of pick_branch_phase. Two acceptable shapes:
- (preferred) introduce a phase_legacy_used counter for the Legacy path that returns saved_phase[var] without explicit initial-phase fallback, and stop incrementing phase_initial_used there. phase_saved_used remains the counter for explicit Saved (which falls back to initial_phase when UNASSIGNED).
- alternatively, drop the Legacy arm's stat bump and let only saved_or_initial_phase / target / best paths emit counters.

Implementation notes:
- src/main.rs:3763-3795 is the pick_branch_phase match; only the Legacy arm needs to change.
- If a new phase_legacy_used field is added, register it in src/stats.rs SolverStats and in any JSON_STATS / trace_full emission so artifacts pick it up.
- Update FEATURES.md or README if the counter list is documented.
- Add or update a test that exercises Legacy policy and asserts the counter shapes (no test currently catches the mislabel).

Tests:
- test_pick_branch_legacy_increments_correct_counter
- existing pick_branch_lit tests must continue to pass

Benchmark gate: none. Telemetry-only fix. Should land before the next 1.16 / 1.15 re-evaluation so future stats artifacts are interpretable.

Risk IDs: telemetry. Rollback: revert the counter rename.
acceptance_criteria: Default-profile stats.jsonl reflects saved-phase usage instead of attributing all 900k+ decisions to 'initial' usage. New counter (or restored interpretation) is documented. cargo test and smoke suite pass.

title: [1.4a] Glucose-style blocking restart from level EMA
description:
Task class: solver-behavior / performance-claim under epic [Phase 1 - Search, decision, phase, restart, and learned-clause logic].

Background: solver/11-kissat-port/src/main.rs already maintains restart_fast_level and restart_slow_level EMAs (fields at main.rs:961-963, updated in update_restart_ema at main.rs:3416-3417), but should_restart (main.rs:3420-3440) never reads them. The plan section 1.4 declares the fields but does not specify the consuming condition. Modern Glucose / Kissat block restarts when the recent trail/level EMA is significantly above its slow average, signalling a productive SAT prefix; suppressing the restart preserves that prefix.

Goal: extend RestartPolicy::KissatEma should_restart so that when restart_fast_level / restart_slow_level exceeds a blocking margin (Glucose uses ~1.4; Kissat tunes by mode), the restart is suppressed even if the LBD condition fires. Record a stats counter for blocked restarts. Keep behavior unchanged when SAT_RESTART != kissat-ema. Wire a SAT_RESTART_BLOCK_MARGIN (or equivalent) through SolverConfig + CONFIG_SCHEMA per the plan 0.3 contract.

Implementation notes:
- Add restart_blocking_margin to SolverConfig with default in the Glucose/Kissat range (~1.4) and a corresponding SAT_RESTART_BLOCK_MARGIN env var.
- Extend should_restart to consult fast_level vs slow_level once both EMAs are initialized.
- Add a stats counter (e.g. restarts_blocked_by_level) and surface it in trace_full / JSON_STATS.
- Reset level EMAs alongside lbd EMAs on focused-mode entry (see fix 5b2.2.24) for consistency.

Tests:
- test_blocking_restart_suppresses_when_level_high
- test_blocking_restart_no_effect_when_level_low
- test_blocking_restart_uninitialized_emas_do_not_suppress
- test_blocking_restart_disabled_for_legacy_luby_and_reluctant
- test_blocking_restart_counter_increments_on_suppression

Benchmark gate: search-core and discriminating with SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_RESTART=kissat-ema, paired vs current build. Expected wins on SAT-heavy / phase-saving instances (battleship, Timetable, DLTM_twitter); watch for UNSAT regressions and verify learned-clause LBD distribution did not degrade.

Acceptance:
- Counters move in expected direction (some suppressed restarts) without lost solved instances in regression-guards.
- No proof/model failures on smoke + invariant + proof-on UNSAT smoke.
- compare_bench.py shows no significant PAR-2 regression; promote behind the existing kissat-ema flag.

Risk IDs: same restart-trajectory risk family as 5b2.2.7. Rollback note required if rejected.

title: Fix: high-LBD learned clauses get lower initial used_recently than Kissat
description:
In solver 11's learn path (~main.rs:1990), newly learned clauses are initialized with used_recently based on their tier:
  - LBD <= TIER2_MAX_GLUE (6): used_recently = 3
  - LBD > 6 (tier3): used_recently = 1

Kissat always sets c->used = MAX_USED (value 31, a 5-bit field saturating at 31) at learn.c:110, regardless of the clause's glue. This gives every newly learned clause maximum initial protection from deletion regardless of quality.

The used counter is decremented during reduce_db passes. Starting high-LBD clauses at used_recently=1 instead of the maximum means they can be collected after the very next reduce_db, before they have had a chance to be used. This makes the tier3 clause retention policy more aggressive than Kissat's and may cause useful clauses to be deleted prematurely.

Implementation:
1. In the learn/add_learned_clause path, initialize used_recently to the same maximum value (e.g. 3 or whatever the u8 MAX_USED analog is) regardless of the clause's LBD tier.
2. Let the reduce_db decrement logic determine when the clause is evictable, not the initial value.
3. If desired, keep a lower initial value ONLY for clauses whose LBD exceeds a very high threshold (e.g. > 20), but align first with Kissat's uniform initialization and measure the effect.
notes: s11-01 progress 2026-05-22: Selected as next logical Phase 1 blocker after bv triage. This is the narrowest P2 search-policy bug before larger LBD-tier/reduce scheduling work: newly learned high-LBD clauses currently start with less deletion protection than Kissat's MAX_USED initialization, which can bias later reduce_db experiments and prematurely delete clauses before they have a chance to prove useful. Implementation plan: align initial used_recently for every learned clause with the solver's MAX_USED_RECENTLY analog, update focused tests/docs, run cargo tests, smoke/invariant checks, and profile benchmark.
close_reason: Implemented uniform learned-clause initial used_recently retention. initialize_learnt_lbd now sets every newly learned clause to MAX_USED_RECENTLY regardless of LBD tier, matching Kissat's maximum initial learned-clause used counter semantics while leaving tier classification, reduce-DB aging, and reason-use marking unchanged. Added test_learned_clause_initial_used_recently_is_max_for_all_lbd_tiers covering tier1/tier2/tier3 initialization, updated README, SOLVER11_STATE, and plan text to avoid stale tier3=1 guidance, and recorded artifacts in log/1.14-learned-used-init/summary.md. Fresh-eyes review checked learn path, metadata side table, reduce-DB candidate collection/aging, docs, and plan text. title: Fix: kissat_update_scores not called when entering stable mode
description:
Kissat calls kissat_update_scores (bump.c:114-120) when switching TO stable mode in mode.c:183. This refreshes the VSIDS heap so that variable scores accumulated during focused mode are correctly reflected in the heap order before stable mode begins making decisions.

Solver 11's maybe_switch_search_mode() (~main.rs:3340) handles mode transitions but only resets the VMTF search pointer for the focused-to-stable direction. It does NOT rebuild or reschedule the VSIDS heap. As a result, the stable-mode heap may have stale ordering at mode entry, causing early stable-mode decisions to be suboptimal.

Implementation:
1. Identify the stable mode entry branch in maybe_switch_search_mode.
2. After setting the mode to stable, call a heap-rescore or reschedule function equivalent to kissat_update_scores: iterate over unassigned variables and re-insert them into the VSIDS heap with their current bump scores.
3. Alternatively, mark the heap as dirty and lazily rebuild on the next pick_branch_lit call in stable mode.

This is a correctness/quality issue for the focused -> stable transition, not just a micro-optimization. Kissat reference: mode.c:183, bump.c:114-120.
notes: s11-01 progress 2026-05-22: Selected after bd ready and bv triage/plan. Ignored container epics and chose the ready P2 focused/stable behavior blocker. Rationale: stable-mode decisions depend on the VSIDS heap, while focused-mode VMTF can let VSIDS scores change without guaranteeing a clean stable-entry heap order. Fixing this narrow mode-transition issue should precede larger reduce_db schedule, dynamic tier, and search-tick mode-gating work. Plan: add a Kissat-style stable-entry heap refresh/rebuild, cover stale-heap behavior with a unit test, update current-state docs, run focused mode tests, full unit/smoke/invariant checks, an advanced focused/VMTF smoke, and the default profile benchmark.
close_reason: Implemented stable-entry VSIDS heap refresh for focused/stable mode. maybe_switch_search_mode now rebuilds the branch heap from current variable activities whenever the new mode is Stable, matching the role of Kissat's update_scores before stable decisions resume. Focused-entry behavior remains unchanged: LBD EMA averages reset and VMTF search cursor resets when entering Focused. Added test_mode_switch_to_stable_refreshes_vsids_heap_scores to simulate stale heap ordering after focused-mode score changes and verify stable mode picks the refreshed top variable. Updated README, SOLVER11_STATE, and plan text. Fresh-eyes review covered mode-switch reachability, VMTF pick path, VSIDS pick path, heap rebuild filtering, backtrack reinsertion, default-mode reachability, and docs; no additional implementation bugs found. Validation: cargo fmt --check passed; new regression test passed; cargo test mode_switch passed 6/6; cargo test heap passed 8/8; full cargo test passed 252/252; standard smoke passed 9/9; invariant smoke passed 9/9; focused/stable VMTF smoke passed 9/9; advanced focused/VMTF smoke passed 9/9. Default profile first run solved 11/11 PAR-2 642.264; rerun solved 11/11 PAR-2 627.429, better than the immediate previous default profile 631.833, confirming no default-profile regression. Artifacts recorded in log/1.14-stable-heap-refresh/summary.md.

title: Fix: mode switching uses conflict count for both modes; stable should gate on search ticks
description:
Kissat uses two different limits for mode switching (mode.c):
- Focused → stable: CONFLICTS >= limits.mode.conflicts, where the interval is nlogpow(count/2, 4) * modeint (nlogpow is n * 4th-power of log2(n)). This grows super-linearly with mode count.
- Stable → focused: search_ticks >= limits.mode.ticks, where delta_ticks is the tick count from the previous stable phase. Stable mode is sized by actual propagation work, not conflict count.

Solver 11 (maybe_switch_search_mode, main.rs:3329) uses conflicts for both modes with sqrt(mode_switches + 1) * scale * init_conflicts scaling. This:
1. Does not use search ticks for the stable-mode gate (missing propagation-work accounting).
2. Uses sqrt scaling instead of Kissat's nlogpow(count, 4) for the focused-mode gate. nlogpow grows much faster, giving focused mode longer intervals as search progresses.
3. Does not call any equivalent of kissat_init_averages when switching modes (mode.c calls this to reset all averages on every switch, not just the EMA restart values handled by bead 5b2.2.24).

Required changes:
1. Add search_ticks counter incremented at each literal visit in propagation (in the watcher scan inner loop). Ticks are the mechanism Kissat uses to measure inprocessing and mode work.
2. Use search_ticks as the stable-mode gate instead of conflicts.
3. Change focused-mode interval formula to nlogpow(focused_mode_count, 4) * base_interval.
4. On every mode switch, reset all mode-sensitive averages (not just EMA restart values).

Note: add SAT_MODE_USE_TICKS=on config flag as an opt-in until validated, so the change does not silently alter default behavior before benchmarking.
notes:
Implemented 2026-05-22 in solver/11-kissat-port. Added SAT_MODE_USE_TICKS=on as an opt-in config/feature flag. Default behavior is preserved: mode tick accounting is off unless the flag is enabled, and propagation dispatch uses const generics so default watcher scans do not pay a per-watcher runtime flag check. Added SolverStats.search_ticks and JSON/trace_full output. In tick mode, propagation records search_ticks for binary implication edges, watcher visits, and long-clause replacement literal visits during normal search only; temporary assumptions do not tick. Focused/stable mode switching now matches the Kissat shape behind the flag: focused mode still switches by conflicts, focused intervals use Kissat nlogpown(count, 4) * mode_init_conflicts with log10(count + 9), stable mode switches by search_ticks using the previous mode's tick delta, and all restart EMAs (LBD and level, fast and slow) reset on every tick-mode mode switch. Fresh-eyes review found and fixed an integration bug where the stable tick gate was only checked after conflicts; the no-conflict scheduling path now calls maybe_switch_search_mode for tick mode before restart/decision work, with a regression test. Updated CONFIG_SCHEMA.csv, FEATURES.csv, FEATURES.md, README.md, and SOLVER11_STATE.md. Older 624-628 baselines show the expected single-run spread dominated by sudoku variance and no lost solved instances.
Post-close opt-in candidate profile (2026-05-22): ran SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_SEARCH_MODE=focused-stable SAT_MODE_USE_TICKS=on bash tools/bench.sh -d benchmarks/profiling solver/11-kissat-port at 300s timeout. title: Fix: LBD-tiered reduce_db trigger uses literal/clause budget, not SQRT-scaled conflict limit
description:
Kissat fires reduce_db when CONFLICTS >= limits.reduce.conflicts, then schedules the NEXT reduce at current_conflicts + SQRT(reductions) * base_interval (reduce.c:193: UPDATE_CONFLICT_LIMIT(reduce, reductions, SQRT, false)). The initial interval is ~1000 conflicts, growing as sqrt(k) after k reductions.

Solver 11's LBD-tiered path uses two triggers (should_reduce_db, main.rs:3924):
  live_learned_clause_count - trail.len() >= reduce_db_limit   (clause-count based)
  OR learned_literals > learned_lit_budget                       (literal-count based)

The literal-count budget also scales with reductions (refresh_learned_lit_budgets uses sqrt(reduction_count)), but the clause-count trigger fires first and does not scale properly with the LBD-tiered policy. The clause-count path is a MiniSat-legacy artifact that interacts poorly with the tiered policy: as tier3 clauses accumulate, live_learned_clause_count grows faster than the trail, firing reduce every 5-10 conflicts.

Fix: for ReducePolicy::LbdTiered, replace the primary trigger with a conflict-count limit that starts at reduceinit (e.g. 1000) and grows as SQRT(reduce_db_calls) * base_interval. Keep the hard literal limit as an emergency overflow guard only. Add SAT_REDUCE_INIT config key for the base interval.

This eliminates the cascading GC that produces 12,025 reductions in 60s on mp1 (1 per 6 conflicts). Kissat gets 26 reductions for the same instance on a SQRT-scaled schedule.
notes: Completion note 2026-05-22: Implemented LBD-tiered reduce_db scheduling as a conflict-count schedule, not legacy learned-clause/literal pressure. For SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered, reduce_db_limit now means the next absolute conflict count. Defaults: first reduction at 1000 conflicts; reschedule after each reduction to current_conflicts + sqrt(reduce_db_calls) * SAT_REDUCE_DB_INTERVAL/default 1000. SAT_REDUCE_DB_INIT and SAT_REDUCE_DB_INTERVAL remain the existing config knobs; no duplicate SAT_REDUCE_INIT was added. Legacy reduction behavior keeps its learned-clause-count trigger and MiniSat-style budget adjustment. The normal learned_lit_budget is now only the deletion target inside a scheduled LBD-tiered reduce, not a trigger. The hard learned-literal guard remains an emergency trigger but now scales as max(64 * learned_lit_budget, 64 * original_literals), refreshed after initial clause load and after preprocessing, so it does not fire continuously on large formulas. Fresh-eyes review caught and fixed an initial bug where hard budget was too low: mp1 direct trace initially still did 10809 reductions by 590k conflicts; after the final guard fix the same 60s trace ended at 580k conflicts with 91 reductions, matching the intended SQRT schedule shape. title: Fix: LBD-tiered reduction uses static tier thresholds; needs per-mode histogram
description:
Solver 11 uses hardcoded TIER1_MAX_GLUE=2 and TIER2_MAX_GLUE=6 (main.rs:68-69). Kissat computes tier limits dynamically from a per-mode glue usage histogram (tiers.c). The histogram tracks how often clauses at each glue level are accessed since the last retier; tier1 is set to cover the top 50% of used clauses by frequency (TIER1RELATIVE=0.5) and tier2 covers the top 90% (TIER2RELATIVE=0.9, options.h:152-154).

With avg_lbd=50+ in focused/stable mode, static tier1=2 and tier2=6 means virtually all learned clauses are tier3, which triggers constant GC. Dynamic tiers would push the thresholds up to match the actual distribution (e.g., tier1~25, tier2~70 on mp1), keeping the best-used clauses protected.

Second gap: Kissat decrements c->used on EVERY reduce pass for every redundant clause (reduce.c:71: 'if (used) c->used = used - 1'), including those NOT being deleted. This slowly ages clauses off their tier protection. Solver 11 never decrements used; clauses with used_recently=true stay protected indefinitely.

Required changes:
1. Add per-mode glue usage histogram: stats.focused_glue_used[glue] and stats.stable_glue_used[glue] incremented at deduce time (in add_analyzed_clause_from_slice / mark_learned_clause_recent).
2. Implement compute_tier_limits() that reads the histogram for current mode and computes 50th/90th percentile thresholds. Call it at the start of reduce_db_lbd_tiered().
3. In the reduce pass, decrement used counter for all scanned redundant clauses (not just those being deleted).

Evidence: mp1 focused/VMTF 60s run, log/1.12a/reretest-300-focused-vmtf: reductions=12025, avg_lbd=50.4. Kissat on same instance: reductions=26. The 462x difference in GC frequency is primarily caused by static tier thresholds at 2/6 vs a dynamic ~25/70.

Audit note 2026-05-22 (fresh-eyes Phase 1 pass): while reviewing this bead, also verify the candidate-ordering correctness item from plan 1.3 - "Candidate ordering should use integer keys, not float comparisons" via ReduceCand { lbd, size, used_recently, activity_rank }. If reduce_db_lbd_tiered (src/main.rs:4562) still sorts by raw f64 activity for tie-breaking, the planned integer-key invariant has not landed yet. Cheap to verify alongside the per-mode-histogram work and worth a sub-fix so 5b2.2.31 lands in the planned shape.
Audit note 2026-05-22 (sub-fix from fresh-eyes pass): also evaluate the TIER1_MAX_GLUE constant. solver/11-kissat-port/src/main.rs:68 sets TIER1_MAX_GLUE=2 statically. Combined with the recent fix (commit 6849f82) that initializes used_recently=MAX for every tier, the tier1/tier3 protection asymmetry is carried entirely by size/used_recently keys in ReduceCand. Modern Kissat moves the tier1 boundary upward during stable mode rather than holding it at 2. When implementing per-mode histograms here, also try a small sweep: tier1 in {2, 3} x mode in {focused, stable} on search-core + discriminating, with per-mode learned-LBD histograms attached to the writeup. Record rejected variants with counters so the next loop does not retry blindly.

title: Fix: EMA restart state not reset when entering focused mode
description:
In maybe_switch_search_mode() (main.rs:3329), the fast/slow LBD EMA values (restart_fast_lbd, restart_slow_lbd) are not reset when switching modes. Kissat resets EMA windows on mode transitions so each mode phase starts with a clean restart calibration.

When entering focused mode from a stable phase that had high average LBD (e.g., 50+), the slow EMA is calibrated to stable-mode statistics. The EMA-based restart then fires at the wrong rate in the new focused phase because the baseline is wrong.

Evidence from mp1 focused/VMTF run (log/1.12a/reretest-300-focused-vmtf): glucose_restarts=329, reluctant_restarts=5497. The tiny number of glucose restarts (329) despite many focused-mode decisions suggests the EMA is calibrated to a high-LBD baseline from stable mode and slow to trigger in focused mode, while reluctant restarts (stable mode) dominate.

Fix: when switching to focused mode, call restart_fast_lbd.reset() and restart_slow_lbd.reset() (set initialized=false, value=0.0) so focused mode starts its EMA from scratch. Do not reset on switch to stable because stable uses reluctant restarts, not EMA. Add a test confirming EMA state is clean after a focused-mode switch.

Reference: Kissat src/restart.c — resetema() called from mode.c switchmode() on entering focused mode.

Added test_mode_switch_resets_lbd_ema_only_when_entering_focused covering both sides of the transition. Updated README and SOLVER11_STATE docs. title: Fix: target_phase incorrectly cleared on focused/stable mode switches
description:
In maybe_switch_search_mode() (main.rs:3348), reset_target_phase() is called on every mode switch. Kissat does NOT do this — target phase accumulates continuously across mode switches and is only cleared on restarts (perform_restart_if_pending, main.rs:3714).

Clearing target_phase on mode switch discards all phase information accumulated during the preceding focused epoch whenever the solver transitions to stable mode. This degrades SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved and best-then-target-then-saved policies, which are the default for focused/stable mode.

Evidence: the 1.12a retest (log/1.12a/summary.md) shows focused/VMTF on mp1 with phase_save_target=707,779 (many target captures), but the solver fails to use them effectively because they get cleared on every mode switch (mode_switches=10 in 60s).

Fix: remove reset_target_phase() from maybe_switch_search_mode(). Verify target_phase is still cleared on restarts only. Add a test that confirms target_phase is preserved across a mode switch.

Reference: Kissat src/phases.c — targetresetphases() is only called from restart.c, never from mode.c.

title: [0.13] Repair trace and diagnostic config flag parsing
description:
Background:
While debugging the Section 0 overhead, an integration bug surfaced: solver 11's CONFIG_SCHEMA.csv and allowed_env_vars list include SAT_TRACE_PROOF, SAT_TRACE_PREPROCESS, SAT_TRACE_PREPROCESS_DETAILS, and SAT_TRACE_SEARCH_INTERVAL, but SolverConfig::apply_env_overrides currently parses SAT_TRACE_FULL and SAT_CHECK_INVARIANTS while skipping the individual trace flags. A direct run with SAT_TRACE_SEARCH_INTERVAL=1000000000 produced no solver 11 search summary, while solver 10 emitted the expected final search counters.

Goal and intent:
Make the trace/diagnostic flags documented by Section 0 actually work. These flags are needed to debug overhead, compare search trajectories, and support later optimization work without ad hoc code edits.

Implementation guidance:
- Parse SAT_TRACE_PROOF, SAT_TRACE_PREPROCESS, SAT_TRACE_PREPROCESS_DETAILS, and SAT_TRACE_SEARCH_INTERVAL in SolverConfig::apply_env_overrides.
- Ensure replay override behavior remains consistent with the schema and allowed_env_vars.
- Add tests that construct env maps and assert the corresponding SolverConfig fields are set.
- Add a small integration-style test or documented command proving SAT_TRACE_SEARCH_INTERVAL causes solver 11 to emit final search counters.
- Ensure SAT_TRACE_FULL still implies preprocess and detail tracing as intended.

Constraints and considerations:
- This is not the main performance fix, but it enables reliable debugging and overhead gates.
- Avoid increasing default runtime overhead; trace flags must remain disabled by default.
- Keep schema, README, validator, and generated artifacts consistent.

Testing expectations:
- cargo test must cover env parsing.
- A direct smoke command with SAT_TRACE_SEARCH_INTERVAL set should show a final `c search done ...` line.
- Run ci_solver11_fast after the fix.

How this serves the larger project goal:
Future Phase 1 and Phase 2 work needs trustworthy diagnostics. Trace flags that appear in the config contract but do not execute create false confidence and make regression analysis slower.

title: [0.11] Add zero-cost default limit-check fast path
description:
Background:
Section 0 added structured runtime limits and UNKNOWN contract behavior. The implementation currently calls Solver::limit_hit(config, solve_start, proof_log) at several search/preprocess checkpoints. Even when every limit option is unset, this helper walks a chain of optional checks, including counters, wall-clock, RSS, learned-literal, binary-clause, extension-byte, and proof-byte limit cases. This is not the dominant overhead compared with always-on propagation diagnostics, but it is avoidable default-path work.

Goal and intent:
Keep the Section 0 limit contract while making the no-limits default path as close to zero-cost as practical. Normal competition-style runs without SAT_LIMIT_* should not pay a measurable tax for dormant limit machinery.

Implementation guidance:
- Add a precomputed limits_enabled / active_limit_mask field to SolverConfig or a small RuntimeLimits helper.
- At each solve/search checkpoint, skip limit_hit entirely when no limits are active.
- Where possible, split cheap always-needed solve checks from expensive wall/RSS/proof-byte checks.
- Preserve precise UNKNOWN reasons and proof-temp cleanup when limits are active.
- Avoid checking max_rss_mb or Instant::elapsed unless the corresponding limit is set.

Constraints and considerations:
- Do not weaken limit semantics introduced in 0.8.
- Do not remove proof-byte/extension-byte/binary-clause limit support.
- The change should compose with the hot stats overhead fix from 0.10.

Testing expectations:
- Unit tests for active/inactive limit mask behavior.
- Existing output-contract UNKNOWN limit tests must still pass.
- Direct run with SAT_LIMIT_TICKS=0 must still return structured UNKNOWN and remove temp proof artifacts.
- Run cargo fmt, cargo test, SAT_STATS_JSON=on cargo test, smoke, invariant smoke, ci_solver11_fast.
- Include repeated interleaved timing evidence before/after or explain why 0.10 dominates the remaining delta.

How this serves the larger project goal:
Resource limits are necessary for safe automation, but default performance baselines must reflect solver quality, not dormant safety checks. This bead removes another Section 0 infrastructure tax before Phase 1 performance work begins.
acceptance_criteria: When no SAT_LIMIT_* variables are set, solver 11 avoids the full limit-hit option chain in search/preprocess hot checkpoints; all existing UNKNOWN/limit tests still pass; repeated interleaved overhead data is recorded; cargo test, smoke, invariant smoke, and ci_solver11_fast pass.

Plan is to precompute whether any runtime/resource limits are active and skip the full limit_hit option chain at search/preprocess checkpoints when the default no-limit configuration is used, without changing UNKNOWN semantics when a limit is active.
