title: Decouple SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved from EMA restart in default kissat configurations
description:
Task class: configuration / default-bundle policy. Prevents future kissat-feature combinations from including SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved when SAT_RESTART=kissat-ema is active.

Background: deeper investigation 2026-05-24 (log/kissat-investigation-2026-05-23-broad/DEEPER_FINDINGS.md, Phase 3 sweep table) tested three configurations that bundle target-phase with EMA restart or with lbd-tiered:
- H5 (C_lbd_ema + SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved)
- H6 (D_lbd_tiered + SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved)
- H7 (E_lbd_ema_tiered + SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved)

All three regress 6s299b685_Iter30 by 7-8× (146s / 124s / 145s vs A_default 17s). The HWMCC hardware-verification instance solves in 3,764 conflicts under baseline / B / C / D, but jumps to 7,000-32,000 conflicts under any target-phase variant. The target-phase heuristic (saves an assignment between restarts) gives the wrong polarity on this instance type, causing wasted re-search.

Other Iter30 regressions confirming the bundle is the issue:
- F_full_kissat (E + target-phase + chrono): Iter30 127s
- G_focused_stable (uses best-then-target-then-saved): Iter30 94s

By contrast, configs that omit target-phase keep Iter30 in 16-18s range:
- C_lbd_ema: 18.2s
- D_lbd_tiered: 17.1s
- E_lbd_ema_tiered: 18.1s
- H1 (C + block_margin): 16.3s
- H4 (E + block_margin): 17.4s

Distinction from SAT-playground-5b2.2.45: that bead documents how SAT_PHASE behaves under SAT_SEARCH_MODE=focused-stable mode. This bead is about not BUNDLING target-phase with EMA restart in default kissat-feature configs (independent of focused-stable mode).

Implementation notes:
- Today SAT_PHASE is opt-in (default Legacy). The bundling issue arises when a kissat-style 'default kissat profile' is constructed in config.rs and includes target-phase + kissat-ema together.
- Either: (a) keep SAT_PHASE=legacy as the kissat-feature default when EMA is on, and require explicit user opt-in for target-phase; or (b) detect HWMCC-style instances and skip target-phase saving for them; or (c) document this combination in CONFIG_SCHEMA.csv as 'do not combine with kissat-ema unless instance is known to benefit from saved-phase' and never make it default.
- The simplest minimum-disruption path is (a): never include SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved or best-then-target-then-saved in the same default profile as SAT_RESTART=kissat-ema.

Tests:
  test_default_kissat_profile_does_not_combine_target_phase_with_ema
  test_target_phase_remains_opt_in_when_ema_active

Acceptance criteria: cargo test pass, smoke pass, invariant smoke pass. Verify in source review (config.rs, profile defaults) that no compound profile includes both phase=target-then-saved and restart=kissat-ema by default. Add a CONFIG_SCHEMA.csv note documenting the rationale.

Larger project role: prevents the F_full_kissat-style 7-8× Iter30 regression from appearing in future default bundles. This is a guardrail, not an algorithmic change. Related to 5b2.2.45 (which documents phase override semantics inside focused-stable mode); this bead is about default-bundle hygiene more broadly.
notes: s11-02 start 2026-05-24: selected after closing 5b2.2.45 because it is the adjacent Phase 1 config-contract guardrail. Plan: inspect SolverProfile/ProfileAxes defaults and config docs, add a test that no default/profile bundle combines SAT_RESTART=kissat-ema with target-phase policies, document CONFIG_SCHEMA rationale if needed, then run cargo tests/smoke.
close_reason: s11-02 completed 2026-05-24: added guardrail tests so built-in profiles cannot silently bundle SAT_RESTART=kissat-ema with target-phase policies, while explicit SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved remains allowed when EMA is active. Documented rationale in README and CONFIG_SCHEMA.csv. Validation: cargo test 318 passed, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, default smoke 9/9, SAT_CHECK_INVARIANTS=on SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_RESTART=kissat-ema SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved smoke 9/9, git diff --check.

title: Eliminate per-call Vec<bool> allocation in reduce_db_lbd_tiered
description:
Task class: solver-behavior performance bug. Companion to SAT-playground-5b2.2.47 (LBD allocation) and SAT-playground-5b2.2.18.11 (rebuild_reason_pinset scratch reuse).

Background: src/main.rs:5033-5085 `reduce_db_lbd_tiered` allocates a `Vec<bool>` of size `self.arena.len()` on every reduce-DB call:

    let mut delete_clause = vec![false; self.arena.len()];

The arena grows monotonically with original + learned + (later GC'd) clause slots. On medium-suite instances we see arena sizes in the millions of slots; on competition instances this can be tens of millions. Each LBD-tiered reduce currently pays:

1. `vec![false; arena.len()]` allocation + zero-fill.
2. Walk of `candidates` (post-sort) to mark `delete_clause[cand.clause_idx] = true`.
3. Walk of `learned_clause_ids` (size O(live learned)) to gate eviction by `delete_clause[clause_idx]`.
4. Free.

Step 1 touches the entire arena footprint (a multi-MB memset) even though only the small set of marked candidates needs to be looked up. The current schedule fires every sqrt(reduce_db_calls)*interval conflicts, so on long runs the cumulative cost is significant.

This bead violates plan section 2 invariant "propagation, conflict analysis, decision selection, and reduce-db candidate scans do not allocate in steady state" (called out in 5b2.2.18.11 description). 5b2.2.18.11 covers `rebuild_reason_pinset` but not this site.

Goal: replace the per-call `Vec<bool>` with a sparse marker. Two reasonable shapes:

Option 1 (preferred): keep candidates already sorted by eviction priority, then walk them once to mark using a u64 generation stamp on a Solver scratch vector. The scratch is allocated once at solver construction, sized to `arena.capacity()`, and grown only on arena reallocation. Reset is O(1) (bump generation), like the existing `lbd_stamp` pattern.

    self.reduce_delete_gen = self.reduce_delete_gen.wrapping_add(1).max(1);
    if self.reduce_delete_gen == 0 { self.reduce_delete_mark.fill(0); self.reduce_delete_gen = 1; }
    // mark survivors during the candidate walk:
    for cand in candidates { ... self.reduce_delete_mark[cand.clause_idx] = self.reduce_delete_gen; ... }
    // then walk learned_clause_ids and check membership by gen:
    if self.reduce_delete_mark[clause_idx] == self.reduce_delete_gen { ... evict ... }

Option 2: sort `candidates` by `clause_idx` after the LBD-priority sort, then do a merge-join with `learned_clause_ids` (also sorted by clause_idx normally) to avoid the membership marker entirely. More invasive.

Implementation notes:
- The scratch vector needs to be grown to `arena.len()` when arena grows beyond previous capacity. Cheapest place to check is at the start of `reduce_db_lbd_tiered`.
- Make sure `garbage_collect` either invalidates the scratch (zero-fill or bump generation) since clause indices reloc.
- Same scratch could be reused by `reduce_db_legacy_activity` if that path is changed similarly, but legacy uses in-place sort + filter and does not allocate this Vec, so it's out of scope for this bead.

Tests:
- test_reduce_db_lbd_tiered_no_per_call_allocation (tracking allocator, force several reduces in succession)
- test_reduce_delete_marker_handles_arena_growth (extend arena between reduces)
- test_reduce_delete_marker_generation_wraparound (bump generation past u64::MAX trigger via wrapping_add)
- existing reduce-DB-lbd-tiered tests must pass unchanged (learned_kept_tier1/2/3 counters, evicted clauses)

Benchmark gate: search-core + discriminating with SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered. Counters: reduce_db_calls, learned_collected, GC counters. perf stat on a run with many reduce_db_calls (REGRandom K4 with capped timeout, or a synthetic deep run) — expect the allocator pressure proxy and dTLB miss count to drop. Expected PAR-2: neutral-to-improved (no semantic change; pure overhead removal).

Risk IDs: R10 (allocation invariant), R3 (learned-clause correctness). Rollback: restore the per-call Vec<bool>.
acceptance_criteria: reduce_db_lbd_tiered no longer allocates a Vec<bool> sized to arena.len() per call; tracking-allocator test confirms zero per-call allocation; cargo test, smoke, and lbd-tiered profile benchmark all pass without regression.
notes:
Identified during 2026-05-23 fresh-eyes solver 11 review (second pass). Companion to SAT-playground-5b2.2.47 (compute_lbd) and SAT-playground-5b2.2.18.11 (rebuild_reason_pinset). Together these three sites are the dominant per-reduce-DB allocation cost.
s11-02: Claimed as the companion Phase 1 allocation fix after SAT-playground-5b2.2.47. Rationale: .47 removed the LBD clause Vec allocation and passed same-mode profile before/after, but the lbd-tiered reason-update mode still times out mp1 versus default-off. This bead targets the next ready allocation hotspot in the same reduce/LBD throughput group.
close_reason: s11-02 implemented the reduce-DB allocation fix: reduce_db_lbd_tiered now uses persistent generation-stamped delete marks, reuses reduce_candidates, and compacts learned_clause_ids in place instead of allocating a dense delete vector and rebuilding the learned list each pass. Tests cover marker arena growth, generation wraparound, and zero allocations across repeated no-candidate reduce passes when the marker is reused. Validation: cargo fmt --check; cargo test 299/299; default smoke 9/9; invariant smoke 9/9; SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_LBD_UPDATE_REASONS=on SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered smoke 9/9; same with SAT_LBD_UPDATE_PROP_REASONS=on smoke 9/9. Profile after .47 to after .47+.48: log/phase1/1.14r-lbd-clause-scratch-profile-after 10/11 PAR-2 1122.772 -> log/phase1/1.14s-lbd-reduce-scratch-profile-after 10/11 PAR-2 1121.274, no status changes. Original before .47 to final combined patch: 1123.123 -> 1121.274, no status changes. The feature mode remains non-promotable versus default-off because mp1 still times out.

title: Re-run 1.16 focused/stable matrix after throughput subset (1.14r/s/u/w/aa) lands
description:
Task class: performance-claim, blocks [1.15] Phase 1 gate. Successor to closed 5b2.2.30 [1.16] triage.

Background: the 2026-05-23 close of 5b2.2.30 concluded the residual focused/stable + VMTF gap is 'search-trajectory/inprocessing-dependent' and deferred promotion to Phase 2 vivification. The accompanying stats (log/phase1/1.16-matrix/summary.md) show propagations/s dropped from 4,649,873 (default) to 1,222,290 (focused/VMTF guard100) — a 74% throughput regression that is not explained by search trajectory.

A 4× propagation-throughput drop is consistent with the per-call overhead the open 5b2.2.18.* throughput subtasks already identify: the accounting_mode branch in propagate_impl (1.14s), per-watcher search_ticks RMW (1.14u), per-reason LearnedMeta lookups (1.14r/1.14w), and the per-variable accounting/search_mode branch in bump_analyzed_variable_activity (1.14aa). The 1.16 matrix ran *before* any of those landed, so the comparison was 'high-overhead focused/stable' vs 'low-overhead default,' not 'equal-overhead focused/stable' vs 'equal-overhead default.'

Goal: re-run the 1.16 matrix exactly as before, after the throughput subset lands. If the focused/VMTF aggregate PAR-2 movement holds without throughput penalty, and mp1 is recovered or its loss is much smaller, the deferred verdict changes. If the gap persists, the original 'search-trajectory/inprocessing-dependent' conclusion gets stronger evidence.

Required prior work (all open):
- 5b2.2.18.5 [1.14s] Hoist accounting_mode branch out of propagation hot path via TEMP const generic
- 5b2.2.18.7 [1.14u] Batch search_ticks accumulation in propagation hot loop
- 5b2.2.18.4 [1.14r] LearnedMeta hot/cold split
- 5b2.2.18.9 [1.14w] Fuse LearnedMeta lookups and glue histogram in conflict-analysis hot path
- 5b2.2.18.13 [1.14aa] Hoist accounting_mode / search_mode branches out of bump_analyzed_variable_activity

Also recommended before the re-run (telemetry hygiene; do not block on these if scheduling pressure is high):
- 5b2.2.43 Fix phase_initial_used stat mislabeling — makes the next stats.jsonl interpretable
- 5b2.2.18.15 Remove dead should_restart — silences a build warning that shows up in every benchmark build.log

Methodology:
- Re-use the exact matrix from log/phase1/1.16-matrix/summary.md: profile and search-core suites at 300s / 16384 MB, SAT_STATS_JSON=on SAT_TRACE_FULL=on.
- Rows: default baseline; focused/VMTF guard100; focused/VMTF guard50; focused/stable VSIDS guard100; single kissat-EMA + lbd-tiered.
- Report the same diagnostic table (Conflicts/s, Propagations/s, Reductions, Glucose restarts, Reluctant restarts, Focused/Stable avg LBD).
- Side-by-side comparison vs the 2026-05-23 1.16 matrix.

Promotion decision rule (unchanged from 5b2.2.30):
- focused/VMTF must come within 20% of default PAR-2 on search-core *and* not lose any default-solved row to qualify for default-profile promotion.
- focused/stable VSIDS qualifies on the same criterion if focused/VMTF does not.
- single kissat-EMA + lbd-tiered qualifies under the same rule.

Measurement-asymmetry note: 5b2.2.30's matrix ran focused/stable rows with MODE_TICKS=true and the kissat-ema accounting paths active, while default ran with neither. Some of the observed propagations/s gap is the diagnostic asymmetry, not the feature. After the throughput subset lands, the gap should narrow on this axis even without algorithmic change. The re-run interprets both effects.

Tests:
- no new tests; this is a benchmark-driven evaluation.

Benchmark gate: profile (11 instances) + search-core (9 instances), 300s / 16384 MB, full diagnostics. Required artifacts: log/phase1/1.16-rerun/*/{results.csv, stats.jsonl, summary.log, errors.log, warnings.log} for each matrix row; an updated log/phase1/1.16-rerun/summary.md with side-by-side delta vs the 2026-05-23 matrix; and an explicit keep/tune/revert/park decision per row.

Risk IDs: R5 (search trajectory), R10 (hot-path layout effects). Rollback: if the matrix shows no improvement after the throughput subset, the 5b2.2.30 deferral stands and the residual gap is genuinely inprocessing-dependent.
acceptance_criteria: The 1.16 matrix is re-run with the same methodology after 5b2.2.18.4, .5, .7, .9, .13 land. Side-by-side comparison vs the 2026-05-23 matrix is produced. Promotion decision per row is recorded in log/phase1/1.16-rerun/summary.md. cargo test and smoke pass before each row.
notes:
Created during 2026-05-23 fresh-eyes solver 11 review. Sequenced before 5b2.2.19 [1.15] because the original 1.16 matrix did not control for throughput overhead and the 1.15 gate would inherit the same measurement asymmetry.
Deep investigation 2026-05-24 (log/kissat-investigation-2026-05-23-broad/DEEPER_FINDINGS.md, Phase 1 G_focused_stable result) confirms that re-running the focused/stable matrix on the current code base regresses, not improves, the 10-instance profiling suite:

G_focused_stable (SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered SAT_SEARCH_MODE=focused-stable SAT_PHASE=best-then-target-then-saved):
- Solved 5/10 (vs A_default 10/10)
- PAR-2 3248.5s (+323% vs A_default 768s)
- TIMEOUTS: sudoku, REGRandom, mp1, battleship, case9
- WINS: Kakuro 97.7s (-55%), velev 30.1s (-55%)
- Iter30 regresses 5.4x (94s vs 17s)

The TIMEOUTS are explained by the four kissat-port implementation gaps identified in the deep investigation (Gaps 1-4 in DEEPER_FINDINGS.md):
- Gap 1: no trail reuse on restart amplifies the focused-mode EMA-restart cost in mode-alternation context
- Gap 2: reducer no-op when under budget interacts with mode-switch reset of EMA averages
- Gap 3: bump-to-1 used semantics leaves the wrong subset of clauses live through a mode switch
- Gap 4: restart margin 1.20 vs kissat 1.10 combined with focused-mode mode_init_conflicts=2000 over-switches

Recommendation: do NOT re-run this matrix until at least Gaps 1 and 3 land (beads SAT-playground-5b2.2.35 and SAT-playground-ycw). Re-testing focused/stable without those fixes is wasted compute — the underlying execution model is not yet faithful enough to kissat for mode alternation to work.
Third-pass investigation 2026-05-24 (log/kissat-investigation-third-pass-2026-05-24/THIRD_PASS_FINDINGS.md) tested I_vmtf_only (focused-stable + VMTF) which solved 8/10 on the new profile suite — vs G_focused_stable (without VMTF) solving 5/10. The VMTF flag is what makes focused-stable mode actually useful. Re-running the 1.16 matrix should specifically include I_vmtf_only / S6_vmtf_otfs (VMTF + OTFS) configs which preserve the mp1 (1.5s), battleship (0.95s), Kakuro (60s) wins. These are the configs to revalidate.
Reprioritized P2->P1 (slate-heron triage, post analyzesat-2026-05-28-perf-tax). With single-mode parity refuted as unachievable (5b2.2.56 accepted/closed), the focused/stable feature re-run is now THE lever for beating solver10 and resolving P0 5b2.2.53. Telemetry prereqs 5b2.2.43 + 18.15 are already closed; 18.5 closed this run. Remaining gating prereqs: 18.7, 18.4, 18.9, 18.13 (now P2). Recommend running the new perf-decompose bead first to prioritize those four by measured focused/stable overhead impact.
PREMISE REFUTED by d8p (2026-05-28). This bead assumed the 1.16 focused/stable comparison was unfair because the throughput subset (18.7/18.4/18.9/18.13) had not landed. perf-record + work-controlled measurement (log/d8p-focused-stable-perf/FINDINGS.md) show those overheads are inlined/<1% and absent from the focused/VMTF profile; the regression is a search-trajectory pathology (deep dive max level 307k, avg LBD 42, +16% props/conflict at equal conflicts). Re-running the matrix after the throughput subset lands will NOT change the verdict. Downgraded P1->P3; recommend re-scope to 'confirm d8p on a 2nd instance' or close as superseded by SAT-playground-588 (the real search-policy lever). Confirms the original 5b2.2.30 search-trajectory/inprocessing-dependent verdict.

title: Document SAT_PHASE override behavior in focused-stable mode
description:
Task class: documentation / configuration contract.

Background: src/main.rs:3526-3540 effective_phase_policy silently overrides the user-supplied SAT_PHASE value when SAT_SEARCH_MODE=focused-stable is on:

    Focused mode: Legacy or Saved → Saved
                  TargetThenSaved or BestThenTargetThenSaved → TargetThenSaved
    Stable mode: anything → BestThenTargetThenSaved

So a user setting SAT_PHASE=legacy SAT_SEARCH_MODE=focused-stable does not get the Legacy phase policy in focused mode; they silently get Saved. A user setting SAT_PHASE=best-then-target-then-saved in focused mode gets TargetThenSaved (best is only used in stable mode).

This override is reasonable Kissat-style behavior (focused mode favors target-phase guidance, stable mode favors best-phase consolidation) but it is documented nowhere user-facing:
- README.md at solver/11-kissat-port/README.md lists SAT_PHASE values without saying focused-stable overrides them.
- FEATURES.md / FEATURES.csv do not mention the override.
- CONFIG_SCHEMA.csv lists conflicts/requirements but does not record this overlay.

Goal: add a one-paragraph note in README.md under SAT_PHASE explaining the override matrix, plus a row in FEATURES.md for SAT_SEARCH_MODE noting it overlays SAT_PHASE values. Optionally add a SAT_CONFIG_DUMP output that records the effective policy alongside the user-supplied policy so artifact triage shows both.

Implementation notes:
- README change is small and orthogonal to code.
- If the dump shape changes, src/config.rs::dump and the replay file format need a schema bump or backward-compatible field; consider a follow-up rather than tying it to this bead.

Tests:
- a config-schema test asserting the documented override table matches effective_phase_policy is helpful but optional.

Benchmark gate: none. Documentation only.

Risk IDs: none. Rollback: revert the README/FEATURES edits.
acceptance_criteria: solver/11-kissat-port/README.md describes the SAT_PHASE override matrix when SAT_SEARCH_MODE=focused-stable is on. FEATURES.md notes the overlay. cargo test and smoke pass (no code change).

title: Avoid full O(V) heap rebuild on every focused→stable mode switch
description:
Task class: performance-claim subtask of [1.14] Search-throughput pass.

Background: src/main.rs:2737-2739 refresh_stable_branch_heap_scores calls rebuild_branch_queue (src/main.rs:2723-2735) on every focused→stable transition. rebuild_branch_queue clears branch_heap and branch_pos, re-scans 1..self.assignment.len() to push every unassigned decision variable, then sifts down. This is O(V) work and is paid on every mode switch.

In focused mode the heap is still maintained: bump_variable_activity (src/main.rs:3363-3377) sift-ups on every analyzed variable, and heap_reinsert_unassigned_decision_var (src/main.rs:2697) reinserts on every backtrack. So the heap is *already correct* on entry to refresh_stable_branch_heap_scores in the usual case — the rebuild is defensive against possible activity inversions during focused-mode bumping. But because heap_sift_up runs after every bump in focused mode, the only invariant the rebuild fixes is that previously VMTF-picked vars (which were heap_remove_assigned_top'd via pick_vmtf_branch_var → branch_heap_remove) need reinserting. Those vars are already reinserted by heap_reinsert_unassigned_decision_var on backtrack.

Goal: skip the full rebuild on transitions that do not need it. Two acceptable shapes:
- (preferred) drop refresh_stable_branch_heap_scores entirely and replace with a no-op or assertion that the heap is well-formed. Add a debug_assert that heap_invariant_holds.
- (conservative) keep the rebuild but gate it: only run when VMTF was active during the prior focused mode (self.vmtf_branching_active() was true). Skip otherwise.

Implementation notes:
- maybe_switch_search_mode at src/main.rs:3633 calls refresh_stable_branch_heap_scores when transitioning to Stable; that is the only caller besides tests.
- Profile a focused-stable run with SAT_VMTF=on to confirm the heap is consistent at the transition point. heap_invariant_holds tests can be added to src/main.rs tests.
- If kept, the rebuild can also be made incremental: walk vmtf_queue to find vars that were popped from the heap but not reinserted, and reinsert only those.

Tests:
- test_branch_heap_consistent_after_focused_stable_transition_with_vmtf
- test_branch_heap_consistent_after_focused_stable_transition_without_vmtf
- existing mode-switch tests continue to pass

Benchmark gate: search-core with SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_SEARCH_MODE=focused-stable SAT_VMTF=on. Counters: mode_switches, time around maybe_switch_search_mode (add a timer if not present). Expected: lower wall time on instances with many mode switches, no change to conflict counts / search trajectory.

Risk IDs: R5 (search trajectory if heap is left inconsistent). Rollback: restore unconditional rebuild_branch_queue.
acceptance_criteria: The full O(V) rebuild is gated or removed for the common case. heap invariant remains after every mode switch (covered by new debug_assert + tests). No PAR-2 regression on focused-stable+VMTF runs. cargo test and smoke pass.
notes: Identified during 2026-05-23 fresh-eyes solver 11 review. Not previously captured under 5b2.2.18.* throughput subtasks.

title: [1.14ab] Cache clause header and hoist loop-invariant config flags in conflict-analysis hot path
description:
Task class: performance-claim subtask of [1.14] Search-throughput pass.

Background: A sweep of the conflict-analysis hot path found three small but related cleanups that share the same fix family (cache loop-invariant or repeated-load values once). Bundled into one bead because each individual item is below the typical bench noise band; together they may be measurable, and they all touch the same functions.

Item A: mark_reason_literals_for_analysis reloads clause_header twice (src/main.rs:5210-5217)
    if LBD_META && self.update_reason_lbd && clause_idx < self.arena.len()
        && self.clause_is_learnt(clause_idx)
        && !self.clause_is_deleted(clause_idx)
    { ... }
clause_is_learnt and clause_is_deleted both call clause_header(clause_idx) (= self.arena[clause_idx]). Fix: cache once.
    let header = self.clause_header(clause_idx);
    if clause_header_learnt(header) && clause_header_mark(header) != CLAUSE_DELETED_MARK { ... }

Item B: clause_activity / set_clause_activity reload the clause header per call (src/main.rs:1828-1843)
Each helper calls self.clause_len(clause_idx) which loads self.arena[clause_idx]. bump_clause_activity in src/main.rs:3239-3258 does both a read and a write, so two header loads for one update. Fix: introduce a fused with_clause_activity_mut(clause_idx, |act| ...) (or two helpers that accept a precomputed extra_idx) so the header is loaded once. Composes cleanly with [1.14d] (5b2.2.18.4 / s11-1-14d) if f32 activity lands: the fused helper still benefits.

Item C: Loop-invariant runtime flags checked per literal/reason in conflict analysis
- mark_clause_literals_for_analysis (src/main.rs:5137-5138) checks self.use_resolved_conflict_analysis once per literal walked.
- mark_binary_literals_for_analysis (src/main.rs:5175-5176) checks the same per literal.
- mark_reason_literals_for_analysis (src/main.rs:5207) checks self.reduce_policy == ReducePolicy::LbdTiered once per reason walked.
All three are config-time invariants. Fix options:
  (a) Hoist into local bools at function entry and pass into the inner loop.
  (b) Extend the existing LBD_META const generic with a USE_RESOLVED and a LBD_TIERED const generic so monomorphization removes the branches entirely. Mirrors the HOT_STATS / MODE_TICKS pattern already used elsewhere in the propagate path.

Implementation notes:
- Items A and B are local refactors; tackle first.
- Item C requires touching the call sites in analyze_conflict_to_scratch / analyze_conflict_to_scratch_impl. The existing LBD_META const generic already shows the pattern; add USE_RESOLVED and LBD_TIERED alongside it.
- Verify the existing tests for resolved-conflict-analysis and LBD-tiered reduction continue to pass on every variant of the const generic combinations.
- Do all three under one PR so the conflict-analysis hot path is touched once rather than three times.

Tests:
- Existing conflict-analysis / LBD / resolved-conflict tests must pass unchanged.
- test_const_generic_specializations_match_baseline (synthetic sweep over all combinations of LBD_META / USE_RESOLVED / LBD_TIERED).
- test_clause_activity_fused_helper_matches_split_helpers.

Benchmark gate: search-core + discriminating with SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered (and one run with SAT_LBD_UPDATE_REASONS=on to exercise the Item A path). perf stat for branches / branch-misses / L1-dcache-load-misses around the conflict-analysis call on wide-UIP instances. Expected: small but consistent IPC improvement; no behavior change.

Skip rule: if profiling after the rest of the 5b2.2.18.* block shows conflict analysis is no longer a hot path, this bead may be rejected with a note in log/phase1/triage.md.

title: [1.14aa] Hoist accounting_mode / search_mode branches out of bump_analyzed_variable_activity
description:
Task class: performance-claim subtask of [1.14] Search-throughput pass.

Background: bump_analyzed_variable_activity in src/main.rs:3393-3402 contains loop-invariant branches per iteration:

    for &var in &bumped_vars {
        if !self.accounting_mode.is_temporary() && self.search_mode == SearchMode::Focused {
            self.vmtf_stamp_analyzed_var(var);
        }
        self.bump_variable_activity(var);
    }

Neither self.accounting_mode nor self.search_mode changes during the loop. The compiler may LICM-hoist these via inlining, but the indirect call to vmtf_stamp_analyzed_var (which itself rereads self.vmtf_queue.as_mut()) blocks aggressive optimization across the call boundary.

Goal: hoist the two checks. Two clean options:
  (a) Read both bools once before the loop into locals; branch outside the loop into either a VMTF-stamping or non-stamping variant. Costs code duplication but removes the branches.
  (b) Const-genericize a small finalize_analyzed_variables<const IS_FOCUSED_NORMAL: bool>(...) so monomorphization compiles the branch out. Mirrors the HOT_STATS / MODE_TICKS pattern already used elsewhere.

Implementation notes:
- Pair with [1.14z] (5b2.2.18.11): once the clear-seen pass fuses into bump_analyzed_variable_activity, the combined fused/hoisted function is the per-conflict finalize routine.
- Verify vmtf_stamp_analyzed_var still validates its own preconditions (var > 0, decision_var, not eliminated) — those checks need to remain because they vary per var.

Tests:

- test_finalize_analyzed_variables_stable_does_not_stamp_vmtf
- test_finalize_analyzed_variables_temporary_does_not_stamp_vmtf
- existing VMTF / activity-bump tests must pass unchanged

Benchmark gate: search-core with SAT_SEARCH_MODE=focused-stable SAT_VMTF=on (the only configuration where the branch was non-trivial). perf stat for branches and branch-misses around the conflict-analysis call. Expected: small but consistent IPC improvement; no behavior change.

title: [1.14z] Fuse scratch_bumped_vars clear-seen and activity-bump into one pass
description:
Task class: performance-claim subtask of [1.14] Search-throughput pass.

Background: After UIP construction, analyze_conflict_to_scratch_impl in src/main.rs:5304-5308 walks scratch_bumped_vars to clear scratch_seen and scratch_resolved:

    for &var in &self.scratch_bumped_vars {
        self.scratch_seen[var] = 0;
        self.scratch_resolved[var] = 0;
    }

Then immediately afterwards, the search loop calls bump_analyzed_variable_activity (src/main.rs:3393-3402) which walks scratch_bumped_vars AGAIN to do VMTF stamping and activity bumping. Two full passes over the same vector per conflict, on conflict-analysis-frequent code.

Goal: fuse. Combine the clear-seen / clear-resolved / vmtf_stamp_analyzed_var / bump_variable_activity work into a single iteration. The four operations do not conflict (they update independent fields keyed by var).

Implementation notes:
- The cleanest path is to delete the trailing clear-loop in analyze_conflict_to_scratch_impl and move that work into bump_analyzed_variable_activity (rename it if desired, e.g. finalize_analyzed_variables).
- The fused function still needs the std::mem::take dance (or a by-index iteration; see also gap below) to call &mut self methods like bump_variable_activity.
- Pair with [1.14aa] (hoisted branches in bump_analyzed_variable_activity, see SAT-playground-5b2.2.18.12) so the per-iteration body is simultaneously minimal and branch-free for the common case.
- Verify the order: clear-seen must happen before any path that re-reads scratch_seen for the same var, but bump_variable_activity does not touch scratch_seen. Order is unconstrained between the four ops.

Tests:
- test_fused_finalize_clears_scratch_seen
- test_fused_finalize_clears_scratch_resolved
- test_fused_finalize_bumps_activity_in_same_call
- test_fused_finalize_stamps_vmtf_when_focused
- existing conflict-analysis / activity-bump tests must pass unchanged

Benchmark gate: search-core + discriminating with SAT_USE_LBD=on. Counters: conflict-analysis time if measurable; perf stat for L1-dcache-load-misses around the conflict-analysis call on wide-UIP instances (REGRandom K4, SCPC-500). Expected: small but consistent IPC improvement on conflict-heavy classes.

Risk IDs: R10 (cache layout). Rollback: split back into two passes.
notes:

title: [1.14w] Fuse LearnedMeta lookups and glue histogram in conflict-analysis hot path
description:
Task class: performance-claim subtask of [1.14] Search-throughput pass.

Background: LearnedMeta access in src/main.rs goes through a two-step learned_id_by_clause[clause_idx] -> learned_meta[id] lookup, but the conflict-analysis hot path performs this pair multiple times per learned-clause reason:

- mark_learned_clause_recent (src/main.rs:2127-2138), called per learned-clause reason during the UIP walk, calls THREE separate helpers (learnt_lbd, learnt_used_recently, set_learnt_used_recently) — each doing its own learned_id_for_clause + meta-index. Six array accesses per reason walked.
- maybe_improve_lbd (src/main.rs:2064-2077), enabled by SAT_LBD_UPDATE_REASONS=on, does FOUR-FIVE lookups per improvement: learnt_lbd, set_learnt_lbd, classify_learnt_clause (which calls learnt_lbd again and set_learnt_tier).
- initialize_learnt_lbd (src/main.rs:2050-2056) does FIVE lookups per new learned clause.
- record_current_mode_glue_use (src/main.rs:2148, reached from mark_learned_clause_recent) hits the per-mode glue histogram with a resize check + saturating_add per reason walked — another cache line touched per call.

For UIP walks touching 30+ reasons, the redundant indirections are ~150-200 per conflict, on the hottest path the solver has.

Goal: refactor so each caller obtains LearnedId ONCE (via try_learned_id_for_clause) and operates on &mut self.learned_meta[id.0] directly. Provide a fused mark_learned_reason_used(id) helper that combines: read lbd, max(used_recently, 1), write used_recently, record glue. Also batch the histogram update — accumulate per-conflict glue contributions in a small local vec (or fixed array sized to typical LBD range, e.g. [0; 32]) during the UIP walk, then commit to focused_glue_histogram / stable_glue_histogram once at conflict completion.

Implementation notes:
- Pass a LearnedId (Option<LearnedId>) into mark_reason_literals_for_analysis when the reason is a clause; reuse the LearnedId for downstream helpers.
- maybe_improve_lbd should take LearnedId too and inline its own classify path so the second learnt_lbd lookup disappears.
- initialize_learnt_lbd: capture LearnedId in allocate_learned_id, pass it to set_learnt_lbd, classify_learnt_clause, set_learnt_used_recently in a single batch.
- The local glue-histogram buffer should be a Solver scratch field reset per conflict (no per-conflict allocation).
- Keep public helpers (learnt_lbd, learnt_used_recently, etc.) for non-hot callers; only the conflict-analysis path changes.

Tests:
- test_mark_learned_reason_used_matches_split_helpers_on_random_inputs
- test_fused_lbd_improvement_matches_split_helpers
- test_glue_histogram_batched_matches_per_reason_histogram
- existing learned-clause / LBD / reduce-DB tests must pass unchanged

Benchmark gate: search-core + discriminating with SAT_USE_LBD=on, both with SAT_LBD_UPDATE_REASONS=on and off. Counters: lbd_improved, learned_used_recently_writes (add if absent), conflict-analysis time if measurable. perf stat for L1-dcache-load-misses around conflict analysis on a wide-UIP instance (REGRandom K4, SCPC-500). Expected: lower L1 misses per conflict; small but consistent PAR-2 improvement on conflict-heavy classes.

Risk IDs: R10 (cache layout), R3 (LBD/learned-clause correctness).
notes:
Audit note 2026-05-22 (fifth-pass review): after 5b2.2.31 closed, record_current_mode_glue_use in src/main.rs:2160-2174 now performs TWO histogram increments per call — one into focused_glue_recent/stable_glue_recent (the tier-limit driver) and one into stats.focused_glue_used/stats.stable_glue_used (the cumulative reporting histogram). Each increment is a Self::increment_glue_histogram call with its own resize check + saturating_add, touching different cache lines. Combined with the per-reason call site in mark_learned_clause_recent, this is 4 read-modify-writes per learned reason walked in conflict analysis.

The batching rewrite in this bead therefore has a stronger motivation than the original description suggested: accumulate per-conflict glue contributions in a small Solver scratch buffer (e.g. [u32; 64] sized to expected LBD range), then commit to BOTH the recent and cumulative histograms once at conflict completion. That collapses 4N hot writes into 4 final writes per conflict for N learned reasons.

If the conflict has any glue exceeding the scratch buffer cap, fall back to direct writes for those (rare, e.g. LBD>64).

title: [1.14u] Batch search_ticks accumulation in propagation hot loop
description:
Task class: performance-claim subtask of [1.14] Search-throughput pass.

Background: record_search_ticks at src/main.rs:2987-2992 does a read-modify-write on self.stats.search_ticks per call. It is invoked per watch scan in propagate_impl (main.rs:3101), per inner-clause literal scanned (main.rs:3191), and per binary edge probed (main.rs:3048). The MODE_TICKS const generic correctly compiles the body out when false, but in focused-stable mode (MODE_TICKS=true — its actual reason for existing, see mode_switch_at_ticks use at main.rs:3423), every scan is a single RMW on a shared cache line in self.stats.

For propagation-heavy instances doing 10^8 + scans, this is 10^8 RMWs against one cache line; even when the line is L1-resident, that is a non-trivial fraction of propagation cost. Kissat handles this with batched ticks: increment a local counter inside the inner loop, flush once at function exit.

Goal: rewrite propagate_impl / propagate_binary_implications to accumulate ticks in a local u64 declared at function entry; flush to self.stats.search_ticks at every function return point (conflict / no-conflict / early return). Keep the existing semantics under MODE_TICKS=false (no-op). Preserve correctness around mode_switch_at_ticks — the flushed counter must be visible to maybe_switch_search_mode (called from the conflict path of the search loop, AFTER propagate has returned).

Implementation notes:
- A struct LocalTickAccumulator with #[inline(always)] flush(self, stats: &mut SolverStats) might be cleaner than open-coded flush at every return.
- Audit every return path in propagate_impl (there are multiple: conflict via clause unit, conflict via long-clause, conflict via binary, normal completion); each must flush before returning.
- The flush must happen even when accounting_mode.is_temporary() — but only for the normal stats path; temporary stats stay zero anyway. Match the current behavior (record_search_ticks does the is_temporary check).
- Consider whether the same batching applies to propagations counter writes (record_propagation_accounting). That is paired with bead [1.14s] (TEMP const generic) and the two could compose.

Tests:
- test_search_ticks_match_unbatched_baseline_on_smoke
- test_search_ticks_flushed_on_conflict_return
- test_search_ticks_flushed_on_completion_return
- test_search_ticks_flushed_on_early_unit_conflict_return
- test_search_ticks_zero_in_temporary_assumption_mode
- existing focused-stable tick-based mode-switch tests must pass unchanged

Benchmark gate: search-core with SAT_SEARCH_MODE=focused-stable (the path that actually consumes search_ticks). perf stat for instructions/cycle and L1-dcache-load-misses around the propagate call. Expected: small but consistent IPC improvement on propagation-heavy instances; no change to mode-switch behavior.

Risk IDs: R10. Rollback: revert to per-scan record_search_ticks.
notes:
s11-02 evidence 2026-05-24 from SAT-playground-5b2.2.52: perf stat was attempted but blocked by host perf_event_paranoid=4, so hardware counters were unavailable. Solver stats still show tick-mode work is huge: default K4 recorded search_ticks=27.339B for 54.448M propagations; default battleship recorded 6.280B ticks for 16.547M propagations; VMTF K4 recorded 138.849B ticks for 100.634M propagations. Full-suite focused/stable tick mode remains a trajectory problem too, not only tick RMW overhead: default tick mode PAR-2=1201.538 with mp1 UNKNOWN, while focused/stable no-ticks PAR-2=2293.353 with Kakuro TIMEOUT and Velev UNKNOWN. title: [1.14t] Incremental target/best phase capture (O(delta) instead of O(trail))
description:
Task class: performance-claim subtask of [1.14] Search-throughput pass.

Background: maybe_capture_phase_prefix in src/main.rs:3574-3595 detects a new deepest unconflicted prefix and calls capture_target_phase(assigned) and/or capture_best_phase(assigned) (src/main.rs:3548-3572). Both implementations iterate the entire &self.trail from index 0, even though the previous capture already wrote target_phase[var] / best_phase[var] for every variable below self.target_assigned / self.best_assigned. The prefix is monotone-growing — everything below the prior watermark is already recorded.

This function runs in the no-conflict arm of the search loop (called from main.rs:5388), so it fires once per propagation that does not conflict. On SAT-heavy / deep-prefix instances (battleship, Timetable, DLTM_twitter), the trail can be 50k - 500k+ assignments and a new max prefix is hit frequently. That makes the function O(assigned) per call when it should be O(assigned - prev_assigned).

Goal: capture only the new tail. In capture_target_phase, iterate &self.trail[self.target_assigned..assigned] before updating self.target_assigned. Same for capture_best_phase using self.best_assigned. The unassigned guard inside the loop can be kept defensively, but the slice will only contain assigned literals at capture time (they are on the trail).

Implementation notes:
- Read self.target_assigned / self.best_assigned BEFORE the iteration; the function currently writes the new watermark at the end.
- Verify trail bounds: assigned == self.trail.len() at the call site; old watermark fits in [0, assigned].
- Keep the existing inner unassigned check as a safety net under SAT_CHECK_INVARIANTS=on, but consider eliding it on release builds (literals on the trail are always assigned).
- The same incremental optimization applies to any future variant that iterates the trail for phase work.

Tests:
- test_capture_target_phase_only_touches_new_tail (instrument with a counter or assert no writes to indices below old watermark)
- test_capture_target_phase_handles_first_capture_at_zero_watermark
- test_capture_target_phase_idempotent_when_assigned_equals_watermark
- test_capture_best_phase_only_touches_new_tail
- existing target/best-phase tests must continue to pass unchanged

Benchmark gate: search-core and discriminating with SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved and SAT_PHASE=best-then-target-then-saved, especially on deep-trail SAT-heavy instances. Counters to inspect: phase_save_target, phase_save_best, time spent in maybe_capture_phase_prefix (add a timer if not already present). Expected: lower wall time on SAT-heavy classes, no change on UNSAT-heavy.

Risk IDs: R10 (hot-path layout) and the target/best-phase invariant family from 5b2.2.8. Rollback: revert to full-trail iteration.
notes:
s11-02 evidence 2026-05-24 from SAT-playground-5b2.2.52: full profiling-set runs show phase capture is not just a theoretical hot path. In current default on Iter30, phase_save_target=59842 and phase_save_best=59842 with max_decision_level=61903; search time is 82.31s versus 6.78s in single/LBD, despite only 1.52x conflicts and 1.32x propagations. In VMTF Sudoku, phase_save_target=320706 and phase_save_best=320706 with max_decision_level=307093, and the row goes UNKNOWN at 295.879s. This confirms O(trail) capture can dominate focused/stable deep-prefix rows. Logs: log/phase1/5b2.2.52-s11-default-clean/stats.jsonl and log/phase1/5b2.2.52-s11-default-vmtf-clean/stats.jsonl.
AnalyzeSAT 2026-05-26 branch-phase run found a correctness/status issue separate from this O(delta) performance task: SAT_PHASE=target-then-saved in single-mode search returns UNKNOWN on Sudoku at 295.852s. New bead SAT-playground-6ci tracks rejecting/gating single-mode target phase semantics; this task can stay focused on capture cost after semantics are safe.

title: [1.14s] Hoist accounting_mode branch out of propagation hot path via TEMP const generic
description:
Task class: performance-claim subtask of [1.14] Search-throughput pass.

Background: src/main.rs:2976-2982 record_propagation_accounting branches on self.accounting_mode.is_temporary() for every single propagation. The propagate_impl function already const-genericizes HOT_STATS so hot-stats writes are monomorphized out; the temporary-vs-normal accounting branch is not, so every propagation pays a (predictable but non-free) branch.

Goal: introduce a parallel TEMP const generic on propagate_impl (or refactor propagate so temporary and normal mode dispatch into separate monomorphized functions). Then record_propagation_accounting becomes either temporary_stats.propagations += 1 or stats.propagations += 1 with no branch.

Implementation notes:
- propagate() chooses TEMP at the call site based on self.accounting_mode.is_temporary() once.
- propagate_binary_implications and propagate_impl already take HOT_STATS; add TEMP alongside.
- record_propagation_accounting becomes record_propagation_accounting::<TEMP>().
- VMTF stamping, restart EMA, phase saving already guard via accounting_mode checks — those checks can also accept TEMP if it helps.

Tests:
- existing propagation / temporary-assumption tests must pass unchanged
- test_temporary_assumption_propagation_uses_temporary_stats
- test_normal_propagation_uses_normal_stats

Benchmark gate: search-core. Expected counter: lower instructions/cycle for propagate; lower per-prop branch count via perf stat. PAR-2 effect likely small but non-zero on propagation-heavy instances.

Risk IDs: R10 (hot-path layout). Rollback: revert to runtime branch.
notes:
s11-03 2026-05-24: During SAT-playground-5b2.2.56 I tried a narrow accounting/LBD helper hoist in the propagation path. Full profiling run log/phase1/5b2.2.56-after-prop-accounting-hoist/results.csv was PAR-2 750.454 versus the accepted prop-specialized baseline 745.558 (+4.896 worse), despite some per-instance wins; reverted. Treat this as evidence that a simple local hoist is insufficient, not as closure of the broader TEMP const-generic propagation-accounting bead.
Satisfied by 56e56cc (SAT-playground-5b2.2.61). solver/11-kissat-port/src/main.rs now threads const NORMAL_SEARCH through propagate_impl/propagate_binary_implications/record_propagation_accounting/record_search_ticks/enqueue_impl, dispatched from propagate() off !accounting_mode.is_temporary(). In the NORMAL_SEARCH=true monomorphization record_propagation_accounting is a bare stats.propagations+=1 with no accounting_mode branch — exactly this bead's 'TEMP const generic' ask. Temporary-assumption accounting verified by test_normal_propagation_updates_normal_accounting_and_phase + test_temp_assumption_conflict_restores_propagate_head (asserts temporary_stats.propagations). perf-tax measurement (analyzesat-2026-05-28-perf-tax) confirms it removed ~17-22 insn/prop with no L1-miss change (pure ALU branch removal as intended).

title: [1.14r] LearnedMeta hot/cold split
description:
Task class: performance-claim subtask of [1.14] Search-throughput pass.

Background: src/main.rs:395-402 defines LearnedMeta with lbd:u16, tier:u8, used_recently:u8, removable:bool, vivified:bool, created_at_conflict:u64 — ~16+ bytes after padding per learned clause. The hot accesses (reduce-DB candidate scoring, conflict-analysis LBD update through maybe_improve_lbd, mark_learned_clause_recent) only need lbd / tier / used_recently — 4 bytes. The cold fields (removable, vivified, created_at_conflict) inflate the side table that the reduce_db_lbd_tiered scan walks O(num_learned_clauses) times per reduction.

Goal: split LearnedMeta into a packed hot table (Vec<u32> with lbd[16] | tier[8] | used_recently[8], or three separate Vec<>s) and a cold side table for removable / vivified / created_at_conflict. Reduces L1 pressure on reduce-DB scans on instances with many learned clauses (typical of UNSAT-heavy K4 / Kakuro classes).

Implementation notes:
- Keep the existing helpers (learnt_lbd, set_learnt_lbd, learnt_used_recently, set_learnt_used_recently, learnt_tier) so callers are unchanged.
- Internally route to the new hot table.
- created_at_conflict and the bools move to a parallel Vec keyed by LearnedId.
- Verify the cold fields are only consulted by inprocessing / triage paths, not by the search loop.

Tests:
- test_learned_meta_hot_fields_round_trip_through_helpers
- test_learned_meta_cold_fields_unchanged_during_search
- test_reduce_db_uses_hot_fields_only
- test_lbd_improvement_updates_hot_table
- existing reduce-DB and LBD tests must pass unchanged

Benchmark gate: search-core + discriminating with SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered, especially on UNSAT-heavy instances with large learned-clause counts (REGRandom K4, SCPC-500, aaai10-planning). perf stat for L1-dcache-load-misses around the reduce_db_lbd_tiered call. Expected counter: lower L1 misses per reduce-DB call; possible PAR-2 improvement on UNSAT-heavy classes.

Risk IDs: R10 (cache layout), R3 (LBD/learned-clause correctness).
acceptance_criteria: Keep if it improves aggregate PAR-2 over the profiling suite beyond run-to-run noise. title: [1.14q] Shrink per-variable arrays from usize to u32
description:
Task class: performance-claim subtask of [1.14] Search-throughput pass.

Background: solver/11-kissat-port stores several per-variable arrays as Vec<usize> (8 bytes per variable on x86_64) even though their values comfortably fit in u32:
- decision_level: Vec<usize> (src/main.rs:898)
- branch_pos: Vec<usize> (src/main.rs:933)
- reason: Vec<ReasonCode> where ReasonCode = usize (src/main.rs:900 / 523)

On a 1M-variable instance these three arrays alone consume ~24MB; halving decision_level and branch_pos saves ~8MB — often the difference between L3-resident and DRAM-bound during conflict analysis. The plan cache-layout section does not call this out; easy to miss in plan-vs-code reviews.

Goal: change decision_level and branch_pos from Vec<usize> to Vec<u32>. Document a maximum-variables invariant (e.g. < 2^31). Optionally: also pack ReasonCode into u32 (1 tag bit + 31 payload bits), capping ClauseRef and BinaryClauseId at u32; this is more invasive and should be a follow-up sub-fix.

Implementation notes:
- Introduce a typed VarLevel = u32 newtype or just use u32 directly with conversion at call sites.
- compute_lbd_from_lits (uses decision_level), conflict-analysis loops, learned_clause_asserts_at_level, debug_assert_clause_asserting_after_backtrack — all read decision_level on hot paths.
- branch_pos compares with BRANCH_NOT_IN_HEAP sentinel; ensure the sentinel fits in u32 (use u32::MAX).
- Add a one-time check at solver construction that num_vars < 2^31 with a clear error.

Tests:

Sub-fix candidate: pack ReasonCode into u32. Track separately if pursued.

title: [1.14g+] OTSS on-the-fly self-subsuming resolution
description:
Task class: solver-behavior / performance-claim under epic [Phase 1 - Search, decision, phase, restart, and learned-clause logic].

Background: 1.14g (5b2.2.28) tracks on-the-fly subsumption (OTFS) during clause minimization. OTSS is the related but distinct Kissat-class pass: when a learned clause minimized against reason R produces a strict subset of R, replace R in place rather than only shortening the learned clause. The scratch_resolved[] tracking introduced for resolved-conflict-analysis (use_resolved_conflict_analysis in src/main.rs analyze_conflict_to_scratch_impl) is the same infrastructure OTSS needs, so the marginal code cost is small once OTFS lands.

Goal: while analyzing or minimizing a conflict, detect when the in-progress learned clause is a strict subset of a participating reason clause R; if so, strengthen R in place (delete and re-add via the proof, update watchers, update reason pin sets) under the same FormulaEdit-style discipline as the rest of search. Off by default; gated by SAT_OTSS or a sub-flag of SAT_CLAUSE_MIN.

Implementation notes:
- Reuse scratch_resolved / scratch_seen state already populated by conflict analysis.
- Require live reason guarantees (do not strengthen a locked reason without replacing it).
- Emit proper DRAT add(new) before delete(old) and update the existing learned/original clause meta.
- Counter: otss_strengthened, otss_skipped_locked, otss_skipped_proof.

Tests:
- test_otss_strengthens_long_reason_when_learned_is_strict_subset
- test_otss_skips_when_reason_is_locked
- test_otss_proof_round_trips_through_drat_trim
- test_otss_does_not_change_assertion_level

Benchmark gate: search-core + discriminating with SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered. Track avg_lbd, avg_learned_size, conflicts, propagations, proof_added_clauses, proof_deleted_clauses.

Skip rule: if 5b2.2.28 (OTFS) lands and already captures the bulk of the gain, this bead may be marked rejected with a counter-delta note.

Risk IDs: shares reason-deletion-safety risk with reduce_db / formula-edit work.
notes:
QuietHill (/nextbeads, 2026-05-28 12:25 UTC): releasing claim after mapping out implementation effort. OTSS in kissat (kissat/src/strengthen.c + deduce.c lines 143-157) is NOT a post-analyze pass — it happens DURING analyze_conflict, after each reason resolution, when 'antecedent_size > 2 && resolvent_size < antecedent_size'. The strengthening operation: removes the pivot literal from the reason in place, marks the clause as 'shrunken' (preserving arena slot), updates watchers (unwatch_blocking + re-watch on new highest-level lit), emits SHRINK_CLAUSE_IN_PROOF, and RETURNS the strengthened clause as the new pseudo-conflict so analyze continues from there. Implementation cost in solver 11 is significant: (1) track antecedent_size + resolvent_size through analyze_conflict_to_scratch_impl's loop, (2) add in-place clause shrinking primitive (solver 11 stores length in arena header word — clause_header_size — and learnt clauses have CLAUSE_HAS_EXTRA_BIT meta after the literals, so shrinking requires moving the extras OR taking the kissat approach of marking 'shrunken' and accepting wasted tail until GC), (3) plumb the strengthened clause back as the new conflict ref into the iterative loop, (4) handle the binary-strengthen case (kissat's binary_on_the_fly_strengthen allocates a fresh binary clause and discards the strengthened long clause via mark_clause_as_garbage), (5) proof discipline: SHRINK_CLAUSE_IN_PROOF emits add(shrunken) then delete(original), and the meta of the strengthened clause needs lbd/activity preserved. title: [1.14n] Variable reordering pass in main search loop
description:
Kissat calls kissat_reordering() and kissat_reorder() periodically in the main search loop (search.c:210). This pass re-sorts the VMTF queue or VSIDS-based decision ordering based on accumulated activity scores, keeping the decision heuristic aligned with recent conflict history between major resets.

Solver 11 has no reordering pass. Variable activities accumulate via VSIDS bumps and VMTF stamps, but there is no periodic step that uses this accumulated information to realign the decision structures beyond the per-conflict bump.

Implementation:
1. Add a reordering counter/interval (similar to restart and reduce intervals).
2. In the main search loop, check whether a reordering pass is due.
3. For stable mode (VSIDS heap): the heap self-maintains ordering on insert/update, so a full rebuild may not be needed — investigate whether Kissat's reorder adds significant benefit beyond heap updates.
4. For focused mode (VMTF queue): reorder means stamping variables in activity order to reset the traversal priority.
5. Gate the reordering interval on a conflict or tick count and tune empirically.

Kissat reference: search.c:210, reorder.c.

title: [1.14m] Iterating mode: skip restart/reorder overhead after unit-clause learning
description:
Kissat sets solver->iterating=true whenever a unit clause is learned during conflict analysis (learn.c:51). The main search loop checks this flag (search.c:198) and calls kissat_iterate() to handle the unit without going through the full restart/reorder path, saving scheduling overhead when only units are produced.

Solver 11 has no iterating field or equivalent path. Every conflict cycle goes through the full should_restart + maybe_switch_search_mode sequence regardless of whether the learned clause was a unit.

Implementation:
1. Add an iterating: bool field to the Solver struct.
2. In analyze_conflict_to_scratch_impl (or the learn path), set self.iterating = true when the learned clause has length 1.
3. In the main search loop, after unit propagation on a learned unit, check iterating and skip the restart check and mode-switch check for that conflict cycle. Reset iterating to false after the check.

This is most visible on UNSAT instances where unit propagation at the root generates many unit clauses late in search. Kissat reference: learn.c:51, search.c:198, iterate.c.

title: [1.14l] Bump reason-side variable activities during conflict analysis
description:
Kissat optionally expands reason chains during conflict analysis to bump activity of variables that are NOT in the 1-UIP clause but appear in the reason clauses of 1-UIP variables (analyze.c: analyze_reason_side_literals, called after building solver->clause). This is rate-limited:
- Only fires when decision_rate < bumpreasonsrate (default 10) — i.e., skip when few decisions between conflicts.
- Bounded by bumpreasonslimit (default 10x the current analyzed set size).
- Uses exponential delay (BUMP_DELAY) when the expanded set is too large.

Solver 11's bump_analyzed_variable_activity (main.rs:3254) only bumps variables that appeared directly in scratch_seen (the 1-UIP expansion). Reason-side variables beyond the 1-UIP clause receive no activity bump. This underestimates the activity of variables that repeatedly appear in reason chains without reaching the 1-UIP cut, causing the VSIDS heap to deprioritize them.

Note: this is distinct from bead SAT-playground-5b2.2.29 (LBD-based clause tier promotion). That bead is about lowering a CLAUSE's LBD; this bead is about bumping VARIABLE activities in the heap.

Implementation: after analyze_conflict_to_scratch (main.rs line ~5240), if not in temporary context and decision_rate is below threshold, iterate scratch_conflict_clause literals, expand each variable's reason chain up to a size limit, and call bump_variable_activity for any newly seen variable. Guard with SAT_BUMP_REASONS=on flag.

  bump_reasons_attempted

  bump_reasons_skipped_rate
  bump_reasons_skipped_limit

title: [1.14k] Warmup phase: populate saved phases before main search
description:
Kissat runs a warmup phase (warmup.c) before the main search loop. It iterates: decide (using VSIDS/VMTF order) then propagate_beyond_conflicts (ignore conflict outcomes and keep deciding). On completion, backtrack to level 0 WITHOUT updating saved phases, so the assignment reached at maximum depth is captured in saved_phase.

This populates saved_phase with a heuristically good initial assignment before any real CDCL reasoning begins, giving the first restart something meaningful to return to. It is equivalent to a single-pass local-search initialization.

Solver 11 has no warmup. The saved_phase at search start is initialized to initial_phase (negative literal polarity per MiniSat convention, main.rs:1454), which has no structural information. The warmup would make the initial saved_phase reflect the VSIDS-guided satisfying attempt, which is typically much better.

Implementation: add a warmup() method that runs decide/propagate_beyond_conflicts (propagate accepting multiple conflicts per trail position by ignoring them and continuing to assign) until all variables assigned or timeout. Call kissat_backtrack_without_updating_phases equivalent: backtrack to 0 but leave saved_phase as the assignment captured at maximum depth. Guard with SAT_WARMUP=on flag.

Note: warmup only improves SAT instances; UNSAT instances are unaffected. On instances where the VSIDS ordering happens to find a near-complete assignment quickly, this is a free win before any conflict-driven reasoning.
notes:
Third-pass investigation 2026-05-24 (log/kissat-investigation-third-pass-2026-05-24/THIRD_PASS_FINDINGS.md) recommends pairing warmup with a separate lucky-assignment heuristic (new bead SAT-playground-ide). Warmup populates saved_phase via UP-completion (one-shot); lucky tries trivial all-true/all-false assignments. The two are complementary: warmup gives a heuristically good initial assignment; lucky catches instances where a trivial assignment SATs immediately. battleship-16-31-sat is likely a lucky case (kissat 0.18s vs solver 11 0.95s with VMTF) — warmup alone wouldn't catch it because the assignment must literally be all-true.

title: [1.14j] Trail reuse on restart
description:
Kissat's kissat_restart (restart.c) calls reuse_trail() before backtracking. Rather than always backtracking to level 0, it computes the longest prefix of the current trail that should be preserved:
- Stable mode: keep all levels where the decision variable's VSIDS score exceeds the next candidate's score.
- Focused mode: keep all levels where the decision variable's VMTF stamp exceeds the next VMTF candidate's stamp.
The backtrack target is the computed prefix level, not 0. Counts tracked as restarts_reused_trails and restarts_reused_levels.

Solver 11 always backtracks to level 0 on restart (perform_restart_if_pending, main.rs:3708: 'self.backtrack(0)'). On mp1 focused/VMTF mode, avg_decision_level=882, so each restart throws away ~882 levels of propagation. Trail reuse can preserve a prefix of these, especially in focused mode where VMTF stamps identify the most-recent conflict variables.

Implementation: add reuse_trail() that walks trail_limits from deepest to shallowest and returns the level where the decision variable's score (heap) or stamp (VMTF) falls below the next-candidate threshold. Call from perform_restart_if_pending before self.backtrack(level). Guard with SAT_RESTART_REUSE_TRAIL=on flag for opt-in benchmarking.

Tests:
  test_trail_reuse_stable_keeps_high_score_prefix
  test_trail_reuse_focused_keeps_high_stamp_prefix
  test_trail_reuse_does_not_reuse_at_zero

title: [1.14i] Focused restart interval: logn(restarts) growth
description:
Kissat's focused-mode restart scheduling grows the inter-restart interval with each restart via kissat_update_focused_restart_limit (restart.c):
  delta = restartint + (restarts > 0 ? kissat_logn(restarts) - 1 : 0)
  next_limit = CONFLICTS + delta

where kissat_logn(n) = floor(log2(n)) + 1. So after k restarts in focused mode, the minimum conflicts between restarts grows as log2(k). This prevents focused mode from restarting arbitrarily fast once many restarts have occurred — a soft throttle on EMA restarts.

Solver 11 uses a fixed restart_min_conflicts=50 (KISSAT_EMA_RESTART_MIN_CONFLICTS=50, main.rs:76). With VMTF focused mode, the solver saw 329 glucose restarts and 5,497 reluctant restarts in 60s on mp1 (log/1.12a/reretest-300-focused-vmtf). The fixed threshold does not prevent early restart storms.

Change: in note_kissat_ema_conflict (main.rs:3426) and/or perform_restart_if_pending (main.rs:3708), update restart_min_conflicts after each focused-mode restart to base + logn(focused_restart_count) - 1. Add a focused_restarts counter distinct from the glucose_restarts stat, since the logn growth should apply only to focused-mode EMA restarts.

title: [1.14h] LBD bump on reason clause improvement (kissat-style promote)
description:
In Kissat, when a clause is used as a reason during propagation and its current LBD is higher than the LBD it would get at the current decision level, its LBD is updated downward (promoted to a lower tier). This keeps frequently-used reason clauses from aging into tier 3 even if they had a high initial LBD.

Currently solver 11 only bumps LBD on conflict analysis via SAT_LBD_UPDATE_REASONS. Reason-side bumping lowers the effective LBD of the clause database over time, directly addressing the high avg_lbd=50 regime observed in focused/stable mode.

The SAT_LBD_UPDATE_REASONS flag already exists (config field update_reason_lbd, main.rs). Check whether it is applying the update at the correct point: it should recompute LBD of a reason clause every time it is used as a reason and update the stored LBD if the new value is lower. Verify the update happens at propagation time (not just conflict analysis) and that tier re-assignment happens immediately.

If the flag is correct, this bead is a validation; if the update is only happening at conflict analysis, move it to the propagation hot path.

title: [1.14g] On-the-fly subsumption (OTFS) in clause minimization
description:
After learning a clause, check if the new clause subsumes any existing watched clause. Kissat performs OTFS (on-the-fly subsumption) during the minimize phase: for each literal in the learned clause, scan the watcher list for existing clauses that are subsumed by the new learned clause and delete them.

This reduces the database size without a full reduce_db pass and shortens effective clause lengths → lower LBD on future learned clauses. Particularly valuable in the focused mode regime where avg_lbd is currently 50+.

Implementation: after conflict analysis and minimization, iterate over literals in the final learned clause. For each literal, check watchers for a clause whose literal set is a superset of the learned clause. If found, remove the subsumed clause. Bound the scan to avoid overhead: limit to clauses of length <= learned_len + 4, skip if learned clause has > 20 literals.

This is an independent improvement from vivification (Phase 2 bead 2.3) and can be implemented within Phase 1 since it requires no formula-edit transaction layer.

  test_otfs_does_not_remove_non_subsumed
  test_otfs_proof_logs_deletion

title: [1.14f] Reduce_db minimum conflict interval guard for high-LBD regime
description:
When avg_lbd is high, LBD-tiered reduction fires constantly because all learned clauses land in tier 3. On mp1 with focused/VMTF mode: 12,025 reduce_db calls in 60s (1 per 5ms, 1 per ~6 conflicts) vs Kissat's 26 calls on the same instance. This GC overhead drops effective conflict rate from ~9,890/s (default) to ~1,220/s — an 8x slowdown.

The root fix is lower LBD via inprocessing (Phase 2), but a guard prevents the pathology while Phase 2 is not yet active.

Change: track reduce_db_last_conflicts and add a minimum conflict interval (e.g., 100 conflicts) between successive reduce_db calls. Only fire if both the conflict budget AND the minimum interval have elapsed. The interval should be tunable via SAT_REDUCE_MIN_INTERVAL config key.

Gate: do not reduce more than once per N conflicts where N >= 50 (try 100 as default). Verify on the profiling bench and search-core that this does not regress UNSAT instances that currently benefit from aggressive reduction.

Evidence: log/1.12a/reretest-300-focused-vmtf JSON stats: reductions=12025, conflicts=73125 (1 reduction per 6 conflicts). Compare Kissat log for same instance: reductions=26, conflicts=87156 (1 per 3352 conflicts).

Currently activity: Vec<f64> at src/main.rs:939 (~8MB on a 1M-variable instance). f32 activity halves the array footprint and the bump/decay write traffic in bump_variable_activity (main.rs:3219) which runs once per scratch_bumped_vars entry per conflict. crimson-fox /nextbeads opportunity assessment, 2026-05-28 23:15 UTC (NO code change, NOT claimed — per CLAUDE.md optimization workflow step 4 'do not implement when measured opportunity is negligible'). Measured the f32-clause-activity opportunity from existing stats (log/phase1/crimson-fox-1.14b-candidate-lbd-tiered-on/stats.jsonl, lbd-tiered profiling run). Clause activity is stored inline in the arena as CLAUSE_ACTIVITY_WORDS=2 (f64) per learnt-clause extra (src/main.rs:121, clause_activity_in_arena:1562, clause_activity/set_clause_activity:2366/2374, reduce_candidate_activity_rank:6227 which does activity.to_bits()>>32 assuming 64-bit). f32 would halve that to 1 word. Per-instance arena saving (1 word x learned_clauses_final / arena_words_live): sudoku 82120w/0.742%, 6s299 0.019%, REGRandom 179044w/1.809%, Kakuro 0.185%, SCPC 30499w/3.503%, velev 0.053%, brocard 0.002%, battleship 0.444%. Median ~0.3% of live arena; only SCPC (a 17s instance, not a bottleneck) exceeds 3%. Clause activity is accessed at CONFLICT frequency (bump in mark_clause_literals_for_analysis when reduce_db_enabled; read in reduce_db sort) not propagation frequency, so the write-traffic saving is also modest. AGAINST this <0.3%-median footprint upside: f32 has ~7 sig digits vs f64's ~15; clause_activity_inc starts 1.0 and grows x1.001/conflict, so two clauses bumped at nearby times can compare equal in f32 where f64 distinguishes them -> different reduce-db eviction order -> altered search trajectory (Risk R8, 'preserve ordering semantics and determinism'). This is the exact trajectory-sensitivity failure mode that rejected SAT-playground-5b2.2.39 (OTSS), 5b2.2.59 (paired reducer), and s11-1-14b (watch compaction) this session. Expected value is clearly negative: negligible (sub-keep-threshold) footprint gain vs real implementation+bench cost and real trajectory-perturbation risk. The bead's own audit note already records the prior f32-clause-activity result as 'neutral'. Recommendation: leave OPEN as a parked low-priority experiment; only revisit if a future profiler run shows the learnt-clause arena footprint is a measured bottleneck on a specific instance (it is not on the current profiling suite). If revisited, implement behind an opt-in flag (SAT_F32_CLAUSE_ACTIVITY) with a same-trajectory A/B at SAT_USE_LBD=on SAT_REDUCE=lbd-tiered and reject on any eviction-order-driven status change. title: lbd-tiered emergency reduce deletes down to soft budget (~97% cliff), not a fraction of hard budget
description:
From SAT-playground-4a3 investigation (VioletRidge 2026-05-29, base 724f573, FINDINGS_4a3.md).

reduce_db_lbd_tiered (main.rs:6451) always deletes candidates until projected_lits <= self.learned_lit_budget (the SOFT budget, main.rs:6477), even when the reduce was triggered by the HARD budget (emergency). The soft budget is tiny (LEARNED_LIT_BUDGET_BASE=2000 + 300*sqrt(reduce_db_calls)), so an emergency reduce nukes ~97% of the learned DB in a single pass.

Measured on mp1 (SAT_REDUCE_DB_INIT=5000000 to disable the scheduled path, isolating emergency): one emergency pass at ~250k conflicts dropped learned clauses from 199,999 to 6,646. Keep the scheduled (non-emergency) path deleting to the soft budget as today. Add a focused test asserting an emergency reduce on a synthetic over-hard-budget DB stops at the fractional-hard target, not the soft floor.

title: Gap SC-3: SAT_REORDER uses pure VSIDS activity; kissat uses clause-weighted score
description:
solver/11-kissat-port/src/main.rs:3104 reorder_branching_by_activity rebuilds the VMTF queue from VSIDS activity order via activity_reorder_vars(). Pure activity reorder, no formula-structure signal.

benchmarks/reference-solvers/kissat-latest/src/reorder.c:24-217 computes a clause-weighted score per literal:
- table[size] = 1, 1/2, 1/4, ... for sizes 2..reordermaxsize=100
- each irredundant clause adds table[size] to every literal in it
- each binary watcher edge adds table[2] for both ends
- per-variable score: weight = max(pos,neg) + 2*min(pos,neg)
- sorted by weight, tie-broken by VMTF stamp (focused) or VSIDS score (stable)
- focused mode: move sorted variables to queue front
- stable mode: update VSIDS scores by adding the weight (preserves activity history)

This structural signal lets kissat identify which variables sit at the densest part of the remaining formula after preprocessing reduced the easy structure. Pure-activity reorder cannot see formula shape after eliminations.

Out-of-scope for the 2026-05-27-search-control investigation (SAT_REORDER was off in the ablation), but no existing bead covers this in bd search reorder (only 5b2.2.18.2 covers binary propagation reordering, unrelated).

Reference: benchmarks/reference-solvers/kissat-latest/src/reorder.c:24-217.

Fix sketch:
- Port compute_weights() as a method on Solver computing weights[lit] for active vars.
- Port less_focused_order / less_stable_order comparators.
- In reorder_branching_by_activity, replace activity_reorder_vars() with the weighted comparator, keeping the existing VMTF-queue rebuild and VSIDS rescale paths.
- Add SAT_REORDER_MODE=activity|kissat env var to keep both during validation; default to 'activity' until the kissat path proves itself.

Acceptance: with SAT_REORDER=on SAT_REORDER_MODE=kissat the reorder pass produces a different decision sequence with non-zero clause-weighted score differences vs activity-only on at least one profiling instance; cargo test green; smoke green; no PAR-2 regression vs SAT_REORDER=on SAT_REORDER_MODE=activity on the profiling suite.
notes: Consolidation 2026-06-13: P3 -> P4. SAT_REORDER is off-default with no promotion path until reorder matters; the clause-weighted-score port needs its own implementation + gate and does not block anything. Revisit if/when reorder enters a default-candidate config.

title: Implement jumpreasons binary reason chain flattening
description:
Task class: micro-optimization. Implements kissat's binary reason chain flattening.

Background: When kissat assigns a literal L via binary propagation with reason 'other', it inspects whether 'other' itself was binary-propagated. If so, it skips the intermediate level and uses other's reason directly.

Kissat (benchmarks/reference-solvers/kissat-latest/src/assign.c:32-45):
  if (GET_OPTION (jumpreasons) && level && a->binary) {
    other = a->reason;  /* a is 'other's assigned record; jump to a->reason */
  }
  kissat_assign (...);

Default jumpreasons=1 (ON).

Solver 11's enqueue path stores binary reasons directly without chain flattening.

The effect: during conflict analysis, traversing binary reason chains is shorter under kissat. On binary-heavy formulas (kissat's classification.bigbig flag — > 99% binary clauses), this saves several iterations per reason in the analyze loop.

Evidence: log/kissat-investigation-third-pass-2026-05-24/THIRD_PASS_FINDINGS.md Gap 11. Not measured directly on the profiling suite (most instances aren't bigbig), but a clear semantic feature of kissat that solver 11 doesn't have.

Proposed change: in solver 11's enqueue/assign path, when assigning a literal via binary propagation:
1. Check if the 'other' literal in the binary clause is itself binary-assigned
2. If so, look up other's reason and use that
3. Otherwise use the current binary reason

Implementation notes:
- The binary-fast path (src/main.rs:3261-3299, propagate_binary_implications) is the place to do this.
- Need to inspect ReasonRef::Binary for the 'other' literal in the binary clause.
- One extra indirection but flattens the chain.

Tests:
  test_jumpreasons_flattens_chain
  test_jumpreasons_off_keeps_direct_reasons
  test_jumpreasons_preserves_correctness_of_drat_proof

Acceptance criteria: cargo test pass, smoke pass, invariant smoke pass with SAT_USE_LBD=on smoke. Profile bench shows no regression on the 10-instance suite. On binary-heavy formulas (would need to identify candidates), conflict analysis should traverse fewer reasons.

Larger project role: closes Gap 11 from the 2026-05-24 third-pass investigation. P4 / low priority — modest expected impact unless instance set shifts to binary-heavy formulas. Implementation is small but care needed for DRAT proof correctness.
notes:
Claimed via /nextbeads. Work order position 1 of 1. Worktree /tmp/sat-worktrees/bluelake-b16, branch agent/bluelake/jumpreasons, base origin/main a48f9f5. Selected after my prior LH-1 attempt failed: choosing well-scoped, off-by-default phase1 work with no overlap to s11-06's shrink area (still owns 8ch).
**Released by /nextbeads (BlueLake, 2026-05-27 23:05 UTC).** Did not implement.

After reading the actual Kissat reference at `benchmarks/reference-solvers/kissat-latest/src/assign.c:32-45` (kissat_assign_binary), confirmed that Kissat's reason model is *literal-based*: `a->reason` is a unsigned-literal pointer, and jumpreasons replaces `other` (the propagator literal) with `a->reason` (the literal that propagated `other`). The implication graph chains through literals.

Solver 11's reason model is *clause-based*: `ReasonRef::Binary(BinaryClauseId)` stores the binary clause id, and conflict analysis recovers the parent literal by walking the clause body. The reason-invariant in this representation is: 'the reason clause must contain the implied literal.'

Naïvely transposing Kissat's fix (replace `lit`'s reason with `other`'s reason) breaks the invariant — `other`'s reason is a different binary clause that does not contain `lit`. Conflict analysis would extract the wrong parent and produce an incorrect learned clause.

Doing this 'properly' requires one of:
1. Add a new `ReasonRef::ParentLit(i32)` variant that stores the parent literal directly (Kissat-style), and teach conflict analysis to handle it. Significant structural change to the reason representation.
2. Implement jumpreasons only as a conflict-analysis short-circuit: when walking back from a binary-reason literal whose parent is also binary-propagated, skip the parent in the marking loop. But this changes the learned-clause shape (parent literal is at the current decision level so should be counted in 1UIP detection) — risks producing a non-asserting clause.

Both options are beyond a P4 well-scoped change. The bead's 'Fix sketch' ('inspect ReasonRef::Binary for the other literal in the binary clause') assumed the change was a small pointer adjustment; with the actual reason-representation mismatch it is not.

Recommendation: leave b16 open. Either upgrade scope to 'add ReasonRef::ParentLit variant + jumpreasons handling' (medium-effort, low-priority structural cleanup) or close as 'won't fix without representation change' depending on whether the binary-heavy formulas hypothesized by the third-pass investigation are actually in the target benchmark set.

Worktree `/tmp/sat-worktrees/bluelake-b16` is empty (no code changes); will be torn down.

In the port this is a two-line change in the binary-fast enqueue path (main.rs:4296-4303); level bookkeeping unchanged since the port levels everything at current level. No data-structure work needed. FINDINGS.md R19/H20.

title: Align minimization depth limit with kissat (1M -> 1k)
description:
Task class: parameter alignment. Tightens solver 11's recursive minimization depth limit to match kissat's reference.

Background: Solver 11 (solver/11-kissat-port/src/config.rs:14):
  const DEFAULT_MINIMIZE_DEPTH_LIMIT: u32 = 1_000_000;

Kissat (benchmarks/reference-solvers/kissat-latest/src/options.h:82):
  OPTION (minimizedepth, 1e3, 1, 1e6, 'minimization depth')

Solver 11's default depth limit is 1000x larger. In recursive clause minimization (lit_redundant in src/main.rs:1450+), this means solver 11 can descend through up to 1 million levels of reason chains before giving up. Kissat caps at 1000.

In practice, depths rarely exceed several hundred on typical instances. But on pathological learned clauses with deep reason chains (e.g. instances with chained binary clauses), solver 11 can spend significant time on a single minimize call that kissat would bound.

title: Implement focused-mode phase cycling diversification (every 8 mode switches)
description:
Task class: search diversification. Implements kissat's periodic phase polarity flip in focused mode.

Background: Kissat's kissat_decide_phase (benchmarks/reference-solvers/kissat-latest/src/decide.c:178-187):
  if (!solver->stable) {
    switch ((solver->statistics.switched >> 1) & 7) {
      case 1: res = INITIAL_PHASE; break;
      case 3: res = -INITIAL_PHASE; break;
    }
  }

Every 8 mode switches in focused mode, kissat alternates between using the default initial phase (false) and its inverse (true) for ALL phase decisions. This is forced diversification to escape locked-in phase patterns.
